  • Strong service orientation and ability to effectively work as a member or leader of a team by cooperating with others, offering to help others when needed, and considering larger organizational goals rather than individual concerns. Includes the ability to build &/or support a constructive team spirit where members are committed to the goals and objectives of the organization.
  • Plan, organize, and successfully multitask to meet multiple deadlines and frequently new work tasks within required timeframes. Proven flexibility to successfully work on a variety of projects quickly and accurately.
  • Effectively manage change and adapt.

  • Ability to work various hours, including nights, early mornings, and weekends

Job.JobTitle: Dean, Humanities, Social Sciences & Visual Arts
Job.CustomJobTypeName: Science, Biotech & Research, Social Service / Non Profit
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Pay: $85,000 to $100,000 a year
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Leesburg, FL

About this job

Academic dean reporting to the Associate Vice President for Academic Affairs, responsible for leading faculty and staff in Humanities, Social Sciences, and Visual Arts disciplines. Oversees budget management, class scheduling, student learning outcomes assessment, and collaboration with secondary schools and community partners.

Good fit if you have a master's degree in humanities, social sciences, or visual arts, five years in a college setting with four years teaching experience, and one year of supervisory experience.

Full job description

Job Summary

Reporting to the Associate Vice President for Academic Affairs (AVPAA), the academic dean is responsible for leading faculty, sustaining a student-centered academic culture that promotes collaboration, innovation, excellence, and integrity in teaching, and maintaining a collegial, respectful, and high-performing work environment for all employees.
 
 This position works in concert with AVPAA to recommend faculty appointments, professional development, academic student support (e.g., the library and learning centers), and evaluation in accordance with college policies and procedures. 
 The academic dean provides leadership to personnel and management of procedures and processes in 

assigned areas; will coordinate activities and work to resolve faculty and student issues, and will collaborate with personnel from across the college and community in support of the College's mission.


 The Dean of Humanities, Social Sciences, and Visual Arts provides administrative oversight to the designated discipline areas, and any directly related support services/programs.

Responsible for promoting and sustaining a collegial, respectful, and high-performing work environment and demonstrating LSSC’s values of caring, communicating, collaborating, and celebrating.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

include, but are not limited to the following:   

  •  Supervise full-time employees and adjunct faculty or other part-time staff within the discipline areas of oversight. Ensure fiscal responsibility in the development and management of the schedule of classes and resource management in assigned budgets; monitor spending and approve expenditures according to established policies and procedures.
  • Collaborate with secondary school partners to coordinate course offerings and other partnership initiatives.
  • Collaborate with College partners in support of initiatives such as articulation agreements.
  • Direct and manage course schedules and teaching assignments following the College’s policies and procedures.
  • Support faculty excellence in instruction to ensure student success.
  • Collaborate with instructional leaders throughout the College on initiatives and operations.
  • Track and analyze student performance, enrollment, and learning outcomes to make informed decisions regarding the status of academic programs and resource management (e.g., personnel and classroom resources)

The Service Technician at Nextran Truck Centers is a skilled position that is responsible for repairing and maintaining our customers’ Medium & Heavy-Duty Trucks. This includes preventative maintenance, repairs, disassembly, and reassembly, and writing detailed work notes.

Essential Duties:

Performs work as outlined on the repair order with efficiency and accuracy, in accordance with dealership and factory standards.
  • Diagnose the cause of the malfunctions and perform repairs.
  • Communicates with the parts department to obtain needed parts.
  • Saves and tags parts of the job if under warranty or if requested by the customer.
  • Documents all work performed and recommended on the repair order.
  • Reports machinery defects or malfunctions to the supervisor.
  • Ensures that the vehicle is kept clean. Notifies the service advisor/dispatcher immediately of anything that has happened to change the appearance or condition of the vehicle.
  • Maintains and is accountable for all dealership-owned tools and manuals. Returns all tools and manuals to the proper place and in the same condition as when they were received.
  • Understands, keeps abreast of, and complies with federal, state, and local regulations, such as hazardous waste disposal, OSHA Right-to-Know, etc. Keeps abreast of manufacturer technical bulletins.
  • Operates all tools/equipment in a safe manner and reports any safety issues immediately to management.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Skills and Qualifications:

  • Three-plus years of diesel mechanic experience.
  • ASE or Cummins Engine Repair Certificate is a plus.
  • English proficiency is essential for understanding safety protocols, customer interactions, and internal communications.
  • Basic computer skills
  • Valid CDL License a plus, recommended within 1 year of hiring.

Mathematical Skills:

Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide in all units of measure, using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals. Ability to compute rate, ratio, percentage, draw and interpret bar graphs.

Reasoning Ability:

Ability to solve problems and deal with a variety of variables in situations with only limited resources.Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram, or schedule form.

Physical Demands:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to perform the essential functions of this job successfully. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is:

  • Regularly required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel and reach with hands and arms.
  • Use of torque wrenches, air powered tools or hand tools.
  • Use of arms in a raised position above shoulder level for prolong periods of time. Use of creeper or rolling device to enable tech to work underneath vehicle.
  • The employee frequently is required to walk; climb or balance; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl; and talk or hear.
  • The employee is required to stand and sit for extended periods of time (hours) while making repairs.
  • Entry or exit from the cab of the vehicle.
  • Climb to a safe position to access the engine compartment area, firewall or roof of a vehicle to perform repairs.
  • The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to 50 pounds, frequently lift and/or move up to 100 pounds, and occasionally lift and/or move more than 100 pounds.
  • Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.
  • Ability to push/pull large tool chest from vehicle to vehicle.

Work Environment:

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly exposed to moving mechanical parts. The employee is frequently exposed to vibration. The noise level in the work environment is usually loud.

Summary

The Service Technician at Nextran Truck Centers is a skilled position that is responsible for repairing and maintaining our customer’s Medium & Heavy-Duty Trucks. This includes preventative maintenance, repairs, disassembly and reassembly, and writing detailed work notes.

Essential Duties

  • Performs work as outlined on repair order with efficiency and accuracy, in accordance with dealership and factory standards.

  • Communicates with the parts department to obtain needed parts.

  • Saves and tags parts of the job if under warranty or if requested by the customer.

  • Documents all work performed and recommended on the repair order.

  • Reports machinery defects or malfunctions to the supervisor.

  • Ensures that the vehicle is kept clean. Notifies service advisor/dispatcher immediately of anything that has happened to change the appearance or condition of the vehicle.

  • Maintains and is accountable for all dealership-owned tools and manuals. Return them to the proper place and in the same condition as when they were received.

  • Understands, keeps abreast of, and complies with federal, state, and local regulations, such as hazardous waste disposal, OSHA Right-to-Know, etc. Keeps abreast of manufacturer technical bulletins.

  • Operates all tools/equipment in a safe manner and reports any safety issues immediately to management.

Skills and Qualifications

  • High School Diploma

  • Basic computer skills

  • Up to Two years related experience and/or training as a Technician.

  • Valid CDL License a plus, recommended within 1 year of hiring.

Mathematical Skills

Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide in all units of measure, using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals. Ability to compute rate, ratio, and percent and to draw and interpret bar graphs.

Reasoning Ability

Ability to solve problems and deal with a variety of variables in situations with only limited resources. Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram, or schedule form.

Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is

  • Regularly required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel and reach with hands and arms.

  • Use of torque wrenches, air powered tools or hand tools.

  • Use of arms in a raised position above shoulder level for prolong periods of time. Use of creeper or rolling device to enable tech to work underneath vehicle.

  • The employee frequently is required to walk; climb or balance; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl; and talk or hear.

  • The employee is required to stand and sit for extended periods of time (hours) while making repairs.

  • Entry or exit from the cab of the vehicle.

  • Climb to a safe position to access the engine compartment area, firewall or roof of a vehicle to perform repairs.

  • The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to 50 pounds, frequently lift and/or move up to 100 pounds, and occasionally lift and/or move more than 100 pounds.

  • Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

  • Ability to push/pull large tool chest from vehicle to vehicle.

Work Environment

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly exposed to moving mechanical parts. The employee is frequently exposed to vibration. The noise level in the work environment is usually loud.

Essential duties and related qualifications may be changed as needed to meet the changing demands of the organization. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Job.CustomJobTypeName: Accounts Payable / Receivable, Accounting / Finance / Banking
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: 5401 Energy Air Court, Orlando, FL
  • Education: High school diploma or GED
  • Workplace: Drug-free workplace

About this job

Process vendor invoices and subcontractor pay applications for an energy company in Orlando. Track invoices, purchase orders, and maintain subcontractor insurance certificates while ensuring accuracy and timeliness of accounts payable records.

Good fit if you have two to five years of accounts payable experience, know lien law and AIA Schedule of Values, and have a high school diploma with accounting coursework.

Full job description

Job Title: Accounts Payable Specialist

Classification: Hourly/Non-Exempt

Reports to: Controller

Department: Accounting

Introduction:

  • The role of the Accounts Payable Specialist is to collect, report, and process all Vendor invoices and pay applications from subcontractors. He/she is to assure accountability, accuracy, and confidentiality of any and all payables related information and to track pay applications, invoices, purchase order receivers and unvouchered liabilities.

Functional Role:

  • The basic function of this position is to manage the smooth flow of Accounts Payable information of the company. To track all invoices and pay applications received and match all purchase order receivers to the appropriate invoices. They are also responsible for coordinating the approval of all subcontractors pay applications with the appropriate Project Manager and to ensure pay applications are posted to accounts payable in the accounting period that they apply to.

Responsibilities:

  • Responsible for maintaining Insurance certificates for subcontractors ensuring all insurance requirements are at the minimum amounts required by the subcontract and are current with respect to policy expiration dates.
  • Responsible for accurate accounting records of the Company’s Accounts Payable and Vendor records.
  • Maintain the close security of company Accounts Payable and Vendor records.
  • Maintain the confidentiality of company Accounts Payable and Vendor records.
  • Keep management apprised of the collection status of past due accounts and lien position within the time requirements that protect all lien rights.
  • Ensure the Accounts Payable documents are processed in a timely and error-free manner.

Requirements:

  • Education: High School diploma with courses in accounting.
  • Experience: Two to five year’s experience in Accounts Payable and AIA Schedule of Values.
  • MUST have lien law knowledge and experience.
  • Skills, knowledge, and abilities - Ability to work independently and to work well with others in a multi-functional fast paced environment. Good comprehension of Accounts Payables, Subcontractor and spreadsheet software, excellent reading, writing and verbal skills. Must understand AIA Schedule Of Values.
  • Reasoning Ability – Ability to apply principles of logical thinking to a wide range of intellectual and practical problems, ability to deal with a variety of abstract and concrete variables, ability to manage a variety of activities simultaneously.
  • Language Skills – Ability to communicate and give answers in a clear and precise style, ability to compose standard letters with proper format, grammar, punctuation, and spelling, using all parts of speech, ability to speak with poise, voice control, and confidence, using correct English with a well modulated voice.
  • Physical – While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to talk on the phone and use a computer.
  • Work Environment - The work is normally performed in a standard office environment with usually quiet to moderate noise levels.

DFWP/EOE

About this job

Provides executive administrative support to the Director of Human Resources and departmental functions including recruitment, benefits, and records. The role handles confidential personnel information while working in a busy, public-facing environment with frequent interruptions.

Good fit if you have four years of progressive administrative experience, including at least two years supporting an executive or senior manager.

Full job description

Nature of Work

The purpose of this class is to provide high-level, direct executive administrative support to the Director of Human Resources and skilled administrative and technical support to the Human Resources Department. The position independently coordinates and follows through on the Director’s administrative assignments, schedules, correspondence, reports, and other priorities; exercises discretion and sound judgment; and anticipates routine administrative needs. The position also supports departmental functions including recruitment, benefits, training, customer service, records, billing, budget activities, boards, and special projects. The work is performed in a busy, public-facing environment with frequent interruptions and changing priorities.

Essential Job Functions

  • Provides detailed, complex administrative support directly to the Director of Human Resources; independently organizes assignments, monitors deadlines, follows through on outstanding matters, and exercises discretion and sound judgment.
  • Handles sensitive and confidential information, which includes City personnel issues, benefits, employee personnel and medical files, discipline, and performance evaluations.
  • Greets customers, clients, or general public; provides or gathers information; provides services or refers to appropriate person or activity.
  • Answers phones and routes calls, answers questions, and takes messages.
  • Assist the HR Analysts with job postings, applicant tracking and employee recruitment and selection processes.
  • Processes public records requests in collaboration with HR Coordinator.
  • Responds to routine City policy questions.
  • Provides backup administrative support to the City Manager’s office.
  • Maintains office files in accordance with state records retention schedules.
  • Coordinates and maintains service award program.
  • Oversees or prepares forms, letters, booklets, brochures, reports, purchase orders, board meeting agendas, and other forms or records and correspondence as required.
  • Gathers information for entry into computer system; extracts information or reports as necessary.
  • Processes all department billing information and payment requests; audits and monitors billing accounts; resolves problems with billing; and assists with the preparation and input of budget information.
  • Oversees office functions such as dept payroll, personnel records, financial and business processes, inventories, budgets, training, contracts, public information, special projects or events, and others as assigned.
  • Acts as backup to HR Coordinator and assist as needed.
  • Maintains schedules and calendars for the Director and staff; coordinates meetings and follow-up items; makes travel arrangements; schedules and/or attends training seminars or classes; plans and coordinates social events such as receptions and luncheons.
  • Attends board and committee meetings; prepares minutes as needed.
  • Oversees or processes incoming and outgoing mail and routing to appropriate person or office.
  • Maintains supply inventories; orders supplies as needed; prepares purchase orders; pays invoices; operates and performs minor maintenance on office equipment.
  • May supervise staff including training, assigning and evaluating work.
  • Performs other duties as may be assigned by the department director and other department staff.

 

Minimum Requirements

  • Requires a high school diploma or GED, with some college or technical school coursework, and four (4) years of progressively responsible administrative or office experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience that provides the required knowledge, skills, and abilities. In addition, applicants must possess at least two (2) years of substantive, ongoing experience providing direct administrative support to an executive, department director, or senior-level manager. This specific two-year requirement is mandatory, may be included within the four years of administrative experience, and may not be substituted with education or other administrative experience. Demonstrated proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, and other office applications. Ability to work in a fast-paced, public-facing environment with frequent interruptions while exercising independent judgment, initiative, discretion, attention to detail, and strong organizational and follow-through skills. Experience in local government administration and with a multi-departmental finance and accounting system is preferred. May occasionally require work outside regular business hours.

  • Must possess a valid Florida driver’s license and satisfactory driving record as a condition of initial and continued employment.

  • Notary Public (preferred) or ability to acquire upon employment.

  • Special skills or equipment certification may be required.

Quick facts

  • Pay: $18.62 an hour
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Leesburg, FL
  • Experience: Entry level

About this job

Perform routine manual stormwater maintenance and installation work including trenching, ditch cleaning, and fixture installation. The City provides training for required certifications, and the role includes vehicle operation, landscape work, and emergency response.

Good fit if you have a high school diploma or GED, valid Florida driver license, and can live within 20 miles of Leesburg for on-call duties.

Full job description

Nature of Work

The purpose of the class is to perform routine manual work in the Stormwater division. This class is responsible for service work such as digging trenches, cleaning ditches; assists with installation of fixtures such as pipes, valves, fittings, and manholes; landscape, road, sidewalk, driveway restoration and other outdoor work. Completes logs or routine records. The class works according to set procedures under direct supervision. Weekend, holiday and after hours work may be required, as well as after-hours response and emergencies.

Essential Job Functions

  • Operates vehicles such as trucks to haul people or material to job sites.
  • Loads and unloads materials such as gravel, dirt, timber, chemicals, or other materials, tools, and equipment.
  • Performs maintenance duties as assigned; assists with setting up forms and pouring concrete, serves as traffic flagger on street or utility projects.
  • Maintains outdoor areas by cutting grass, pruning trees and bushes, raking leaves and debris, and other maintenance tasks.
  • Performs utility service work such as digging trenches, cleaning ditches; assists with installation of fixtures such as pipes, manholes, and sewer lines.
  • Performs maintenance functions such as greasing and maintaining equipment, and replacing valves; performs light repairs and installations as directed.
  • Maintains indoor areas such as shop, facilities and office areas, performing light maintenance such as painting and minor repairs.
  • This position is subject to assigned on call rotation.

Minimum Requirements

Requires a High School Diploma or GED

Must obtain the following certifications within 18 months of hire (City will provide training):

  • TTC approved certification

  • Confined Space Entry Certification

  • Class C Stormwater Certification

Requires a valid State of Florida driver license and satisfactory driving record as a condition of initial and continued employment. Must obtain a Class B CDL permit within 6 months of hire and Class B CDL within one year of employment. 

Must be available for call to duty at any time pertaining to system emergencies. Exceptions may be made on a case by case basis.

This position requires employees to reside within a 20-mile radius of the City limits of Leesburg within six (6) months of employment for continued employment due to on call rotation requirement.

Quick facts

  • Pay: $20.13 an hour
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Leesburg, FL
  • Education: High school diploma or GED

About this job

Entry-level operator of solid waste collection equipment including front-loaders and rear-loaders on designated routes. Involves manual labor, heavy lifting, equipment maintenance, and customer communication in Leesburg.

Good fit if you have one year of experience operating medium-sized trucks or equipment and hold a valid Florida Class B CDL with airbrake endorsement

Full job description

Nature of Work

This is the entry-level class in the Solid Waste Equipment Operator classifications. This class works under general supervision, performs routine tasks, semi-skilled and/or skilled tasks in the operation of front-loaders, roll-offs, side-loaders, rear-loaders, or similar equipment, and performs heavy manual labor for collecting, transporting, and disposing of solid waste materials from residential and commercial sources. Manual work and heavy lifting is also performed.

Essential Job Functions

  • Operates solid waste collection equipment to follow designated collection route.
  • Communicates with supervisors to inform them of progress made on work assignments.
  • Learn job-related procedures and techniques, primarily through verbal instruction, observation, and on-the-job training;
  • Respond to customer and public inquiries in a courteous manner and perform duties such as assessing concerns or complaints, problem solving and response efforts, and follow-up when appropriate.  
  • Collects solid waste such as refuse, recyclable materials, yard waste, and other materials.
  • Uses a two-way radio to communicate with supervisor and to receive instructions.
  • Transports solid waste materials to appropriately designated location for disposal or processing.
  • Monitors operation of equipment, provides minor maintenance or service and reports conditions in the field to the supervisor in a timely manner and request repairs or abatement of problems or issues in the field; 
  • Performs inspections of vehicles; performs basic maintenance activities, and keeps the interior and exterior of assigned equipment clean.  
  • Report unsafe working conditions, accidents and injuries to supervisor.
  • Inform supervisor of problems, emergency situations, unsafe or broken sanitation containers and unsafe, difficult, or poorly maintained collection sites.
  • Ability to work cooperatively with co-workers and the general public, using good judgment to resolve customer complaints in a positive and timely manner, using tact and courtesy.
  • Complete paperwork, forms, and reports related to collection services.
  • Attends meetings to exchange information; attends in-service training to gain or improve skills. 
  • Provide support as needed during special events and activities involving the delivery, setup, and removal of sanitation containers from field locations; assist in maintaining refuse containers in clean, working condition; perform other special event/activity tasks as needed;
  • Perform related duties as assigned and follows applicable standards and department-specific safety policies and practices.

Minimum Requirements

Requires a High school diploma or general equivalency diploma (GED).

Requires one year of experience in the operation of medium-sized trucks or equipment such as garbage trucks required; or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience, which provides the necessary knowledge, skills and abilities for this job.

Requires knowledge of traffic laws, ordinances, and rules for operating a class B commercial vehicle; including experience reading and understanding route maps and street signs.

Requires an orientation of up to three weeks. Duties are performed under training and close supervision until proficiency is demonstrated.

Weekend, holiday and afterhours work may be required, as well as after-hours response and emergencies.

Requires the ability to work under a minimum degree of stress related to duties that require constant attention to detail and tight deadlines. 

Requires the ability to follow specific oral and written instructions

Requires a valid State of Florida Class B Commercial Driver’s License (CDL) with airbrake endorsement and satisfactory driving record as a condition of initial and continued employment.

Special skills or equipment certification may be required.

Nature of Work

The Firefighter is responsible for all firefighting-related and EMS duties and operations as assigned. Involves contact with a wide variety of personalities both inside and outside the City limits. Requires a high degree of independent decision making in emergency situations; involves complex emergency and maintenance duties that may have direct impact upon the operations of the Fire Department; incumbent is exposed to all manner of environmental conditions including inclement weather, extreme temperatures, dust, noise, dim lighting, and all other conditions as present in the performance of essential function. Incumbent may also experience such hazards as fumes, flames, chemicals, blood, other body fluids, and all other hazards as required in performance of essential functions; requires the operation of various equipment, machinery, apparatus, and rescue vehicles as needed. May require working long hours and for extended periods of time between meals and breaks in some emergency situations.

Essential Job Functions

  • Basic knowledge of fire science including fire behavior, fire chemistry, firefighting and emergency rescue techniques and practice; operation and maintenance of firefighting and emergency medical equipment, tools, and apparatus.
  • Basic knowledge of building construction, writing practices, fire code, mathematics, and hydraulics.
  • Operates complex machinery or equipment that requires extended training and experience such as trucks using hydraulic pumping equipment, rescue vehicles, firefighting apparatus, protective equipment, electronic telecommunications equipment, or medical equipment.
  • Identifies persons requiring immediate care, provides life-saving procedures for emergency care.
  • Paramedic Incentive (Only): In accordance with Article 6 of the CBA – Identifies persons requiring immediate care, provides life-saving Advance Life Support procedures for emergency care in accordance with the Medical Director’s protocols.
  • Paramedic Incentive (Only): In accordance with Article 6 of the CBA – Medical clearance to work as a Paramedic from the Lake County Medical Director. 
  • Field Training Officer: Demonstrates utilization of advanced fire ground or EMS equipment and procedures, develop instructional programs, and instructional methodology. 
  • Attends instruction sessions in firefighting methods, equipment operation, rescue procedures, hazardous materials mitigation, and related subjects.
  • Gathers, organizes, analyzes, examines, or evaluates data or information and may prescribe action based on such data or information.
  • Gives information, guidance, or assistance to people to directly facilitate task accomplishment; may give instructions or assignments to helpers or assistants.
  • Guides others, making frequent decisions, affecting the individual, coworkers, and others that depend on the service or product.
  • Must learn all streets and hydrant block numbers within 18 months of employment, and from that point maintain a good working knowledge of streets, hydrants, and block numbers.
  • Skill in effectively communicating with people of diverse cultural and educational backgrounds.
  • Make decisions quickly and independently. Recognizes potential problems, helps to resolve problems, or refers problems to supervisor, as needed.
  • React effectively and make quick decisions under pressure, stressful conditions, or in emergency situations according to standard operating procedures/guidelines.
  • Follow state and local laws, departmental rules and regulations, and NFPA standards in responding to fires and emergency calls, and in driving and operating fire vehicle, apparatus, and equipment.
  • Completes required departmental forms, records and reports regarding maintenance, inspections and inventory.
  • Perform such tasks as cleaning and maintaining, quarters, tools, equipment, and apparatus.
  • Quickly and safely respond to fires and emergency calls with a company using appropriate procedures, techniques, methods, apparatus, tools, and equipment; attend to sick and injured persons; and perform all aspects of fire grounds operations according to standards.
  • Work in very difficult work environment including conditions of high heat, low visibility, confine space, on elevated ladder or apparatus, at accident scenes, under pressure or stressful conditions, and under adverse weather condition wearing full personal protective equipment.
  • Inspect buildings and identify fire hazards; perform company fire safety inspections and make recommendation for corrections or referrals.
  • Use current and modern job-related office and field equipment, including computer hardware and software applications used to produce reports, documents, and work-related research; and proficiently operate a two-way radio.
  • Recognize potential problems, help resolve problems, or refer problems to supervisor, as needed.
  • Follow state and local laws, departmental rules and regulations, and NFPA standards in responding to fires and emergency calls.
  • React effectively and make quick decisions under pressure or stressful conditions or in emergency situations according to standard operating procedures.
  • Identify and resolve routine equipment, operational, or technical problems and to refer or consult with appropriate staff and resources, as needed.
  • Read maps, know directions/locations and best routes to reach destinations.
  • Operate/use auxiliary equipment (area maps, mobile data terminal, MDT).
  • Perform routine test, inspection, and servicing of a variety of tools, specialized equipment, and apparatus.
  • Perform firefighting duties, as assigned.
  • Work a 24-hour shift, maintain complete response readiness at all times, and perform additional duties as assigned. Supports the safety of one another in a company or team.
  • Use current and modern job-related office and field equipment, including computer hardware and software applications used to produce reports, documents, and work-related research; and proficiently operate a two-way radio.
  • Pass an annual respirator certification as required by the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA).
  • Completion of Driver Working-Out-Of-Class program “WOC” at the completion of employee’s second year of employment
  • Ability to pass an annual physical in accordance to NFPA 1582.
  • Ability to do the essential job tasks in accordance with NFPA 1582.
  • Ability to complete an annual fitness program in accordance with NFPA 1583.

Minimum Requirements

Requires a high school diploma or GED; general knowledge of elementary physics, chemistry and mechanics; basic algebra involving variables and formulas, basic geometry involving circumferences, areas, and volumes, and computes ratios, rates, and percent. Performs skilled work involving rules/systems but solves problems almost constantly reading technical instructions, procedures manuals, and charts to solve practical problems; composes routine and specialized reports, forms, and letters; speaks compound sentences using normal grammar and word form. Performs specialized technical work requiring general understanding of operating policies and procedures and their application to problems not previously encountered; applies specialized technical principles and practices in the solution of problems; requires normal attention with short periods of concentration for accurate results and occasional exposure to unusual pressure. As of October 1, 2020, no employee shall engage in secondary employment that is in direct contradiction of F.S.S. 112.1816.

Candidates who are currently enrolled in a certified Fire Academy program will be considered. Successful completion of the program and attainment of the required State of Florida Firefighter Certificate of Compliance will be required upon hire and as a condition of continued employment.

Must have and maintain a current /valid State of Florida driver’s license and satisfactory driving record as a condition of initial and continued employment.

Special protective services skills and/or equipment certifications are required.

LICENSE/CERTIFICATES: 

Special Certifications and Licenses refer to state, federal, or professional certifications or licenses required entering or maintaining the job.

  • State of Florida Certificate of Firefighter Compliance I&II
  • Valid State of Florida Emergency Medical Technician Certification (EMT); or
  • Valid State of Florida Paramedic Certification (approved by Medical Director)
  • Valid CPR certification and/or ACLS (Paramedic Incentive)
  •  Valid State of Florida driver license
  •  NIMS 100, 200, 700, 800
  •  Wildland Firefighting S-130, S-190, L-180

Nature of Work

The purpose of the class is to read and record utility meter readings. Under general supervision, performs outdoor work involving the reading and recording of city utility meters. Duties include excessive walking, bending and driving in inclement weather conditions. Although the employee works independently and is often physically removed from supervision, duties are performed within the framework of pre-established policies and procedures.

Essential Job Functions

  • Follows prescribed routes to read and record utility meter information; 
  • Visually inspects meters and generates work order if meters needing repair or replacement;
  • Reports any irregularities noted on route;
  • Maintains and clears meter boxes of bugs, dirt and vegetation, as needed;
  • Enter meter information into hand held devices.
  • Maintains and stocks city vehicle.
  • Inspects vehicles, performs service or minor maintenance and reports malfunctions.
  • Re-read meters to verify readings;
  • Performs routine office tasks, such as typing, filing, faxing, phoning, and copying.
  • This position is subject to stand-by status. 
  • Maintains traffic control and ensures vehicle and pedestrian safety procedures are observed.
  • Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with employees and the public as necessitated by the work.

Minimum Requirements

  • Requires a high school diploma or GED. 

  • Requires a minimum of two (2) years of experience working outside performing general physical labor.

  • A general knowledge of computers is required including Microsoft Office.

  • Must be able to work with little supervision and there is considerable discretion to act independently.

  • Requires general knowledge of street locations throughout the City service area.

  • Weekend, holiday and afterhours work may be required, as well as after-hours response and emergencies.

  •  Requires a valid State of Florida driver license and satisfactory driving record as a condition of initial and continued employment.

  • Special skill or equipment certification may be required.

Quick facts

  • Pay: $23.56 to $34.82 an hour
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Leesburg, FL
  • License: Valid driver's license

About this job

Provides accounting functions for the City of Leesburg including reconciliation, payroll tracking, fixed asset management, and financial reporting. Works with accounts under general supervision and prepares audit documents.

Good fit if you have an associate degree in accounting or related field, one year of accounting experience, and a valid Florida driver's license.

Full job description

Nature of Work

The purpose of the class is to provide accounting functions in conformance with generally accepted accounting principles. The class is responsible for accounting, disbursement, maintenance, review, interpretation, analysis and reconciliation of accounts within assigned area of responsibility. The class works within a general outline of work to be performed, and develops work methods and sequences under general supervision.

Essential Job Functions

  • Performs accounting functions in accordance with Federal, State, and local laws, rules, and requirements for assigned accounts.
  • Reconciles all funds and accounts for assigned areas of responsibility; researches discrepancies, collects information, and reports findings.
  • Tracks payroll activity for all departments and related funds.
  • Tracks fixed assets for General and Capital funds; inventories fixed assets.
  • Posts payments, journal and general ledger entries as assigned.
  • Prepares required financial reports such as worker’s compensation, pension, 941, element object reconciliation etc.
  • Prepares audit documents, assists with or performs audits.
  • Performs data entry of all financial activities for assigned accounts and funds; verifies and reconciles accuracy of data entered.
  • Attends staff or project meetings to exchange information; attends in-service training and technical or professional classes, seminars, or conferences to improve technical or professional skills.
  • Performs routine office tasks, such as typing, filing, faxing, phoning, and copying.

Minimum Requirements

Requires an Associate of Science Degree (A.S.), Vocational Technical Degree, specialized training, or self-education equivalent to satisfactory completion of two years of college education with emphasis in accounting or a closely related field.

Requires one year of work experience in accounting.

Must possess a valid Florida driver’s license and satisfactory driving record as a condition of initial and continued employment.

The class works according to some procedures, but decides how and when to do things under general supervision.

Essential Job Functions

  • Operates mobile equipment to transport materials, tools, equipment, and personnel to job sites and to remove debris or other materials from job sites in support of plant operations, maintenance and/or repair of infrastructure.
  • Operates specialized mobile equipment to support City operations such as utilities construction and repair, concrete laying, and other specialized operations.
  • Monitors truck, tractors, tools and equipment and ensures for the proper operation of equipment used. Reports major malfunction to supervisor and services equipment to ensure proper operation.
  • Operates hand and power tools and equipment to support maintenance operations such as weed cutting, debris removal, grass cutting, digging or filling, portable pumps and other maintenance tasks.
  • Inspects equipment and performs minor maintenance; reports malfunctions to supervisor.
  • Troubleshoots and repairs the sprayfield infrastructure and associated facilities.
  •  Reads and interprets plans and drawings and uses this information to perform job tasks.
  • Performs minor administrative tasks such as completing job-related logs and forms, answering phones, or providing information.
  • Performs simple clerical tasks. Maintain hauling manifests.
  • Performs assigned duties as needed and requested.

Minimum Requirements

High School Diploma or GED.

Must be able to run various equipment with minimal instruction

Requires a valid State of Florida Driver’s License and satisfactory driving record as a condition of initial and continued employment.

Must obtain a Class A CDL permit within 3 months of hire. Must obtain a Class A CDL license with tanker endorsement within 6 months of hire.

Special skills or additional equipment certification may be required.

Nature of Work

Buyer - $24.50 - $36.21 per hour

The purpose of this position is to perform responsible specialized work in procurement of assigned types of commodities at competitive prices in connection with the Central Procurement Operation of the City. Employees in this classification do detailed work involved in purchasing assigned commodity groups, including review of requisitions. Work involves the ability to communicate with vendors and City personnel in order to discern needs and ability to furnish needed materials. The employee exercises considerable judgment and initiative in the performance of work tasks. Work is performed under the general supervision of the Procurement Manager and Senior Buyer in accordance with established policies and is reviewed through observation and analysis of reports. Works with supervisor to prepare specifications for bidding and quoting purposes. Prepares bid packets, and quote packets, and public advertisement of tabulations.

Senior Buyer – $26.50 - $39.17 per hour 

The purpose of this position is to perform highly specialized work in the purchase of a variety of complex commodities for the City.  Employees in this classification function at senior professional level to perform detailed work in the preparation, research, writing, evaluating and administration of solicitations and contracts. The position consists of technical and professional work in the procurement of goods and services in compliance with federal, state and local policies and procedures. The Senior Buyer may act on behalf of the Procurement Manager in their absence. This position ensures proper administration of the solicitations, specifications, scopes of work and resulting agreements or contracts, purchase orders issued by the City in support of departmental activity.  Leads and participates in work of other staff within the division.

Essential Job Functions

Buyer

COMMERCIAL CONSTRUCTION SUPERINTENDENT

Direct Hire Opportunity | South Florida

Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced Commercial Construction Superintendent to independently oversee daily field operations and lead commercial construction projects from mobilization through final project turnover.

The ideal candidate will have a strong background in commercial construction, excellent leadership and communication skills, and the ability to coordinate subcontractors, manage project schedules, maintain safety standards, and ensure quality workmanship.

Projects typically range from $1 million to $5 million and include healthcare, retail, industrial, medical, and commercial interior build-outs, renovations, and ground-up construction.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced construction professional looking for a long-term career with a competitive compensation and benefits package.

Key Responsibilities

  • Oversee daily jobsite operations, including subcontractor coordination, deliveries, site logistics, and inspections.
  • Maintain a clean, safe, and organized jobsite while enforcing all safety requirements.
  • Review construction drawings, specifications, and subcontractor scopes to identify potential issues.
  • Coordinate with Project Managers to maintain project schedules and resolve field-related challenges.
  • Develop short-term look-ahead schedules and ensure subcontractors have the necessary manpower and materials.
  • Monitor construction progress and ensure quality standards are met.
  • Maintain daily reports, progress photos, inspection records, and project documentation using Procore.
  • Communicate professionally with clients, architects, engineers, inspectors, vendors, and subcontractors.
  • Identify potential scope changes, unforeseen conditions, and schedule or cost impacts.
  • Monitor field expenses, equipment needs, and material requirements.
  • Oversee punch-list completion, final inspections, and project turnover.
  • Provide hands-on support when necessary while maintaining overall responsibility for field supervision.

Qualifications

  • Minimum of 5 years of commercial construction superintendent experience preferred.
  • Proven ability to independently manage commercial construction projects from start to finish.
  • Experience with commercial build-outs, renovations, and/or ground-up construction.
  • Experience managing projects valued between $1 million and $5 million is highly desirable.
  • Strong knowledge of construction drawings, specifications, scheduling, and construction methods.
  • Experience coordinating multiple subcontractors and construction trades.
  • Proficiency with Procore and Bluebeam preferred.
  • OSHA 30 certification preferred.
  • First Aid/CPR certification preferred.
  • Excellent leadership, organizational, and communication skills.
  • Valid driver's license and ability to travel to local project sites.
  • Ability to work outdoors and accommodate occasional project-related schedule adjustments, including nights or weekends.

Compensation & Benefits

  • $75,000 annual base salary
  • Performance-based bonus eligibility.
  • Company-paid employee-only health insurance premium.
  • $1,000 monthly company contribution toward offered family health coverage.
  • 401(k) with company match up to 4%, subject to plan terms.
  • Two weeks of starting paid time off.
  • Paid holidays.
  • Mileage reimbursement with a monthly minimum.
  • Company-provided phone and iPad.

  • Assignments outside the local area may be considered travel assignments and handled under applicable travel arrangements.
  • Occasional nights and weekends may be required depending on project needs.

About this job

Design and evolve deal enablement frameworks that translate Siemens' commercial strategy into clear guidance for global sales teams. The role bridges product, pricing, finance, and sales to ensure consistent, scalable execution across complex B2B software solutions and new business models.

Good fit if you have 8+ years in commercial operations, deal desk, or sales operations at a complex B2B enterprise software company, with experience designing global deal guidelines and IFRS 15 revenue recognition knowledge.

Full job description

Siemens Digital Industries Software is a leading provider of solutions for the design, simulation, and manufacture of products across many different industries. Formula 1 cars, skyscrapers, ships, space exploration vehicles, and many of the objects we see in our daily lives are being conceived and manufactured using our Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) software.

Position Overview:

Siemens is a global technology powerhouse focusing on the areas of intelligent infrastructure, automation, and digitalization. Within Global Sales Excellence (GSE) HQ, our mission is to empower our sales and commercial teams with world-class operational frameworks, deal enablement structures, and streamlined processes. We champion operational excellence, ensuring that complex commercial strategies translate into clear, scalable, and frictionless execution for our teams and customers.

We are currently seeking a Deal Enablement Architect for the commercial and operational frameworks that enable products, business models and cross-business opportunities to be sold consistently, efficiently and at scale. The GSE HQ Deal Enablement Architect owns the design and evolution of the business-facing elements of the Global Deal Enablement Operating Model.

The role connects Product, Strategy, Pricing, Finance, Sales and operational stakeholders to translate commercial strategy into clear and practical guidance for the field. Its purpose is to ensure that Deal Guidelines, new products, new business models and cross-business propositions are designed for execution, with clear parameters, watch-outs and escalation pathways. The role challenges complexity at source and ensures lessons from execution are continuously fed back into better guidance and commercial design.

Key Responsibilities:

1. Deal Guidelines Architecture

  • Own providing Finance Enablement and Governance perspectives into the global architecture and lifecycle of Deal Guidelines.
  • Define the framework, structure and governance for global Deal Guidelines.
  • Translate commercial, financial, contractual and operational requirements into simple, actionable seller guidance.
  • Drive continuous simplification and rationalization of guidelines.
  • Define mechanisms to measure adoption, effectiveness and usability.
  • Analyze recurring questions, exceptions and escalations to identify remediation opportunities.
  • Convert repeatable expert judgement into clear rules and guidance.
  • Ensure changes in strategy, products or business models are reflected in Deal Guidelines.
  • Drive the principle that standard business should not require expert interpretation

2. Product Introduction Alignment

  • Establish Deal Enablement readiness as an integral component of product introduction.
  • Work across Product Segments, Strategy, Pricing, Finance and Operations to define:
  • How the product should be sold
  • Standard commercial parameters
  • Pricing and packaging considerations
  • Contracting and quoting implications
  • Permitted and non-standard scenarios
  • Known watch-outs
  • Required guidance
  • Exception and escalation routes
  • Challenge upstream product or commercial design where unnecessary complexity will create downstream seller friction or manual intervention.

3. New Business Model Readiness

  • Own Deal Enablement readiness for new and evolving commercial models.
  • Assess the impact of new business models on deal execution.
  • Identify gaps across commercial policy, pricing, processes, contracting, finance and operations.
  • Develop practical guidelines for new commercial structures.
  • Define boundaries between standard, guided and exception business.
  • Support initial transactions and capture lessons from early adoption.
  • Convert early-stage learning into repeatable guidance.
  • Avoid temporary workarounds becoming permanent complexity.

4. Cross-Business Collaboration

  • Develop scalable Deal Enablement concepts for opportunities spanning multiple businesses, portfolios or organizational structures, for example OneTech / OpsSW-type collaboration.
  • Define clear execution principles for cross-business opportunities.
  • Clarify commercial interfaces, responsibilities and decision points.
  • Identify conflicting policies or operating assumptions.
  • Develop reusable cross-business frameworks rather than deal-specific workarounds.
  • Simplify how sellers navigate organizational boundaries.
  • Partner with relevant business organizations to identify common models that can be standardized.
  • Organizational complexity should not become seller or customer complexity.

Key Deliverables:

Global Deal Guideline framework

  • Deal Guideline lifecycle and governance
  • Guideline adoption and effectiveness framework
  • Guideline simplification/remediation backlog
  • Product Introduction Deal Readiness framework
  • New Business Model readiness framework
  • Cross-business Deal Enablement frameworks
  • Commercial parameter / watch-out frameworks
  • Standard vs exception decision principles

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, Operations, Engineering, or a related field (MBA or advanced degree preferred).
  • 8+ years of progressive experience in commercial operations, deal desk leadership, sales operations, pricing strategy, commercial/contract management, or product go-to-market within a complex B2B enterprise software or technology environment.
  • Proven track record of designing, scaling, and governing global deal guidelines, quoting frameworks, and commercial operating models.
  • Exceptional ability to bridge product, strategy, pricing, finance, legal, and sales stakeholders to translate complex corporate requirements into simple, actionable field guidance.
  • Direct experience driving operational readiness for complex technology offerings, including SaaS, subscriptions, usage-based models, and multi-product/cross-business bundled solutions.
  • Strong knowledge of IFRS 15 software revenue accounting and revenue recognition requirements for software, SaaS, and related service offerings.
  • Demonstrated methodology for identifying and eliminating upstream operational complexity, reducing manual exceptions, and ensuring standard business requires no expert interpretation.
  • Experience defining frameworks to measure guideline adoption, analyzing recurring escalation patterns, and using feedback loops to continuously improve commercial design.
  • Highly structured thinker capable of breaking down ambiguous commercial challenges into clear parameters, watch-outs, and escalation pathways.
  • Outstanding ability to influence senior cross-functional leaders and drive consensus across diverse organizational silos.
  • Experience navigating matrixed, multinational enterprise structures and coordinating cross-business initiatives across international boundaries.
  • Experience working with enterprise platforms and digital technologies, including Salesforce, SAP, and AI-powered bots/agents, with the ability to leverage these tools to improve business processes, data insights, and operational efficiency.

About this job

Solutions Account Executive for building automation controls at Siemens' Pensacola branch, serving the Gulf Coast region. You'll develop customer relationships, manage a sales pipeline, and spend at least 50% of time on customer-facing activities to achieve booking and profit goals.

Good fit if you have 4+ years of building automation sales experience, financial acumen, and a valid driver's license for in-person customer visits.

Full job description

Position Location: This role supports our Pensacola, FL branch location, which serves customers throughout the Gulf Coast and greater Pensacola, FL area.

Here at Siemens, we take pride in enabling sustainable progress through technology. We do this through empowering customers by combining the real and digital worlds. We are improving how we live, work, and move today and for the next generation! We know that the only way a business thrives is if our people are thriving. That’s why we always put our people first. Our global, diverse team would be happy to support you and challenge you to grow in new ways. Who knows where our shared journey will take you?

Our Smart Buildings help to create efficient, safe, adaptable, and responsible environments. Our aim isn’t just about improving buildings; it’s about creating perfect places that improve people’s lives.

Transform the everyday with us!


The Solutions Account Executive is committed to supporting our new construction business within our commercial Smart Buildings Automation Controls Solutions team. Our Solutions Sales team will achieve booking and profit goals by developing and implementing plans to grow, develop, and manage contractor, consultant, developer, and end-user relationships; capitalize on sales opportunities within the territory; and effectively execute sophisticated deals independently within our established guidelines. Our Sales Executives are ambassadors of quality Siemens technology, products and services, and your expertise and regular interaction with the customers will help them optimize and facilitate a safe, emergency-ready workplace.


As a Solutions Account Executive, you will:

  • Achieve new order/booking and profit goals based on your assigned quota.
  • Develop and maintain a qualified funnel of opportunities including forecasting expected order intake. Deliver on forecasted results consistently.
  • Develop a comprehensive understanding of the marketplace, competitor offerings, customers, and decision influencers across the region, segments, and verticals within the region. Keep current on automation market business and product trends.
  • Develop a vertical market and account management plan that focuses on strategic growth. Identify new business opportunities to grow in new markets or adjacent segments and develop “go to market” strategies to drive business to the end user customer and the standard construction channel.
  • Act as a consultant to multiple levels of the customer’s organization by understanding their challenges and recommending services to ensure their building systems perform as required to achieve business goals.
  • Attend industry-specific networking events; actively participate in professional organizations such as ASHRAE, AEE or USGBC to build a network of contacts and to represent Siemens in the market.
  • Consult with the customer and determine budgeting and investment requirements.
  • Position Siemens as an industry leader among service providers, leveraging Siemens world-class digital service delivery as a key differentiator.
  • Collaborate with operations and internal teams to deliver excellent customer outcomes.
  • Work with your internal sales support to enable you to spend more time with your customers.
  • Collaborate with sales estimators to prepare cost estimates and customer bid packages.
  • Partner with other sales business teams to plan, target, and acquire new projects and accounts.
  • Set pricing based on identified value of the services offered to the customer.
  • Work with operations, finance, legal and other inside and outside resources to obtain the sale.
  • Actively participate in sales department meetings, workshops, and seminars to stay knowledgeable on current market, business, and product trends.
  • Expected to spend minimum 50% of time in customer facing activities, performed in person and on customer site. 
  • Work with existing customers supporting their needs and act as a hunter to bring new customers to the business. 
  • Travel overnight ~10% for training and business development as required based on your assigned territory. 


You will make an impact with these qualifications:

Basic Qualifications: 

  • High School Diploma or state-recognized GED
  • 8+ years of Sales Experience in building automation or a related field (Senior Level) | 4+ years of Sales Experience in building automation or a related field (Mid-Level)
  • Must be able to demonstrate:
  • Financial expertise to estimate and sell technical solutions and service offerings effectively and independently 
  • Account development and strategic sales skills 
  • Organizational, presentation, and negotiation skills 
  • Verbal and written communication skills in English
  • Experience with Microsoft Office suite 
  • Must be 21 years of age and possess a valid driver's license with limited violations; must meet eligibility requirements to participate in Siemens' fleet vehicle program
  • Legally authorized to work in the United States on a continual and permanent basis without company sponsorship

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Business or Engineering
  • Salesforce CRM 
  • Software, IoT, and networking experience 
  • Experience in the life sciences, healthcare, education, data center, and commercial office vertical markets 
  • Experience selling to end users/owners and demonstrated understanding of how to market, position, and sell cloud-based, data-driven service programs such as fault detection and diagnostics to existing and new customers

Senior Field Service Engineers are responsible for the I&C on our power distribution equipment at our Hyper-Scale Data Center sites. Scope includes, but not limited to, setting communication devices and topology industrial networks, uploading HMI/ PLC programs, installation of I/O and CPUs, integration of 3rd Party EPMS, initial testing, operation, troubleshooting and modification of customer equipment and systems including MV/LV switchgear, transformers, metering, power monitoring, power quality, and protective relays.

As a Senior Field Service Engineer, you will: 

  • Create test scripts and MOP (Methods of Procedures) related to Data Centers Cx activities. 
  • Setting communication devices and topology industrial networks; uploading HMI/ PLC programs; installation of I/O and CPUs 
  • Integration of 3rd Party EPMS; initial testing, operation, troubleshooting and modification of customer equipment and systems
  • MV or LV Circuit breakers; metal clad/vacuum switchgear; breakers or LV equipment testing; analyzing test results
  • Equipment Condition Assessments 
  • Electrical Control Circuits Troubleshooting & Repair 
  • Provide on-site assistance with or perform programming, start-up, checkout, commissioning, and validation processes. Participate in job site final walk-through, complete all job closeout documentation, and provide customer training. Act as technical resource to customers and field employees  
  • Provide instructions to customer personnel regarding proper operation and routine inspections. Train customers to maintain and adjust complex equipment. Provide expert advice, training, and technical assistance to support staff and train lower-level employees. Complete and submit reports covering all job activity. Responsible for maintaining complex tools, test equipment, calibration items, etc.
  • Must be available to respond to emergency and relief assignments.
  • Plan and estimate labor categories, rates, material dollar costs, and transportation expenses to complete complex proposals. Perform review of complex task plans, drawings, and installation schematics; provide continual guidance throughout the project duration. (FSE only) 
  • Perform and supervise preliminary and detailed site audits to develop design concepts and schematics.
  • Perform Site Lead activities during the cycle of the client’s construction schedule, when required. 


You will make an impact with these qualifications: 

Basic Qualifications: 

  • 5+ years of experience troubleshooting and repairing electrical control circuits and ability to obtain thermography certification 
  • 5+ years of experience in the installation and/or maintenance of Power Automation Switchboards 
  • 5+ years of experience using electrical test sets to perform AC and DC high potential testing, transformer turns ratio testing, transformer power factor testing, and other power system test practices and procedures 
  • Must be able to demonstrate:
    • Skills at interpreting protective coordination studies and testing and configuring protective relays 
    • Capability to read bills of material, electrical blueprints, and power system study reports 
    • Experience with the installation, commissioning, and maintenance of low and medium voltage power distributions systems 
    • Familiarity with the arc flash and shock hazards of 13.8 kV and the following electrical equipment: Siemens GIS, AIS, WL, RL, and SB breakers and switchgear 
    • Familiarity with ANSI, NEC, NFPA, IEEE, and NETA codes and standards 
  • Must be able to carry and move equipment and tools weighing up to 75 pounds unassisted 
  • Demonstrated proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, and Outlook) 
  • Must be 18 years of age and possess a valid driver's license with limited violations ; must meet eligibility requirements to participate in Siemens' fleet vehicle program
  • Legally authorized to work in the United States on a continual and permanent basis without company sponsorship 

Preferred Qualifications: 

  • Bachelor’s Degree – preferably EE/ME
  • AVO, NETA, and NICET certifications

Job.JobTitle: Head of Planning, Forecasting & Incentive Management
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Remote

Full job description

Location: Any Siemens location in the world

Head of Planning, Forecasting & Incentive Management

Company Overview

We are a leading global software company dedicated to the world of computer aided design, 3D modeling and simulation— helping innovative global manufacturers design better products, faster! With the resources of a large company, and the energy of a software start-up, we have fun together while creating a world class software portfolio. Our culture encourages creativity, welcomes fresh thinking, and focuses on growth, so our people, our business, and our customers can achieve their full potential

Position Overview

Process & Data Domain sets clear common standards for internal-facing processes, data, and the application backbone – acting as the business interface to IT for how common sales applications and related data fit together across the company.

Within it, Global Sales Applications owns the main global sales tools – including Salesforce CRM, ICM / Anaplan, rebate management, and quoting applications – and works with IT DevOps and FS SEA to maintain, improve, roll out, and train users on these applications.

Key Responsibilities

• Shape the strategy and operating model for Planning, Forecasting & Incentive Management within FS PDD SA – defining how Siemens connects quota management, forecasting, incentive compensation and performance measurement into a coherent, scalable application framework across Sales Units.

• Build the PFI team as a credible centre of expertise within Global Sales Applications – establishing clear ways of working and productive interfaces with Sales Finance, HR, FS PDD PE (Process Engineering), FS PDD DAI (Data & AI Lab), IT DevOps, and SHERPA stakeholders.

• Lead and develop a diverse team – nurturing talent, fostering collaboration, and shaping a working culture that turns ambition into outcomes.

• Own the business architecture for the PFI application landscape – connecting Salesforce CRM, CPQ, ICM / Anaplan, incentive compensation, ERP and BI platforms into a unified framework that supports planning, forecasting, quota management and incentive administration.

• Define common business definitions, KPIs and measurement frameworks that ensure consistency across systems, data and reporting – establishing a single source of truth for sales performance across Siemens.

• Sponsor PFI-related transformation initiatives and technology roadmap topics, acting as the business owner for platform improvements delivered through IT DevOps in coordination with the SHERPA X programme.

• Ensure data integrity across the PFI application ecosystem, governing how planning, quota, forecasting and compensation data flow between systems and into executive reporting.

• Lead governance for performance metrics, compensation frameworks and seller scorecards – partnering with Sales, Finance, HR, Operations, IT and Analytics to drive alignment between business objectives and performance measures.

• Oversee executive dashboards and performance reporting, ensuring senior leadership has accurate, timely and actionable visibility of forecast, quota attainment, incentive outcomes and seller productivity.

• Drive analytics that improve seller productivity and business outcomes – evaluating the effectiveness of quota plans, compensation designs and sales programs, and translating findings into recommendations for leadership.

• Represent PFI in cross-FS and FS PDD SA governance discussions, surfacing application dependencies, data risks and platform decisions that require cross-functional alignment.

Qualifications

• Ten or more years of experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, Sales Strategy or Performance Management, with deep expertise in quota planning, territory management, forecasting, incentive compensation and sales performance measurement.

• Five or more years leading teams and cross-functional transformation programs at enterprise scale, with a track record of delivering business architecture and technology change across global organizations.

• Demonstrated experience designing end-to-end business processes and application ecosystems that span planning, forecasting, incentive compensation and performance reporting. Familiarity with technology company operating models is a benefit, not a requirement.

• Strong understanding of Salesforce CRM, CPQ, Anaplan, incentive management platforms, ERP and BI tools, and how they connect to form a coherent sales performance management system.

• Experience leading a team and developing talent with an inclusive leadership style, with a strong collaboration mindset across departments and organizational boundaries.
