About this job

The Office of the General Counsel at University of Central Florida seeks an Associate General Counsel to focus on labor and employment matters. The role involves advising university departments on employment issues, managing litigation and administrative proceedings, supporting collective bargaining, and tracking legal developments affecting higher education.

Good fit if you have 4+ years of attorney experience, Florida Bar membership or eligibility, and background in employment law, labor matters, or higher education legal counsel.

Full job description

Office of the General Counsel:

The Office of the General Counsel is the legal office of the University of Central Florida and is responsible for the coordination and management of all legal issues and matters affecting the University. We provide legal services to UCF across a range of issues, manage UCF’s legal affairs, and are responsible for protecting UCF’s legal interests. Our mission is to support the University as a public research institution and provide practical, timely, and strategic advice and legal services to unleash the potential within every individual.

The Office’s services cover a wide range of issues, including governance, corporate matters, regulatory compliance, employment law, intellectual property, foreign influence, student conduct, academic affairs, litigation, data privacy, real estate, construction, and much more.

 

The Opportunity:

The University of Central Florida's Office of the General Counsel is seeking an experienced attorney to join its legal team as Associate General Counsel, with a primary focus on labor and employment matters. This role offers the opportunity to serve as a trusted legal partner to university leaders and stakeholders, providing practical, strategic counsel on complex and often sensitive workplace matters. The Associate General Counsel will advise on employment and labor issues, support collective bargaining, manage employment-related litigation and administrative proceedings, and help the university navigate an evolving legal and regulatory environment.

The ideal candidate will bring sound legal judgment, strong communication skills, and a collaborative, solutions-oriented approach to legal practice. This is an opportunity for an attorney who enjoys working across a large, complex organization and translating legal requirements into thoughtful, actionable guidance.

 

Responsibilities:

Employment Law:

  • Provide day-to-day employment advice to University departments and DSO’s including but not limited to all central units and to all colleges. Provide legal guidance to Office of Nondiscrimination and Accommodations Compliance and/or Student Accessibility Services regarding civil rights laws covering discrimination, harassment, retaliation and accommodations. Train units on Human Resources related matters.

Litigation and Administrative Proceedings:

  • Represent the University in administrative proceedings, including but not limited to OCR, EEOC, and FCHR. Manage outside counsel assigned to litigation for the University and all direct support organizations and/or serve as counsel of record for the University in litigation not covered by State Risk management, as assigned. Provide pre-litigation support and advice to University departments including but not limited to Risk Management.

Labor:

  • Advise the bargaining teams for all campus unions, including attendance at bargaining sessions, pre-bargaining strategy sessions and status communications with university leadership. Advise on labor matters, represent university in labor proceedings, and provide day-to-day advice to university leadership on collective bargaining agreement interpretation.

Legal Developments:

  • Track state and federal legislative updates and case law development in area of subject matter specialties, including sharing updates with colleagues and drafting, reviewing, and revising University regulations and policies as needed.

Contracts:

  • Review university contracts and other commercial activities, including drafting labor and employment related instruments.

Garnishments:

  • Serve as counsel of record on garnishment matters involving University and DSO employees.
  • Other duties as assigned by the Vice President and General Counsel or designee.

Minimum Qualifications: 

Law degree and 4+ years of experience as an attorney. Must be a member of the Florida Bar or become a member within twelve months of employment

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience providing legal counsel within, or representing, a higher education, public-sector, government, or similarly complex organization.
  • Five or more years of progressively more responsible experience.
  • Knowledge of federal and state laws and regulatory requirements affecting higher education, with experience in Florida higher education preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience advising clients on labor and employment matters, including employee relations, discipline, termination, discrimination, harassment, retaliation, accommodations, and/or other workplace matters.
  • Experience handling employment-related litigation and administrative matters, including matters before agencies such as the EEOC, FCHR, OCR, or comparable federal or state agencies.
  • Demonstrated ability to provide practical, clear, and responsive legal counsel to leaders and stakeholders on complex or sensitive matters.
  • Strong legal research, analysis, writing, and communication skills, including experience drafting legal memoranda, responses, policies, agreements, and other legal documents.

 

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

  • This role requires the successful candidate to work on-site at UCF's Main Campus in Orlando, FL, as their primary work location. On-site presence is an essential function of this role.
  • All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.

University Operations:

University Operations at UCF is committed to creating a supportive and welcoming environment for our faculty, staff, students, and the broader community. Visit our website or follow us on Facebook and Instagram to learn more.

 

The Opportunity:

The Planning, Design and Construction Department within University Operations is seeking to hire a Construction Project Manager III. This position is responsible for the coordination and management of design and construction efforts to ensure the successful completion of both minor and major projects, in alignment with project schedules, budgets, and UCF's institutional strategy. The role involves planning, directing, and overseeing the design and construction of facilities, systems, and structures. The Construction Project Manager III leads the development of design and construction projects, manages their organization, scheduling, and implementation, and represents section leadership when needed.

Responsibilities:

Project Planning, Design & Compliance

  • Oversee all aspects of construction projects, including managing contractors, architects, engineers, and consultants, ensuring compliance with the Project Manager Manual.
  • Support sustainability goals and address design or implementation issues in collaboration with project teams.
  • Review project scopes and documents before bidding and permits.
  • Conduct inspections to ensure adherence to safety codes and regulations.
  • Ensure project documents meet UCF’s standards.

 

Budget, Contracts & Procurement

  • Develop and manage budgets and cost-tracking reports, identifying and resolving potential financial or quality issues.
  • Negotiate change orders and contract modifications with stakeholders.
  • Prepare estimates, bids, and Guaranteed Maximum Prices (GMP). Ensure timely payments for designers and contractors.
  • Develop purchasing strategies to address pre-construction challenges.

 

Project Execution & Stakeholder Management

  • Create and manage project schedules to meet deadlines.
  • Monitor contractor performance and track progress against the schedule.
  • Address delays and site emergencies as they arise.
  • Manage all phases of campus construction projects, collaborating with departments and facilities staff.
  • Maintain regular communication with stakeholders and involve them in decision-making.

 

Leadership & Departmental Support

  • Mentor and train junior project managers, improving departmental standards and efficiency.
  • Serve as signature authority in the absence of department managers.

 

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's or Master's degree and 4+ years of relevant experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6). 

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Six or more years of experience managing complex construction or renovation projects through the full project lifecycle, from planning and design through construction and close-out.
  • Experience managing multiple projects simultaneously in the multimillion-dollar range, preferably within higher education, institutional, government, healthcare, or another similarly complex environment.
  • Experience developing and managing capital project budgets, schedules, procurement activities, change orders, project estimates, bids, and Guaranteed Maximum Price agreements.
  • Knowledge of applicable building codes, safety requirements, sustainability practices, and construction standards, with experience supporting project compliance and quality control.
  • Project Management Professional (PMP), Certified Construction Manager (CCM), LEED credential, or an advanced degree in construction management, architecture, engineering, or a related field.
  • Experience using project management information systems or construction-management platforms, such as Trimble Unity Construct, Microsoft Project, Procore, or comparable software, and providing formal or informal leadership through mentoring, training, or guiding project team members.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

  • The anticipated salary range for this position is $89,076 - $111,345. The final salary will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.
  • This role requires the successful candidate to work on-site at UCF as their primary work location. On-site presence is an essential function of this role.
  • Position requires a valid class E driver’s license. The position may involve driving to various locations on and off campus to conduct University business.
  • All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.

The Opportunity (Job description):

The Department of Writing and Rhetoric (DWR) at the University of Central Florida (UCF) is accepting applications for part-time, adjunct faculty positions with an anticipated start date of January 11, 2027. This appointment is to teach in-person first-year composition courses on our main Orlando campus.

UCF’s First-Year Composition (FYC) Program serves more than 6,000 students annually and received the 2023 CCCC Writing Program Certificate of Excellence Award. FYC is driven by collaboratively-developed student learning outcomes and ePortfolios. The FYC curriculum is informed by guiding principles developed from rhetoric and composition praxis.

Part-time, adjunct faculty report to the Director of First-Year Composition and typically teach two courses.

As an independent writing department, DWR is the academic home to 11 tenure-earning faculty members, 35 full-time instructors and lecturers, and 15 graduate teaching assistants. DWR’s talented writing faculty have a range of expertise in rhetoric and composition and draw from various approaches to teach writing. The department offers a major and minor, graduate program, and certificate programs. The department houses the Center for Writing Excellence encompassing the University Writing Center and the Writing Across the Curriculum program.

UCF offers faculty members at all ranks opportunities for professional development and advancement through its Faculty Center for Teaching and Learning, Office of Faculty Excellence, and Center for Distributed Learning. One of the nation’s largest universities, UCF is a metropolitan, Hispanic serving institution (HSI) that promotes a diverse and inclusive environment. UCF holds the Carnegie Foundation's highest classifications for research activity and community engagement. Central Florida is one of the nation’s fastest-growing and diverse metropolitan areas and is home to a variety of cultural and natural attractions.

 

Responsibilities:

 

  • Teach first-year composition and support student writers
  • Establish strategies and practices that meet the program learning outcomes and ePortfolio
  • Utilize and develop curriculum informed by best practices in writing studies
  • Evaluate student writing in a timely manner   
  • Collaborate with students and colleagues in DWR

 

Minimum Qualifications:

 

  • Master’s degree from an accredited institution in Rhetoric and/or Composition or closely related field; degree must be conferred by August 1, 2026.
  • A minimum of two years teaching college-level composition courses.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Ph.D. in Rhetoric and/or Composition from an accredited institution.
  • Graduate coursework in Composition Histories, Theories, and/or Pedagogy.
  • Demonstrated excellence in teaching college composition and experience working with a range of diverse writer populations, particularly multilingual writers.

Additional Application Materials Required:

 

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/.  In addition to the online application, candidates should attach the following PDF documents:

  • curriculum vitae with contact information for three references,
  • teaching philosophy, and
  • unofficial transcript(s) of graduate-level coursework.

The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.

 

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.

Review of applications will begin immediately.

Questions regarding this search should be directed to Dr. Shane Wood at shane.wood@ucf.edu or for more information on DWR, visit http://writingandrhetoric.cah.ucf.edu.

About this job

Support students receiving employer-sponsored tuition benefits through Guild Education by managing billing, payments, and refunds. Work across multiple campus departments to ensure accurate fee assessment, third-party contract billing, and positive student experiences.

Good fit if you have a bachelor's degree, strong Excel skills, experience with financial or administrative customer service, and attention to detail.

Full job description

Financial Affairs:

Financial Affairs partners with our UCF community to continuously improve and deliver outstanding administrative and financial services through innovative business and technological solutions and sound fiscal stewardship.


The Opportunity:

As a Student Accounts Analyst within the University of Central Florida's (UCF) Financial Affairs division, you'll combine hands-on customer service with financial operations to support students who receive employer-sponsored tuition benefits through Guild Education, one of the nation's leading workforce education platforms. This role serves as UCF's primary liaison for Guild-sponsored students, managing the full billing cycle from eligibility verification through payment reconciliation and refund processing. You'll collaborate regularly with Guild Education, sponsored students, Financial Aid, and key campus offices, including participating in bi-weekly stakeholder meetings to ensure seamless processing and a positive student experience. Success in this role calls for working knowledge of student fee assessment, third-party contract billing, UCF financial policies, and related areas such as Florida Prepaid, deferrals, waivers, 1098-T tax forms, and online payment processing. If you're detail-oriented, thrive in a collaborative environment, and want your work to directly impact students' educational journeys, this is the opportunity for you.


Classification Title: Student Accounts Specialist I


Responsibilities:

  • Serves as the university liaison, Invoicing Guild for various organizations using Guild and university platforms. Communicates with Guild Education, Guild-sponsored students, and other campus offices regarding changes in policy and procedure, billing, timing of billing/payment/reconciliation, and additional employer requirements.
  • Calculates sponsored tuition and fees, digital course materials, qualified housing charges, and offsetting scholarship/grant amounts for eligible students based on sponsor requirements.
  • Researches and responds to questions and inquiries from students, faculty, staff, and others concerning accounting entries, programs and responsibilities of Student Account Services including Guild, tuition and fee charges, waivers, Florida Prepaid, third-party billing, deferrals, direct deposit, refunding, 1098T statements, service indicators, loans and collections, and payment processes.
  • Presents tuition and fee information in a clear and concise manner to help alleviate student/parent and other third parties' misunderstandings about the student's responsibilities regarding payment of tuition and fees.
  • Resolves elevated customer service issues that could not be resolved by other staff members.
  • Calculates and requests refunds back to Guild Education based on overpayment due to late application of scholarships/grants, changes in residency status, and/or late changes in tuition and fees.
  • Calculates and requests revenue share payments to Guild Education based on current MOU with university.
  • Works with Federal, State and Local governmental agencies, Corporate Partners, Financial Aid, Payment Processing, Veteran's Affairs, Registrar, International Student Services, Graduate Studies, Student Development and Enrollment Services, International Governments, and outside agencies to coordinate billing and refunding activities.
  • Assembles, reviews, verifies, and corrects data for financial records, including recording receipt corrections and posting payments and charges to the general ledger.
  • Reviews, verifies, and processes group transactions to apply various charges and payments to both student and organizational accounts.
  • Creates Group Posts or posts groups as needed.
  • Reverses charges or payments per the Reversal spreadsheet as needed.
  • Calculates and posts deferment to students' accounts and works with Office of Student Financial Assistance to ensure deferments are calculated in students' resources.
  • Uses discretion and independent judgment in determining methods and appropriate billing when a myriad of sources may be paying on a student account.
  • Adheres to Federal Regulations, Florida Statutes, Privacy Act and individual agency platform security access and billing requirements.
  • Maintains a close working relationship coordinating various functions with several agencies outside of the university.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's or Master's degree and 0+ years of relevant experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including advanced functions such as VLOOKUP and query writing.
  • Experience with data analysis and reporting, with the ability to interpret and present data insights effectively.
  • Experience with PeopleSoft Query, particularly in updating query criteria.
  • Experience addressing inquiries or concerns from customers, students, or clients in a financial or administrative capacity.
  • Ability to multitask effectively in a fast-paced environment.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

The anticipated hourly rate for a well-qualified candidate is expected to be $20.29 - $22.57. The final rate will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.

Full job description

Counseling and Psychological Services:

Counseling & Psychological Services is home to an interdisciplinary team of full-time psychologists, social workers, mental health counselors, treatment coordinators and support staff who are fully committed to the success and well-being of our students.

 

The Opportunity:

The University of Central Florida’s Counseling and Psychological Services (CAPS) is seeking a professional and detail‑oriented Medical Secretary I to provide essential administrative support in a fast‑paced mental health setting. This position serves as a key point of contact for students and clients and plays an important role in creating a welcoming, respectful, and confidential environment.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Serve as the first point of contact for Counseling and Psychological Services clientele and the campus community at large.
  • Create a welcoming, nurturing, and respectful environment for clients.
  • Electronically check-in arriving clients, process all initial electronic client data, and follow-up contact as needed and/or assigned.
  • Assist clients with electronic check-in processes and procedures.
  • Schedule/reschedule appointments.
  • Observe client behaviors and report to Counselor anything of significance.
  • Work effectively with individuals from varied backgrounds and experiences, including those with psychological challenges or those in distress.
  • Provide primary telephone coverage; assess nature of client calls; determine if immediate assistance by a counselor is indicated; create a professional image of CAPS through responsive, respectful telephone behaviors.
  • Follow established CAPS opening and closing protocol.
  • Provide support to professional staff and CAPS projects as requested in a timely manner.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications:

High School Diploma or equivalent and 0+ years of relevant experience.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 1+ year experience working in a medical, clinical, or mental health office setting.
  • Experience providing front desk and high‑volume telephone coverage in a healthcare or administrative environment.
  • Experience using electronic records systems, scheduling platforms, or similar administrative software.
  • Experience handling confidential or protected health information (PHI) in compliance with privacy standards.

The most successful candidates may possess the following qualities:


  • Ability to maintain boundaries as related to confidentiality.
  • Ability to quickly learn new policies and procedures and computer software programs.
  • Ability to prioritize assigned projects.

 

Additional Application Materials Required:

In addition to your application please include a resume.

  • All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.

The Opportunity:

University Operations is seeking to hire two Information Security Professional IIs support UCF's Identity Governance and Access Management (IGA/IAM) program. The Information Security Professional II administers, monitors, and improves identity lifecycle and access management processes for enterprise systems and institutional users. The role performs operational and technical work related to identity provisioning, access governance, role-based access control, privileged access management, compliance activities, reporting, documentation, stakeholder support, and identity security operations. The position supports students, faculty, staff, researchers, guests, affiliates, sponsored accounts, privileged accounts, and enterprise applications. Working closely with campus stakeholders, application owners, distributed IT teams, and information security partners, this role helps ensure access is appropriately granted, reviewed, documented, and removed when no longer required. The position also supports audit readiness, compliance initiatives, process improvement efforts, and operational continuity through backup support of other Identity Governance and Access Management functions.


Responsibilities:

Identity Lifecycle Management

  • Manage identity lifecycle activities for students, faculty, staff, researchers, guests, affiliates, and sponsored accounts.
  • Perform provisioning, de-provisioning, account updates, affiliation changes, and reconciliation activities.
  • Ensure identity processes are completed accurately and securely in accordance with university policies and procedures.
  • Monitor identity lifecycle operations across university systems.

Access Management & Authorization Support

  • Review, process, and support access requests for enterprise applications and services.
  • Apply established access models, business rules, approval workflows, and authorization procedures.
  • Assist users and business units with access-related requests and troubleshooting.
  • Collaborate with campus partners and technical teams to resolve access-related issues.

Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)

  • Maintain RBAC structures, entitlement mappings, and access assignment processes.
  • Support updates, testing, documentation, and improvement of authorization frameworks.
  • Partner with business and technical teams to resolve access-control issues.

Access Governance, Reviews, Audits, and Compliance

  • Coordinate periodic user access reviews, entitlement validation, and access certification activities.
  • Support audit requests, internal reviews, third-party assessments, and compliance evaluations.
  • Collect, validate, and maintain access records, documentation, and evidence.
  • Identify access discrepancies, track remediation efforts, and prepare reports supporting audit and compliance requirements.
  • Contribute to security documentation, including plans of action and milestones (POA&Ms) and related compliance artifacts.

Guest, Affiliate, and Sponsored Account Administration

  • Administer guest, affiliate, and sponsored account processes from onboarding through de-provisioning.
  • Validate sponsorships, manage renewals and expirations, and ensure access aligns with business needs and institutional policies.

Privileged and Machine Identity Governance

  • Support governance of privileged accounts, administrative accounts, service accounts, service principals, application registrations, and other machine identities.
  • Maintain inventories, conduct periodic reviews, track exceptions and remediation activities, and support control validation efforts.
  • Help ensure privileged access processes remain documented, controlled, and auditable.

Stakeholder Support and Collaboration

  • Provide support to university stakeholders, application owners, distributed IT teams, and information security partners.
  • Deliver responsive customer service and issue resolution.
  • Escalate complex governance, technical, security, or risk-related matters as appropriate.
  • Serve as backup support for other Identity Governance and Access Management functions.

Documentation and Process Improvement

  • Develop and maintain standard operating procedures, work instructions, knowledge articles, and process documentation.
  • Ensure documentation remains accurate, consistent, and audit-ready.
  • Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, strengthen controls, reduce manual effort, and enhance user experience.
  • Promote operational efficiency, knowledge sharing, and service continuity.

Reporting and Data Analysis

  • Prepare and maintain identity and access management reports.
  • Conduct data quality reviews, reconciliations, and access trend analysis.
  • Protect sensitive identity, access, and security information while supporting management reporting needs.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree and 2 years of relevant experience; or High School Diploma (or equivalent) and 6 years of relevant work experience in lieu of degree; or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with Identity Governance and Administration (IGA) or Identity and Access Management (IAM) platforms.
  • Knowledge of identity lifecycle management, provisioning, and de-provisioning processes.
  • Experience supporting role-based access control (RBAC) and access governance practices.
  • Familiarity with privileged access management concepts and controls.
  • Experience supporting audits, compliance reviews, and access certifications.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and documentation skills.
  • Ability to communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Experience working in higher education or other complex enterprise environments.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

Position requires a valid Class E driver’s license. This position may involve driving to various locations on and off campus to conduct University business.


The anticipated salary range for this position is $64,518 - $80,000. The final salary will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.


All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.


This role requires the successful candidate to work on-site at UCF as their primary work location. On-site presence is an essential function of this role.


UCF is seeking to fill multiple roles. Candidates for this job posting will be considered for additional Information Security Professional II vacancies in this department.

About this job

Secure major gifts of $25,000+ for the College of Business by cultivating relationships with alumni, parents, and community partners. Manage a donor portfolio independently, develop fundraising strategies, and collaborate with college leadership to advance philanthropic goals.

Good fit if you have 6+ years of major gift fundraising experience and are authorized to work in the U.S.

Full job description

Advancement & Partnerships:

Join our dynamic and growing Advancement & Partnerships team as we work together to power partnerships and transform lives through philanthropy.

Together, we can unleash the potential of people and ideas to positively change the world.  Your efforts on our team will help us to build the University for the Future.

 

The Opportunity:

The Director of Development for the College of Business (COB) is responsible for securing major gifts of $25,000+ by cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding alumni, parents, friends, and community partners. This position plays a pivotal role in advancing the college’s priorities and UCF's mission by building meaningful relationships with current and prospective donors.

The Director will independently manage a portfolio of major gift donors, develop and implement fundraising strategies, and partner with the Dean, faculty, and leadership to drive philanthropic growth for COB initiatives.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Manage a portfolio of major gift prospects/donors, with a focus on individuals, through discovery, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
  • Design and implement fundraising strategies that support the needs and priorities of COB and UCF.
  • Conduct face-to-face visits and develop donor-centered proposals to secure major gifts.
  • Collaborate with the Dean and division leadership to expand the fundraising pipeline and strengthen engagement of advisory board members.
  • Ensure effective use of prospect management tools, research, contact reports, and our CRM database.
  • Acknowledge and recognize gifts in ways that are meaningful to donors and aligned with UCF’s strategic plan, vision, and values.
  • Maintain best practices in office systems, records, acknowledgments, and stewardship activities.
  • Perform related duties as required to advance the college's fundraising success.

 

Minimum Qualifications: 

Bachelor's or Master's degree and 6+ years of relevant experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Demonstrated experience identifying, cultivating, and closing major gifts of $25,000 or more from individual donors.
  • Experience as a frontline fundraiser, gift officer, nonprofit development professional, or similar relationship-driven revenue generation role.
  • Experience in higher education advancement, nonprofit fundraising, healthcare philanthropy, alumni engagement, or a related fundraising environment.
  • Experience building and managing donor, prospect, client, or partner relationships through a portfolio-based engagement cycle.
  • Experience developing donor-centered proposals, gift agreements, or persuasive fundraising materials.
  • Proficiency with Blackbaud, Salesforce, Raiser’s Edge or comparable fundraising, donor management, or CRM platforms.
  • Deep leadership experience.
  • Ability to travel in and out of state for meetings and events as needed.

The most successful candidates may possess the following qualities:

  • Strong communication, active listening, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to engage a variety of donor and partner audiences.
  • Demonstrated initiative, resilience, and self-motivation in a goal-oriented fundraising or revenue-generating environment.
  • Strategic thinker with excellent organizational skills, able to manage multiple projects and deadlines simultaneously.
  • Familiarity with or interest in UCF, College of Business, business related fields, or university advancement.

  • The anticipated salary for a well-qualified candidate is between $85,000-$100,000.
  • Advancement and Partnerships values the unique contributions that each team member brings to our division. The anticipated pay scale indicated for this position generally applies to candidates who meet the minimum requirements and several of the preferred qualifications outlined above. All offers are contingent on successful background and reference screens.

About this job

Tenure-track assistant professor position in Clinical Psychology at UCF's Department of Psychology, one of the largest in the nation. Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in multiple modalities and conduct research in health services psychology within a department housing APA-accredited Ph.D. and master's programs.

Good fit if you have a Ph.D. in health services psychology, are eligible for Florida licensure, and have research interests complementing clinical psychology strengths.

Full job description

The Opportunity

The Department of Psychology in the College of Sciences (COS) at the University of Central Florida (UCF) invites applications for one full-time, 9-month, tenure track assistant professor position in Clinical Psychology, anticipated to begin in August 2027. We seek dedicated and collegial educators/scientists who can establish collaborative relationships within the department/college as well as with other colleges at the university and within the community. The successful candidate will be expected to teach undergraduate and graduate courses in different modalities, including face-to-face and online. The instructional duties and services assignments are in accordance with the department’s current equitable workload policy.


Area of research specialization within health services psychology is open. We are interested in collaborative candidates with programs of research that can contribute to and complement program, department, and university strengths (see faculty areas of expertise here: https://sciences.ucf.edu/psychology/people/).


The Department of Psychology is one of the largest departments by enrollment at UCF, with more than 50 full-time faculty and approximately 4,000 undergraduate majors. The department has three broad areas of emphasis in clinical psychology, human factors and cognitive psychology, and industrial and organizational psychology. UCF’s online bachelor’s degree in Psychology is ranked #3 in the nation by U.S. News and World Report. All members of the department share a common goal of understanding behavior through empirical investigation, which is reflected in teaching and research. 


The department is home to two terminal master's programs in Clinical Psychology and I/O Psychology, and three Ph.D. programs in Clinical Psychology, I/O Psychology, and Human Factors and Cognitive Psychology.


The Clinical Psychology Ph.D. Program has maintained American Psychological Association (APA) accreditation since 2003, and in 2023 received the maximum re-accreditation period of ten years. The program houses a training clinic, which serves the UCF and surrounding communities.

To learn more about the Clinical Psychology program, please see our website at https://sciences.ucf.edu/psychology/graduate/ph-d-clinical/. For more information about the department visit https://sciences.ucf.edu/psychology/.


The UCF College of Sciences (COS) is the largest college at the university and a powerhouse for the regional and national STEM workforce, spanning the natural, computational, physical, and social sciences and housing centers, institutes and initiatives that serve as hubs for research and innovation. Through sharing and applying knowledge, COS is cultivating pathways for students to solve our world’s most pressing and complex problems. With a mission to provide a world-class education in an environment where faculty, staff, and students thrive, research flourishes, and our community prospers; a number of COS academic programs are among those nationally ranked by U.S. News and World Report, Princeton Review, and others.


For more information, please visit https://sciences.ucf.edu.


Minimum Qualifications:

  • Ph.D. in an area of health services psychology from an APA- or PCSAS-accredited program by the date of hire.
  • Eligible for licensure as a Psychologist in Florida, or able to obtain licensure as Psychologist in Florida within 2 years of hire.

Preferred Qualifications:

Ideal candidates will have:

  • A research program with the potential for external funding.
  • Publications in peer-reviewed journals.
  • Evidence of, or potential for, teaching and/or mentoring effectiveness.
  • Demonstrated ability and/or potential to supervise Clinical Psychology Ph.D. students in evidence-based psychological services.

Additional Application Materials Required:

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following:

  • A cover letter of interest which includes statements of research (including future research plans), teaching interest (including evidence of teaching, if available, and clinical supervision interest), and eligibility for licensure as a Psychologist in the state of Florida  or plans for licensure.
  • A curriculum vitae (CV).

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.


The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalence evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials and names and contact information of three professional references.


Questions regarding the position should be directed to Dr. Amie Newins, Search Committee Chair, at Amie.Newins@ucf.edu


Special Instructions to the Applicants:

All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. H-1B visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H-1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.

The Opportunity:

Bring your energy and facilitation skills to a role with university-wide impact. As a Training Specialist II on UCF’s Talent Development team, you’ll lead in-person learning experiences that help employees build skills they can use right away and give supervisors practical ways to support their teams’ performance and growth. If you enjoy connecting with adult learners and seeing them put what they learn to work, you’ll help make professional development part of everyday work at one of the nation’s largest universities.

 

Responsibilities:

About this job

Administrative Assistant II for the School of Data, Mathematical, and Statistical Sciences at UCF. Manages facilities, budgets for student organizations, supervises work-study students, coordinates faculty meetings, and handles complex administrative projects for approximately 100 faculty and graduate students.

Good fit if you have 2+ years of administrative experience, strong organizational skills, proficiency with Microsoft Office and enterprise systems, and can work on-site in Orlando.

Full job description

The Opportunity: 

The Kanouff School of Data, Mathematical, and Statistical Sciences is seeking an Administrative Assistant II position to position performs complex administrative, fiscal, and project coordination functions for SDMSS. This includes autonomous facilities management, independent budget tracking for student groups, and the supervision of student work-study staff, which requires specialized knowledge and decision-making beyond general administrative support.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Independently manage and track all physical assets for the unit, including issuing and collecting keys and rooms for approximately 100 faculty, postdocs, and graduate students. This high-risk function requires daily autonomous decision-making.
  • Serve as the primary administrative liaison for the Mathematics Safety Team and independently coordinate all complex building work orders and property asset management.
  • Manage official internal and external communications on behalf of the Director and School; organize and serve as recording secretary for all faculty meetings (taking attendance and minutes).
  • Handle high-volume, sensitive academic support tasks, including securing building-wide room reservations and overseeing the secure copying and distribution of all faculty exams.
  • Coordinates student employment and onboarding activities for the department, including recruitment support, interview scheduling, hiring documentation, onboarding, training coordination, and ongoing administrative support for student employees. Provide direct and daily supervision for 4-6 Federal Work Study students.
  • Independently manage the financial health and track budgets for multiple School student organizations (e.g., Math Club, Math Knights, Actuarial Science), including all receipt processing and reconciliation.
  • Coordinate complex administrative projects (e.g., over a dozen faculty office transitions). Process all colloquium speaker and visitor travel arrangements.
  • Provide front-desk coverage, screen complex incoming calls, triage office visitor issues and resolve or direct to appropriate places for resolution. Order all departmental supplies and coordinate textbook documentation.

Minimum Qualifications: 

High School Diploma or Equivalent and 2+ years of relevant experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to interact professionally with students, faculty, and visitors.
  • Strong organizational skills, including the ability to track physical assets and to maintain accurate electronic records of inventory, requests, and deadlines.
  • Experience with the Microsoft Office suite (Word, Excel, Outlook) and enterprise systems including PeopleSoft and Workday.
  • Ability to work collaboratively within and across teams, with demonstrated adaptability, problem-solving skills, and the ability to learn new processes quickly.

 

Additional Application Materials Required:

Consideration will be given to applications that include a resume and cover letter.

Office of Research:

The University of Central Florida (UCF) Office of Research sets the standard for excellence in service to our stakeholders by supporting research, commercialization, and economic growth. Through strategic partnerships, collaboration, and integrity, we foster an environment where employees can pursue their personal and professional goals while contributing to organizational success. We serve as an essential resource for attracting and retaining premier talent and research funding through operational excellence, innovative technology, and cohesive teamwork.

  

The Opportunity:

The Finance/Budget Analyst will process financial transactions within university financial systems. They will also prepare statements and reports relating to an assigned area of responsibility, monitor records of past and present operations, and apply university accounting policies and procedures in working with accounting records and reports. The Analyst is tasked with assembling, analyzing, and reconciling data and transactions. They will monitor departmental accounts for compliance with applicable regulations and coordinate with the Budget/Finance Director and/or Manager on fiscal compliance.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Prepare budgets and forecast revenues and expenses and provide specialized financial reporting and analysis for Office of Research, including but not limited to the Institutes and Centers, Service Centers and Faculty Cluster Initiatives.
  • Develop and load budgets and associated adjustments into budget management systems and monitor budgetary variances and corrects as appropriate.
  • Correct unassigned budget transfers to appropriate revenue or spend categories and reconcile accounts to ensure accuracy of transactions.
  • Prepare costing allocations for payroll funding, corrections to payroll funding and review, reconcile, and validate Workday work tags, initiate work tag changes as needed.
  • Collaborate with HR on workforce funding planning and allocations and identify appropriate funding sources for various financial and HR transactions.
  • Prepare, review, or correct workforce funding changes and approve, deny, or return Workday spend transactions.
  • Work closely with other members of the business center and sponsored programs team to disseminate accounting information and ensure compliance.
  • Act as liaison between the PI, Office of Research and colleges/units. 
  • Perform all other duties as assigned.

 

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree and 4+ years of relevant experience or combination of relevant comparable education and experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6). 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in financial forecasting, budget development, budget monitoring, and financial reconciliations, preferably within a higher education environment.
  • Proficiency in financial management systems, such as Workday or comparable ERP platforms.
  • Familiarity of financial regulations, policies, and accounting standards, particularly those applicable to higher education and research institutions.
  • Demonstrated experience in post award financial management, including the administration of sponsored projects, contract and grant accounts and coordination with principal investigators.

About this job

Cloud Computing Engineer I supporting UCF's research enterprise through building, deploying, and managing secure cloud environments. Role combines cloud infrastructure work with direct researcher collaboration on projects involving sensitive data, scripting, and automation.

Good fit if you have a bachelor's degree or four years of relevant work experience, plus hands-on cloud platform experience.

Full job description

Graduate and Research Information Technology (GRIT):

Graduate and Research Information Technology (GRIT) is the dedicated information technology organization supporting UCF’s research enterprise. GRIT delivers specialized technology services, enterprise solutions, and strategic guidance to faculty, staff, and research administration units across the university. Operating within the Office of Research, GRIT encompasses key functional areas such as research administration systems, data and analytics, application development, systems integration, and customer support.

GRIT partners closely with academic and administrative stakeholders through established governance structures and collaborative working groups to ensure that technology initiatives align with UCF’s research priorities. With a commitment to innovation, security, and excellent service delivery, GRIT advances the university’s mission by enabling efficient research operations, supporting compliance and reporting needs, and strengthening technology capabilities that empower discovery and institutional growth.

 

The Opportunity:

The GRIT team within UCF's Office of Research is seeking a Cloud Computing Engineer I to assist in building, deploying, monitoring, and supporting secure, resilient, and cost-effective cloud computing environments that support and enhance research productivity and reliability while following established best practices. This customer-focused position works closely with researchers, systems architects, and other systems team members to support cloud-based research environments and applications.

Responsibilities:

Research Cloud Consultation:

  • Work closely with researchers to help set up research project environments in the cloud, including provisioning and de-provisioning, deploying, managing, operating cloud resources, and supporting research applications hosted in cloud environments.
  • Develop an understanding of research activities through regular engagement with researchers.
  • Assist in estimating cloud costs for research projects.
  • Monitor cloud resources and service health; identify and escalate issues when necessary.
  • May work with research projects with highly restricted data like Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), electronic Protected Health Information (ePHI), personally identifiable information (PII), ITAR-restricted and other protected information as it pertains to various federal agencies and sub-agencies.

Software Development:

  • Support the UCF Research Cloud Environment by developing, deploying, operating, and maintaining cloud services and applications, troubleshooting issues, and helping ensure efficient and reliable cloud-based storage and computing resources.
  • Assist in maintaining Infrastructure as Code templates and deployment automation.
  • Write scripts to automate cloud operations and routine administrative tasks.
  • Perform testing and validation of cloud services and configurations prior to deployment.
  • Apply and maintain security best practices in cloud environments.
  • Follow defined project plans and scopes of work, tracking progress against assigned milestones.

Partnership/Collaboration:

  • Work collaboratively with other team engineers and researchers to build and maintain the applications and services that sit on top of the cloud infrastructure.
  • Assist researchers in gathering and refining technical requirements for cloud-based research projects.
  • Participate in project meetings and technical discussions with researchers and stakeholders to support project objectives.
  • Provide regular communications to project leads with updates.

Documentation/Training:

  • Maintain internal guides and documentation for future contributors.
  • Assist in creating training materials for researchers about the use of cloud environments and related best practices.
  • Support virtual and in-person training events by facilitating logistics, introducing speakers, moderating discussions and participant interactions, providing attendee support, gathering feedback, and assisting with post-event surveys and assessment activities.
  • Develop and apply expertise in specific technologies to support research initiatives and create custom solutions that address researcher needs.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree; or High School Diploma (or equivalent) and 4 years of relevant work experience in lieu of degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6). 


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Technical knowledge or hands-on experience — gained through coursework, academic projects, internships, or other applied work — with scripting or programming languages (e.g., Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, or Bash), Linux environments, version control tools (e.g., Git), Infrastructure as Code frameworks (e.g., Terraform), and/or cloud computing platforms (e.g., AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud).
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences such as researchers and faculty.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a team-oriented environment, collaborating across technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Hands-on experience deploying, configuring, or supporting applications or services in a cloud environment (e.g., AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud) — including through coursework, academic projects, or personal work.
  • Familiarity with cloud security principles and best practices, such as identity and access management (IAM), data encryption, or network security configurations in cloud environments.
  • Experience creating or maintaining technical documentation, process guides, or user-facing instructional materials, as well as hosting workshops for non-technical stakeholders.
  • Familiarity with or exposure to research, academic, or scientific computing environments — including through academic programs, lab work, or support roles.

  • This role requires the successful candidate to maintain residence within driving distance of UCF and be available to report to campus as needed. On-site presence for occasional meetings, special projects, and other business-related activities is an essential function of this role.

The Opportunity: 

This position reports to the Director of UCF Abroad and serves as lead support for administrative and office functions of the unit.

The Administrative Coordinator II assists unit leadership with: financial processes and budget management; prep for student recruitment marketing and events; occasionally assist with data collection and reporting; and primary contact for daily office operations.

 

Responsibilities:

About this job

Controls Specialist II supporting HVAC systems and building automation at UCF. Responsibilities include preventative maintenance, installation and repair of BAS controllers, system updates, and coordination with the commissioning team to improve operational efficiency.

Good fit if you have 4+ years of HVAC and controls experience, knowledge of building management systems software, and a valid Class E driver's license.

Full job description

University Operations:

The University Operations division at UCF is committed to creating a supportive and welcoming environment for our faculty, staff, students, and the broader community. We take pride in delivering exceptional service, sharing our expertise, and upholding the highest standards to ensure a world-class campus experience.

Visit our website or follow us on Facebook and Instagram to learn more.

 

The Opportunity:

Join our team as a Controls Specialist II where you will play a pivotal role in providing technical support, retro commissioning and first-analysis of HVAC performance investigations for coordinated operations and maintenance of HVAC systems to provide a safe, functional, clean, efficient and attractive learning environment. At this level, the employee is expected to have intermediate skills in HVAC and Controls Systems.

Responsibilities:

  • Perform preventative maintenance on HVAC building automation systems and related equipment in order to ensure continuous operation and prevent equipment interruptions through proactive analysis of the BAS front end and back end software platforms.
  • Install, repair, replace and recalibrate BAS controllers, terminal devices and ancillary components to maintain continuously commissioned HVAC BAS controls. 
  • Perform continuous updates and improvements to system front end graphics, back end programming and parametric configurations, databases and networks. 
  • Work in conjunction with the Utility and Energy Services commissioning /retro commissioning team to deliver BAS operational and energy efficiency improvements. 
  • Conduct minor repairs including but not limited to coordinating and assisting in complex corrective and planned maintenance on: pneumatic air systems, DDC controls, cooling towers, chillers, boilers, heating hot water and steam systems, hydronic pumps and related piping and components, chilled water air handlers, fan-coil units, VAV terminal boxes, direct expansion (DX), PTAC units, exhaust fans, ventilated systems, CRAC and CRAH units.
  • Serve as the first response team for indoor environmental work requests received and dispatched by Work Control Center.    

 

Minimum Qualifications:

High School Diploma or Equivalent and 4+ years of relevant experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6). 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Thorough understanding of HVAC controls theory and concepts; to include sequence of operations review, design, implementation, operation, and testing.
  • Proficient in the use of Building Management Systems software such as: Siemens Desigo, Trane, Tracer Ensemble, Tracer Summit, Enteliweb, and WebCTRL.
  • Knowledge of HVAC systems, boilers, chillers, air compressors, fans, and pumps.
  • Experience in repair and maintenance of digital building control systems.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office software (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.) and other computer programs such as Visio is preferred.
  • Skilled in the use and safety of hand tools, power tools, electrical digital meters, balometer, and machines.
  • Ability to read construction drawings and specifications.
  • Ability to read and understand printed process, circuit, and electrical schematics.
  • Ability to troubleshoot electronic and pneumatic controls.

Health Assessment Required:  

UCF policy requires completion and passing of a physical exam for this position.

Position requires a valid Class E driver’s license. This position may involve driving to various locations on and off campus to conduct University business.

May be required to participate in respiratory, medical examination and training in use of respirators.

Knights Experience Team (kNEXT):

The University of Central Florida’s (UCF’s) the Knights Experience Team (kNEXT) primarily provides customer service to the Finance Business Centers (FBCs) and the Human Resources Business Centers (HRBC's) employees, assisting with various tasks as needed. kNEXT also provides administrative support services to staff across all colleges and divisions of the University. kNEXT is designed to reduce the administrative burden on individual colleges, consolidate transaction-based functions, create economies of scale, and improve backroom process efficiency so the colleges can better focus resources on their mission.

The team is made up of HR Specialists and Travel/Procurement Specialists, who will provide information and support across campus, reduce administrative burden, and empower employees to learn and grow. These Specialists will operate as campus experts on processes and procedures, support training and development, provide specialized reporting and analytics, and support central office transactions. All employees within kNEXT will also work to continuously improve processes and workflows.

The purpose of kNEXT is to ensure that the services provided meet or exceed expected performance levels and satisfy the needs of the faculty/staff/students (colleges/divisions).

 

The Opportunity: 

The Knights Experience Team (kNEXT) is seeking a Travel & Procurement Specialist III to lead a team of specialists supporting travel and procurement for one of the nation's largest universities. With more than 70,000 students and 13,000 employees, UCF relies on purchasing and travel processes that are accurate, efficient, and built to serve colleges and divisions across campus. As a working lead, you'll guide and develop your team, serve as a go-to expert for campus partners, and help shape the processes that keep the university moving. Bring your leadership to UCF and help build a team that empowers thousands of faculty and staff to focus on what matters most.

 

Responsibilities:

Team Leadership

  • Supervisory responsibilities, including hiring and training, monitoring performance and providing feedback, maintaining leave requests and personnel records, setting goals and objectives and monitoring accomplishments, enforcing customer service standards, and resolving complex issues.

Procurement, Contracts, and Payments

  • Support requests for the procurement of goods and services ensuring applicable policies and regulations are adhered to and transactions are processed timely and properly reflect the receipt of goods or services.
  • Research suppliers and obtain quotes for goods and services, as needed.
  • Assist with the development of solicitations for bids and participate in the development of contracts and agreements.
  • Identify and review applicable contracts or the need for a Waiver of Competition and Sole Source Certification in accordance with policies and regulations.
  • Initiate and review requisitions, manage purchase orders, and initiate change orders, as needed.
  • Create receipts and supplier invoices or purchasing card transactions to ensure timely payments.

Advancement & Partnerships:

Join our dynamic and growing Advancement & Partnerships team as we work together to power partnerships and transform lives through philanthropy.

Together, we can unleash the potential of people and ideas to positively change the world.  Your efforts on our team will help us to build the University for the Future.

 

The Opportunity:

The Advancement & Partnerships division leads the university’s fundraising and alumni engagement work. We’re looking for a Prospect Research Analyst II to help our fundraisers find and understand the alumni, individuals, companies, and foundations most likely to support UCF.

Working with the Assistant Director of Prospect Research and the broader research team, you’ll turn public information into clear, confidential profiles that shape how we build donor relationships. Your research will inform everything from annual giving to the university’s largest gifts, and your work will help prepare UCF’s president and senior leaders for conversations with key guests at university events.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Research and analyze biographical, business, and financial information on alumni, individuals, corporations, and foundations, then distill findings into concise, confidential profiles that support fundraisers at every gift level.
  • Assign and refine estimated giving capacity ratings using wealth screening data and help develop rating methods based on industry’s best practices.
  • Monitor news, job announcements, and other sources to spot new prospects and relevant updates, alerting fundraising staff when follow-up is needed.
  • Keep donor and alumni records accurate by entering new information and verifying and cleaning existing records.
  • Lead the event briefing process with our donor experience team and campus partners, preparing the university president and senior leadership with background on select guests.
  • Respond to high-priority and ad hoc research requests, working with the team to plan and manage how requests are fulfilled.

Minimum Qualifications: 

Bachelor's degree and 2+ years of related experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in prospect research or donor research in higher education or a nonprofit setting.
  • Working knowledge of fundraising processes and how research supports gift strategy at different levels.
  • Experience with wealth screening tools and assigning capacity ratings.
  • Ability to interpret financial and business information, such as public company filings, real estate records, and foundation tax returns.
  • Experience maintaining records in a donor or constituent database.
  • Strong writing skills, with the ability to summarize complex information briefly and clearly.
  • Experience preparing briefing materials for senior executives.
  • Sound judgment in handling confidential information, with an understanding of ethical standards for prospect research.
  • Ability to manage multiple high-priority requests on tight timelines.

All offers are contingent on successful background and reference screens.

About this job

Monitor compliance with institutional policies, sponsor agreements, and procedures at UCF's Pegasus Research Institute. Develop reporting tools, track corrective actions, and conduct reviews to ensure accuracy and integrity of programmatic, operational, and financial reporting.

Good fit if you have 5-8 years in compliance, audit, or sponsored research, with experience in evidence-quality testing and analytical review.

Full job description

Pegasus Research Institute:

Pegasus Research Institute (PRI) is the University of Central Florida’s applied research institute, bringing together expertise from across UCF to solve complex, real-world challenges. Through multidisciplinary collaboration among faculty, researchers, students, and industry and government partners, PRI helps move innovative ideas from research and prototyping to real-world validation and deployment. Its work spans space technologies, health and human performance, energy and sustainability, immersive experiences, and transformative technologies and national security, creating a dynamic environment where research, innovation, and operational impact intersect.


The Opportunity:

This position is responsible for monitoring adherence to institutional requirements, sponsor agreements, policies, and procedures while ensuring the accuracy, consistency, and integrity of programmatic, operational, and financial reporting. The analyst conducts reviews, maintains compliance documentation, tracks corrective actions, and develops reporting tools that support informed decision-making and continuous improvement.


Responsibilities:

  • Monitor compliance with institutional policies, sponsor requirements, agreements, and established procedures.
  • Maintain documentation, records, and evidence necessary to support audits, reviews, and compliance assessments.
  • Perform evidence-quality testing and document-control activities to ensure reporting accuracy and audit readiness.
  • Develop and maintain reporting calendars, key performance indicators (KPIs), compliance checklists, and control schedules.
  • Track risks, exceptions, corrective actions, and compliance issues, ensuring appropriate follow-up and resolution.
  • Conduct analytical reviews and reconciliations across programmatic, project, operational, and financial reports.
  • Prepare recurring and ad hoc reports that communicate performance, compliance status, trends, and risks to leadership.
  • Identify reporting discrepancies, process gaps, and control weaknesses and recommend corrective actions.
  • Support internal and external audits by gathering documentation, coordinating responses, and tracking remediation efforts.
  • Assist with policy interpretation and provide guidance on compliance-related processes and requirements.
  • Collaborate with program, project, finance, and operational teams to improve reporting quality and process efficiency.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that strengthen compliance controls and operational effectiveness.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution with 5-8 years in compliance, audit, sponsored research, quality assurance, internal controls, or performance reporting.


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Agreement, procedure, and institutional-requirement alignment.
  • Evidence-quality testing, audit readiness, and document control.
  • Reporting calendars, KPI definitions, control schedules, and review checklists.
  • Risk, corrective-action, exception, and issue tracking.
  • Analytical review and reconciliation across program, project, and financial reporting.
  • Policy interpretation and process improvement in regulated environments.

Pegasus Research Institute:

Pegasus Research Institute (PRI) is the University of Central Florida’s applied research institute, bringing together expertise from across UCF to solve complex, real-world challenges. Through multidisciplinary collaboration among faculty, researchers, students, and industry and government partners, PRI helps move innovative ideas from research and prototyping to real-world validation and deployment. Its work spans space technologies, health and human performance, energy and sustainability, immersive experiences, and transformative technologies and national security, creating a dynamic environment where research, innovation, and operational impact intersect.


The Opportunity:

This position provides strategic financial management and sponsored research administration support for the institute's research portfolio. The incumbent is responsible for overseeing budget development, financial forecasting, award management, compliance monitoring, financial reporting, and post-award administration for federal, state, industry, and other sponsored projects. This position serves as a key partner to institute leadership, principal investigators, and administrative offices to ensure sound financial stewardship, regulatory compliance, and effective management of research funding.


Responsibilities:

  • Manage the financial administration of sponsored research programs, grants, contracts, and institutional funding sources.
  • Develop and oversee operating budgets, multi-year financial plans, forecasts, and funding projections for research programs and institute operations.
  • Monitor expenditures and revenue activity to ensure appropriate use of funds and compliance with sponsor requirements and institutional policies.
  • Analyze funding availability and provide recommendations to institute leadership regarding budget planning, resource allocation, and financial strategy.
  • Prepare executive-level financial reports, budget summaries, projections, and ad hoc analyses to support decision-making.
  • Review and monitor cost allowability, cost allocation, cost sharing, and other financial compliance requirements.
  • Coordinate invoicing, account reconciliations, and financial transactions associated with sponsored awards and research activities.
  • Maintain accurate financial records and supporting documentation to facilitate audits, reviews, and sponsor reporting.
  • Manage award setup, modifications, amendments, subawards, and closeout activities in accordance with sponsor and institutional requirements.
  • Ensure compliance with federal, state, sponsor, and institutional regulations governing sponsored research activities.

Minimum Qualifications:

Master's degree from an accredited institution with 7-10 years in strategic communications, public affairs, stakeholder engagement, research communications, or related program communications.


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Communications strategy, message architecture, editorial planning, and brand governance.
  • Executive, public, sponsor, and multi-stakeholder communications.
  • Workshops, events, councils, industry outreach, and stakeholder engagement.
  • Website, content, publication, and technical-communications oversight.
  • Issues, approvals, sensitive-content, and crisis-communications management.
  • Team leadership and workload prioritization across communications deliverables.

Additional Application Materials Required:

  • In addition to the online application, candidates should upload a cover letter and current curriculum vitae.
  • UCF requires all applications and supporting documents be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website.
  • The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.


Questions regarding this search should be directed to Abram Walton, Abram.Walton@ucf.edu and Wayne Fogel, Wayne.Fogel@ucf.edu

The anticipated hourly range for this position is $44.06 - $71.84. The final rate will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.

Human Resources:

UCF Human Resources is a trusted partner and catalyst in making UCF the best place to work and positively impact our community by working together to unleash the potential of everyone at UCF. We make it our mission to support and advance UCF’s goals by fostering a positive and engaging work environment while identifying and responding to the changing needs of our community.


The Opportunity:

UCF Human Resources is seeking a Senior Compensation Partner to serve as the lead compensation consultant for one of the nation's largest universities. With more than 70,000 students and 13,000 employees, UCF makes pay decisions that shape how we attract, retain, and reward the people behind our mission. As a subject matter expert and technical leader, you'll turn compensation priorities into the programs and practices that support employees across the university. You'll also lead the systems and reporting efforts that power those decisions, and you'll mentor and guide colleagues across the compensation team. Bring your expertise to UCF and help build the future of how we recognize and reward our people.


Responsibilities:

Compensation Expertise and Technical Leadership

  • Serve as the lead compensation consultant and subject matter expert, independently resolving complex issues across base pay, salary structures, job architecture, position classification, job evaluations, market pricing, and internal equity.
  • Partner with HR business partners and institutional leaders to develop practical, data-informed compensation solutions that maintain equity, policy compliance, and governance.
  • Provide day-to-day technical guidance and mentorship to compensation colleagues as a primary resource for complex inquiries.

Workday HCM and Advanced Compensation

  • Lead optimization and continuous improvement of Workday HCM and serve as the functional owner of Workday Advanced Compensation, including annual salary program execution.
  • Partner with the Enterprise ERP team to define requirements, perform functional and unit testing, and support implementation through process redesign, documentation, and end-user training.

Projects and Continuous Improvement

  • Lead and support compensation projects, programs, and process improvements, translating leadership priorities into actionable plans, tools, and deliverables.

Compensation Strategy and Salary Programs

  • Support the Senior Director of Compensation in university-wide compensation strategy, planning, and administration of salary programs, including annual salary programs and merit increases.

Reporting, Analytics, and Data Governance

  • Provide functional leadership for compensation reporting, analytics, and dashboards, including Power BI, in collaboration with Enterprise Reporting and HR technology partners.
  • Support compensation data audits, validation procedures, and standardized reporting practices that strengthen data integrity.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's or Master's degree and 4+ years of relevant experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Six or more years of progressive compensation experience, including market pricing, job evaluations, and position classification.
  • Experience serving as a consultant and trusted advisor to HR business partners and organizational leaders, providing sound judgment and data-informed compensation recommendations.
  • Experience mentoring, training, or serving as a technical resource for compensation colleagues.
  • Experience with Workday or a similar Human Resources Information System (HRIS) to support compensation administration and ensure data accuracy and integrity.
  • Experience leading or contributing to compensation or HR systems projects and process improvements, including requirements gathering, testing, process redesign, and end-user training.
  • Experience supporting the administration of enterprise-wide salary programs, such as annual salary programs and merit increases.
  • Experience developing compensation reports, dashboards, or analytics, such as Power BI, and supporting data audits or validation to strengthen data integrity.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

  • The anticipated salary for this position is $110,000. The final salary will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.
  • All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.
  • This role requires the successful candidate to work on-site at UCF as their primary work location. On-site presence is an essential function of this role.
  • Classification Title: Compensation Partner III
