Full job description

Rosen College of Hospitality Management:

The Rosen College of Hospitality Management is comprised of approximately 100 wide-ranging faculty and staff members that represent over 18 different countries and are recognized for their research, teaching skills, and industry impact. Rosen College students are exposed to some of the most modern and well-designed learning laboratories as they pursue one of the many B.S., M.S., and Ph.D. majors offered.


Learn more about UCF’s Rosen College of Hospitality Management.


The Opportunity:

The UCF Rosen College of Hospitality Management is one of the most renowned hospitality programs in the world, and the students who move through its culinary labs are the next generation of industry leaders. As a Food and Beverage Specialist II, you'll be right in the middle of that experience — working alongside the college's Chefs to support hands-on undergraduate culinary lab sessions, maintain the quality and safety of the culinary and beverage lab environments, and help bring large-scale catered events to life.


We are currently seeking a Food and Beverage Specialist II, who brings real kitchen experience and takes pride in both craft and consistency to join this dynamic team. You'll play a meaningful role in shaping the day-to-day learning environment for students while contributing to the operational excellence that Rosen College is known for. If you're passionate about food service and ready to bring your expertise into an academic setting where it truly makes an impact — this is your opportunity.
 

Responsibilities:

  • Assist the Chefs and/or Food & Beverage Specialist III, in training UCF undergraduate students during lab sessions and maintain organization and cleanliness in the culinary and beverage labs.
  • Assist the Food & Beverage Specialist III in planning and executing advanced and complex catered events, internal or external, on the Rosen Campus.
  • Sustain the cleanliness, organization, and safety of all food and beverage supplies, equipment, and facilities on the Rosen College Campus.
  • Adhere to and ensure proper receiving, storage, and inventory (FIFO) practices, and assist with the pickup and delivery of food and beverage products and supplies.
  • Additional duties as assigned based on the needs of the department, college, and UCF as directed by the department head, chair, and dean.

Minimum Qualifications:

High School Diploma or Equivalent and 4+ years of relevant experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).


Preferred Qualifications:

  • 2+ years of experience working in a fast-paced culinary, restaurant, or fast-food environment.
  • Experience assisting with training, mentoring, or guiding others in a food service or kitchen environment.
  • Basic knowledge of food safety, sanitation, and safe food handling practices.
  • Experience supporting catered events, banquets, or large-volume food preparation.
  • Previous experience working in a higher education food lab or similar setting is highly desirable.

The most successful candidates may possess the following qualities:

  • Adaptability and willingness to learn new techniques and processes.
  • Effective collaboration within a team, with the ability to work independently when required.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with a customer service–focused approach.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

Position requires a valid Class E driver’s license. The position may involve driving to various locations on and off campus to conduct University business.


The anticipated hourly range for this position is $15.66 to $17.23 per hour. The final rate will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.


Additional evening or weekend hours may be required to support business needs, events, or project deadlines.


All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.

The Opportunity  

The School of Teacher Education (STE) in the College of Community Innovation and Education (CCIE) is dedicated to preparing and retaining exceptional student education teachers and professional educators who serve children and adults with special needs. In collaboration with Central Florida partners and CCIE's Toni Jennings Exceptional Education Institute (TJEEI), STE provides families of children with disabilities, UCF faculty and students, and educators with access to current information, resources and learning opportunities. Through teaching and research clinics, UCF faculty and students work to offer students with disabilities and their families services focused on assessment, behavior, reading, mathematics and community counseling. 


The School of Teacher Education is seeking applications for a 9-month, non-tenure earning, visiting instructor or lecturer. The successful candidate will teach four courses in the Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) and Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) program each semester, is expected to lead the ABA and BCBA programs, and provide administrative support for the current ABA accreditation, ABA attestations, and potentially support grant administration. The incumbent will also work with graduate affairs on behalf of STE with course substitutions.


This position is located on the Orlando campus and is anticipated to begin Spring 2027.


Minimum Qualifications:

  • Instructor: A master’s degree in education, psychology, or a related field from an accredited institution; Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) credentials; and a minimum of five years of directly relevant professional experience in applied behavior analysis or a closely related area. All qualifications must be met by the time of hire.
  • Lecturer: A terminal degree (e.g., PhD, EdD) in education, psychology, or a related field from an accredited institution, and Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) credentials. All qualifications must be met by the time of hire.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Doctoral-level Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA-D) credentials
  • PK-20 teaching experience
  • Experience with grant-related work (e.g., administration/writing, implementation, support)

Additional Application Materials Required: 

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following: 

  • A curriculum vitae. 
  • A letter of interest describing qualifications for the position, such as research agenda and teaching experience/interest. 

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later. 


The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials. 

Questions regarding this search should be directed to: Dr. Dan Ezell at Dan.Ezell@ucf.edu, Search Committee Chair.  

Special Instructions to the Applicants: 

All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. H-1B visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H-1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer. 


This is a visiting, 9-month, non-tenure track appointment with benefits, annually renewable for up to four academic years (maximum).

Note to applicants: Please keep in mind that a job posted without an end date may close at any time without notice. As such, we encourage you to submit your application and all required documentation as quickly as possible to ensure consideration for the posted position.

About this job

Senior Licensing Associate in UCF's Technology Transfer Office managing protection and licensing of physical science patents, trademarks, and copyrights. Responsibilities include drafting license agreements, assessing new technologies, promoting innovations at scientific conferences, and supervising IP specialists.

Good fit if you have a bachelor's degree with 4+ years of relevant experience, strong legal agreement drafting skills, and interest in technology commercialization.

Full job description

The Opportunity:

As part of UCF's Technology Transfer Office, the Senior Licensing Associate position manages the transfer of physical science technologies from university into commercial sectors. Manages technology review, intellectual property (IP) legal protection, IP license negotiations, and IP promotion in media and at scientific and technology related events.


Responsibilities:

  • Manages the protection and licensing of a portion of the UCF Research Foundation IP portfolio which includes patents, trademarks and copyrights in the areas of physical sciences. Drafts and negotiates license agreements and other types of agreements, including material transfer, inter-institutional, and nondisclosure agreements.
  • Assesses and evaluates new technologies disclosed to Technology Transfer. Identifies commercial uses and recommends appropriate legal protection and ensures adherence to IP laws and regulations.
  • Reviews and edits promotional materials to advertise new technologies to prospective industry partners. Leads outreach to commercialize technologies and promotes new technologies at scientific conferences and to business communities.
  • Reviews, edits, and negotiates IP terms and conditions for UCF sponsored research activities. Coordinates IP matters between contract manager, general counsel, principal investigator, and external sponsor/external counsel.
  • Attracts and cultivates relationships with university researchers, entrepreneurs and industry partners to drive licensing deal flow and potential sponsored research activity.
  • Supervises, trains, and instructs one or more intellectual property specialist, licensing assistant, students and/or interns.
  • Conducts workshops and delivers presentations to educate internal and external communities on Technology Transfer matters, best practices and IP policies.
  • Attends professional trade conferences.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's or Master's degree and 4+ years of relevant experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in Engineering (e.g., Mechanical, Civil, Electrical) or a related physical science field.
  • 3+ years of demonstrated success in drafting, negotiating, and implementing legal agreements.
  • Strong customer service orientation with experience collaborating with faculty, legal teams, and external partners.
  • Proven business development and finance acumen.
  • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills with the ability to build and maintain strong relationships.
  • Ability to evaluate market potential and effectively communicate with different stakeholders.
  • Familiarity with patent assessment and market research methodologies.
  • Prior experience in technology transfer and outbound software licensing.

We urge you to please take the time to complete the application in its entirety.

Full job description

Financial Affairs:

Financial Affairs partners with our UCF community to continuously improve and deliver outstanding administrative and financial services through innovative business and technological solutions and sound fiscal stewardship.


The Opportunity:

The University of Central Florida's Financial Affairs division is seeking a dynamic and experienced Accounting Manager to lead and oversee its student financial cashiering services, in-person and email customer service units, and management of all campus cash/check collections. In this high-impact role, you will be responsible for directing, developing, and guiding a team while ensuring the successful completion of all tasks, projects, and administrative mandates that advance the department's and university's financial goals. If you are a detail-oriented accounting professional with a passion for operational excellence, compliance, and leadership in a fast-paced university environment, we invite you to bring your expertise to Knight Nation.


Responsibilities:

  • Directs and manages the university's main depository account operations, including high-volume deposits exceeding $600 million annually; provides guidance to personnel on administrative policies and procedures to effectively manage administrative and fiscal operations.
  • Hires, trains, coaches, and evaluates staff direct reports.
  • Directs and manages the preparation of daily, monthly, and annual financial reports and reconciliations across two financial systems — Oracle PeopleSoft and Workday; evaluates and modifies business processes to adapt to these systems.
  • Manages the opening, closing, and operations of university cashiering offices; manages cash, check, and wire deposits and reviews and monitors outstanding deposits to the general ledger; interprets, formulates, and implements operational and UCF policies and procedures.
  • Recommends, creates, and implements long- and short-term strategic plan goals and operational plans; analyzes financial functions and makes recommendations for department controls.
  • Responds to audit reports and ensures the continuous existence of internal controls to safeguard and protect the university's funds and other assets; serves as liaison among functional areas and departments.
  • Interprets and ensures compliance with Florida Statutes, BOG regulations, and UCF policies and regulations; responsible for obtaining and maintaining the required annual certification for Student Account Services with respect to Payment Card Industry (PCI) compliance.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's or Master's degree and 4+ years of relevant experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Advanced degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field.
  • Experience in accounting or financial operations within a higher education or public sector environment.
  • Demonstrated experience managing financial reporting and reconciliations in enterprise financial systems, such as Oracle PeopleSoft or Workday.
  • Experience managing and developing a team of professional staff.
  • Familiarity with Florida Statutes, Board of Governors regulations, and public university financial policies and procedures.
  • Proven ability to develop and implement internal controls, audit responses, and process improvement initiatives.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills with the ability to effectively collaborate across functional areas.
  • Knowledge of Payment Card Industry (PCI) compliance standards and experience maintaining related certifications.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

  • The anticipated salary range for this position is $75,000 to $80,000. The final salary will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.
  • All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.
  • This role requires the successful candidate to work on-site at UCF as their primary work location. On-site presence is an essential function of this role.

The Opportunity:

University Operations is seeking to hire Project Portfolio Managers. This role is responsible for providing leadership, oversight, and strategic direction for a portfolio of capital construction, deferred maintenance, and renewal projects with a total value exceeding $140 million. This position leads a team of project management professionals, manages client relationships, and ensures projects are delivered safely, on time, within budget, and in accordance with university standards and objectives. Serving as the primary point of contact for assigned clients, the Project Portfolio Manager oversees projects throughout the full lifecycle, from planning and design through construction and closeout. This position reports to the Senior Director and/or Assistant Vice President of Planning, Design & Construction.


Responsibilities:

Portfolio Leadership & Team Management

  • Lead and oversee a portfolio of capital construction, renovation, deferred maintenance, and renewal projects.
  • Manage project workload assignments and forecast future resource needs to support portfolio objectives.
  • Provide leadership, mentorship, and performance management for project management staff, including Senior Project Managers.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for portfolio clients and maintain strong stakeholder relationships.
  • Monitor portfolio budgets, schedules, progress, quality, and performance metrics to proactively identify and resolve issues.
  • Ensure compliance with established policies, procedures, standards, and project management practices.

Project Management & Delivery

  • Direct and coordinate all phases of complex construction projects from planning and design through construction and closeout.
  • Manage contractors, architects, engineers, and consultants to ensure successful project execution.
  • Review project scope, plans, specifications, and construction documents to ensure constructability and minimize change orders.
  • Monitor project budgets, schedules, and quality standards to support successful outcomes.
  • Provide technical guidance regarding design and construction challenges and facilitate timely resolution of issues.
  • Conduct site visits and inspections to verify compliance with contract requirements, building codes, safety regulations, and university standards.
  • Support campus sustainability initiatives through new construction and renovation projects.

Contract Administration & Continuous Improvement

  • Assist in the preparation of Requests for Proposals (RFPs), Invitations to Bid (ITBs), and other procurement documents.
  • Provide guidance in the selection of architectural, engineering, and construction service providers.
  • Support reporting and performance tracking for project portfolios and team productivity.
  • Promote continuous improvement through process enhancements, lessons learned, and best practices.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's or Master's degree and 4+ years of relevant experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience managing large-scale capital construction portfolios.
  • Experience supervising and mentoring project management professionals.
  • Knowledge of public-sector or higher education construction practices.
  • Experience working with architects, engineers, contractors, and consulting firms.
  • Strong leadership, stakeholder engagement, and strategic planning skills.
  • Professional certification such as PMP, CCM, or related credential.

The Opportunity:

The Landscape and Natural Resources Department at Facilities and Business Operations is seeking an experienced Arborist III to lead the Tree Care team. This is a hands-on leadership opportunity ideal for an arborist who is passionate about tree care and wants to continue working in the field while taking on greater responsibility. The selected candidate will work alongside crew members, providing technical expertise and leading daily tree care operations that support the health, functionality, and aesthetics of UCF's tree canopy.


As the lead Arborist, you will coordinate and participate in a wide range of arboricultural activities, including tree installation, pruning, removals, root remediation, and disease management, while ensuring work is completed safely, efficiently, and to the highest standards. You will also serve as a secondary point of contact for customers, representing the department through effective communication, problem-solving, and a commitment to exceptional service. Responsibilities may evolve based on organizational needs.


Responsibilities:

  • Lead and supervise the daily operations of the tree crew, ensuring tasks are performed safely, efficiently, and to the highest standards.
  • Tree installation, pruning, removals, stump grinding, root remediation, and disease management.
  • Manage workflow, training, and employee development to maintain optimal performance.
  • Maintain and oversee all tree care equipment, including chipper trucks, brush chippers, chainsaws, pole saws, aerial platforms, stump grinders, root pruners, air spades, and compressors.
  • Ensure tools and machinery are safe, properly maintained, and functioning efficiently.
  • Provide coaching and training on job assignments, standards, and customer service, demonstrating correct procedures and adherence to Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
  • Conduct quality checks to ensure services meet UCF standards and process guidelines.
  • Coordinate and schedule safety and tree care-related training for the team.
  • Ensure compliance with safety standards, address medical needs in case of injury, and document all accidents, injuries, and unsafe conditions.
  • Promote and maintain a strong safety culture within the unit.
  • Review work orders and projects for accuracy, ensuring all timelines and details are met.
  • Act as a resource for technical guidance and problem resolution.
  • Serve as a team leader for vegetative debris removal during natural disasters, such as hurricanes and tropical storms, overseeing the safe and efficient removal of fallen trees, branches, and other vegetation.

Minimum Qualifications:

High school Diploma or Equivalent and 4+ years of relevant experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6). 


Preferred Qualifications:

  • 4+ years of arboricultural experience overseeing tree care projects including pruning, removals, and disease management in an institutional or large-scale setting, such as a university, park system, or municipality.
  • Previous leadership roles overseeing tree care teams or related operations.
  • Experience with advanced tree care techniques, such as cabling, bracing, and lightning protection systems.
  • Proficiency in operating and maintaining specialized tree care equipment, including aerial lifts and root remediation tools.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills for customer interaction, report preparation, and team coordination.
  • Experience implementing safety protocols and conducting safety training sessions.
  • Prior experience coordinating tree care or debris removal efforts during or after natural disasters, including hurricanes or tropical storms.

Job.JobTitle: Instructor or Lecturer, Film - Production Design
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Orlando, FL
  • Benefits: Health insurance, paid time off, paid holidays

About this job

Teach undergraduate and potentially graduate film production design courses at UCF's Nicholson School of Communication and Media. This is a 9-month, annually renewable instructor or lecturer position starting August 2027 with a clear promotion path based on years of service and performance.

Good fit if you have a master's degree in Film Production or related field, professional experience in production design, and proficiency in Adobe Creative Cloud, Unreal, DaVinci Resolve, or similar software.

Full job description

The Opportunity 

The Nicholson School of Communication and Media (NSCM) in the College of Sciences (COS) at the University of Central Florida (UCF) invites applications for an instructor or lecturer position in the Film and Media Production and Management degree areas, anticipated to begin in August 2027. This job is a 9-month, non-tenure earning, annually renewable position that offers a clear career path with the possibility of promotion based on years of service and performance.   


The selected candidate will contribute to the mission of the Film and Mass Media program by teaching undergraduate courses and, depending on the highest degree attained, may teach at the graduate level and support the Film MFA degree by providing critiques, mentoring, and serving on graduate thesis committees. The successful candidate may be expected to teach in different modalities including face-to-face and online. The instructional duties and service assignments are in accordance with the department’s equitable workload policy. 


Other typical responsibilities include providing appropriate service in student advising (academic and career) and actively participating in the academic life of the school. This includes attending faculty meetings, graduations, assessing student learning, and engaging in committee work. These activities are integral to our commitment to student success and academic excellence.   


This position has no research expectation, but research and scholarly activities may be supported. 


Additionally, we are especially interested in a candidate who can contribute through their teaching and service to the excellence of our academic community and foster an environment in which faculty, staff, and students from a variety of backgrounds, cultures, and personal experiences are welcomed and can thrive. 


The UCF Nicholson School of Communication and Media (NSCM) is a student-centered experience at the exciting intersection of technology, media, film, advertising, communications and public relations. Our faculty and staff bring an impressive background of experience—from developing health communication to producing Super Bowl commercials—and connect our students to internship and career opportunities. As the premier academic program for communications and media in Central Florida with successful alumni around the globe, NSCM is known for excellence in research, teaching, and service to students and the community. The curriculum blends both the theoretical and applied aspects of the field, offering eight bachelor’s degree programs, four master’s degree programs, and a Ph.D. program in strategic communication. For more information about the school, visit https://communication.ucf.edu. 


The UCF College of Sciences (COS) is the largest college at the university and a powerhouse for the regional and national STEM workforce, spanning the natural, computational, physical, and social sciences and housing centers, institutes and initiatives that serve as hubs for research and innovation. Through sharing and applying knowledge, COS is cultivating pathways for students to solve our world’s most pressing and complex problems. With a mission to provide a world-class education in an environment where faculty, staff, and students thrive, research flourishes, and our community prospers; a number of COS academic programs are among those nationally ranked by U.S. News and World Report, Princeton Review, and others. For more information, please visit https://sciences.ucf.edu. 


UCF, named one of the most innovative public universities in the nation by U.S. News & World Report, is located in Orlando, Florida and is classified as a Very High Research Activity university by the Carnegie Foundation. With more than 70,000 students, UCF is one of the largest universities in the country, offering more than 240 degree programs. UCF is an economic engine, attracting and supporting industries vital to the region's future while providing students with real-world experiences that help them succeed after graduation. For more information, visit http://www.ucf.edu. 


Minimum Qualifications: 

  • A master’s degree (for an instructor) or a terminal degree (for a lecturer) in Film Production, or a related field (e.g., Production Design, Film Arts, Technical Arts, Digital Media, Mass Communication, etc.) from an accredited institution at the time of hire. Applicants with a bachelor’s degree as their highest degree will be considered an instructor applicant only if they can document a minimum of seven years of professional experience in production design in film and/or television production. 
  • Must have excellent communication and organizational skills and the ability to work effectively in a collaborative educational environment with faculty, students, and administrators.
  • Proficiency in production design software such as Abode Creative Cloud, Unreal, DaVinci Resolve, Toon Boom Story Board Pro or relevant software.  

Preferred Qualifications: 

  • Professional Experience (five years or more) of production design, directing, cinematography, editing or relevant disciplines in film and/or television.
  • Professional experience in production design workflows and techniques.
  • At least one year of college-level teaching experience in a relevant discipline.
  • Experience working in virtual production and/or visual effects technologies.
  • Experience teaching in different modalities including face-to-face and online. 

Additional Application Materials Required: 

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following: 

  • A letter of application (cover letter) indicating how you are prepared to join the faculty at UCF. 
  • A curriculum vitae (CV). 
  • A teaching statement of no more than 300 words that addresses the ability to teach using different delivery modes, including online or large classes.

About this job

Two 9-month non-tenure lecturer positions in Counselor Education at UCF's Orlando campus, starting Fall 2027. Responsibilities include teaching graduate courses, advising students, and supervising practicum and internship students in a highly-ranked CACREP-accredited program.

Good fit if you have a terminal degree in Counselor Education or related field and experience in graduate teaching and clinical supervision.

Full job description

The Opportunity

The Department of Counselor Education and School Psychology in the College of Community Innovation and Education (CCIE) at the University of Central Florida (UCF) is seeking applications for two (2) 9-month, non-tenure earning lecturer positions in the Counselor Education Program, anticipated to begin Fall 2027. This position is located on the Orlando campus and summer teaching may be available.


The selected candidate will contribute to the Counselor Education Program’s mission by teaching a variety of graduate level courses, advising students, and supervising practicum and internship students. The ideal candidate will be a dynamic individual with strong teaching, supervision, and interpersonal skills.


The Counselor Education program has been ranked among top-level Counselor Education programs in the country by U.S. News & World Report since 2007. The Counselor Education program offers the following degrees: (a) master’s degrees in Clinical Mental Health Counseling (M.A.), Marriage, Couple, and Family Therapy (M.A.), and School Counseling (M.A., M.Ed.); (b) Educational Specialist Degree in School Counseling (Ed.S.); and (c) a doctoral degree (Ph.D.) in Education—Counselor Education and Supervision. The Clinical Mental Health Counseling (M.A.); Marriage, Couple, and Family Therapy (M.A.); School Counseling (M.A., M.Ed.); and Counselor Education and Supervision (Ph.D.) programs are accredited by CACREP. For additional Counselor Education Program information, visit https://ccie.ucf.edu/cesp/counselored/. For more information about the department, please visit the homepage at: https://ccie.ucf.edu/cesp/


The UCF College of Community Innovation and Education (CCIE) is a one-of-a-kind academic unit with distinct, interdisciplinary expertise and potential for partnership with community stakeholders, conceived to address societal challenges and work alongside the community. Established in 2018, the college offers undergraduate and graduate programs on the main campus and UCF Downtown. At the heart of the college's mission is the institutional commitment to transform lives and strengthen society by developing a unified vision and innovative solutions to complex social issues. CCIE promotes innovation through state-of-the-art interdisciplinary research with social impact, contemporary inclusive teaching and learning practices, and preeminent service for the disciplines, the institution, and the community.


Minimum Qualifications:

  • Terminal degree in Counselor Education or a closely related field from an accredited institution, required by the time of hire.
  • Demonstrated potential for excellence in teaching, service, and leadership.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Earned doctoral degree from a CACREP-accredited program.
  • Experience in graduate teaching and clinical supervision.

The postdoctoral scholar with support a DARPA project focused on developing predictive pressure load models for external hypersonics aerodynamics. About this job

Conduct complex investigations of financial fraud, waste, abuse, and employee misconduct at UCF. Independently manage cases from complaint assessment through evidence analysis and final reporting while promoting accountability and safeguarding university resources.

Good fit if you have 4+ years of fraud investigation or related experience, can obtain CFE certification within one year, and are authorized to work in the U.S.

Full job description

University Audit:

UCF University Audit serves as the university’s internal auditor, providing internal audits and reviews, management consulting and advisory services, investigations of fraud, waste, or abuse, follow-up on recommendations, evaluation of the processes of risk management and governance, and coordination with external auditors.

UCF University Audit reports administratively to the Office of the President and functionally to the Audit and Compliance Committee of the Board of Trustees. This reporting structure promotes independence and full consideration of audit recommendations and management action plans.

 

The Opportunity:

UCF University Audit is seeking an Audit Investigator III to conduct complex and sensitive investigations involving financial fraud, waste, abuse, employee misconduct, and violations of laws, regulations, rules, and university policies. This position independently manages investigations from initial complaint assessment and planning through evidence analysis, documentation, findings, and final reporting while helping promote accountability and safeguard university resources.

The ideal candidate will bring experience in financial fraud investigations, accounting, auditing, forensic accounting, compliance, law enforcement, or a related investigative field. The successful candidate will demonstrate strong analytical and investigative writing skills, discretion in handling sensitive information, and the ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with university stakeholders.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Lead complex and sensitive investigations involving alleged fraud, waste, abuse, employee misconduct, and violations of applicable laws, regulations, rules, and university policies.
  • Independently manage investigations from initial planning through interviews, evidence collection and analysis, documentation, findings, and final reporting.
  • Manage the intake and triage of complaints by assessing jurisdiction, investigative needs, risk, urgency, and the appropriate course of action.
  • Evaluate the potential applicability of the Florida Whistle-blower Act and coordinate with university stakeholders to support appropriate and consistent complaint resolution.
  • Prepare comprehensive investigative reports, workpapers, findings, and related correspondence in accordance with university procedures and professional standards.
  • Assist with reviewing investigative workpapers, managing assignments, and providing backup support to the investigations manager or associate director, as needed.
  • Maintain regular communication with team members and leadership regarding investigative progress, significant developments, and case resolution.
  • Support fraud awareness and prevention initiatives such as the UCF Fraud Risk Assessment Committee, guide University Audit interns, and participate in audits or consulting projects, as needed.
  • Other duties as assigned. 

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s Degree and 4+ years of experience or an equivalent combination of related education and experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).
  • Must obtain Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE) designation within one year of hire. 

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience conducting complex financial fraud, compliance, employee misconduct, or fraud, waste, and abuse investigations.
  • Experience applying accounting, auditing, forensic accounting, or financial analysis principles in an investigative environment.
  • Experience independently managing investigations from complaint assessment through findings and final reporting, including preparing investigative reports and professional correspondence.
  • Experience in preparing for, conducting, and documenting sensitive interviews and communicating with stakeholders at multiple organizational levels.
  • Experience using data analytics, case-management systems, audit software, or emerging technologies to support investigative work.
  • Experience working in higher education, government, the public sector, internal audit, corporate compliance, or another regulated environment.
  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, business administration, criminal justice, or a closely related field. 

 

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

  • The anticipated salary range for this position is $87,500-Negotiable. The final salary will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.
  • All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.
  • This role requires the successful candidate to work on-site at UCF as their primary work location. On-site presence is an essential function of this role.

Job.JobTitle: Professor and Director, School of Communication Sciences and Disorders
Job.JobDescription:
The Opportunity

The School of Communication Sciences and Disorders (CSD) at the University of Central Florida (UCF) invites applications for a 12-month, tenured professor to serve as school director. The position is located at the UCF main campus with an anticipated start date in August 2027.


The successful candidate will assume leadership of a school with a growing team of internationally recognized faculty engaged in rigorous graduate and undergraduate education, expansive clinical service-delivery, cutting-edge research, and innovative partnerships. Opportunities for innovation and expansion abound in the interprofessional context of the College of Health Professions and Sciences within UCF’s Academic Health Sciences Center. The selected candidate will provide academic and administrative leadership (i.e., management of human resources, implementation of a new budget model, academic and clinical programming, student success and research excellence); facilitate intra- and inter- school collaborations to enhance the impact of scholarship, teaching, and service; support and mentor faculty to secure external funding; and advance impactful programming to fulfill the healthcare needs of the community.


The School of Communication Sciences and Disorders was founded in 1969 and was first accredited in 1987. It has a strong history of excellence in teaching, research, and community service. The school includes 34 full-time faculty members serving an average of 175 graduate and 500 undergraduate students. It offers bachelor’s, master’s, and Ph.D. degrees in communication sciences and disorders and ranks among the top 15% of speech-language pathology programs in the nation. The Master of Arts program boasts numerous internal and external affiliations, and the UCF Communication Disorders Clinic serves as the centerpiece for clinical education and applied research. This 15,000+ square foot state-of-the-art facility houses several research labs and specialty services, including audiology, the Aphasia House, the AAC Lab / Florida Alliance for Assistive Services and Technology (FAAST) Center, the Communication Technologies Research Collaborative, the Communication, Aphasia Recovery, and Emotion (CARE) Lab, Early Language & Literacy Intervention & Education Lab, Examining Patient-Provider Language and Interactions in Healthcare (EXPLAIN) Lab.  For more information about the school, visit our website at:  UCF School of Communication Sciences and Disorders - College of Health Professions and Sciences


Along with the School of Communication Sciences and Disorders, the College of Health Professions and Sciences at UCF is home to the School of Health Sciences, the School of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Sciences, the School of Global Health Management and Informatics, and the School of Social Work. The college also houses several labs and research collaboratives, including the CHPS Rehabilitation Innovation Center – a state-of-the art interdisciplinary facility designed to become a destination center for solving complex healthcare problems through allied healthcare research, education, technology development/applications, and collaboration. UCF and its 12 colleges provide opportunities to more than 69,000 students offering 240+ bachelor's, master's, doctoral, and specialist degree programs.


Minimum Qualifications:

  • A research doctoral degree in communication sciences and disorders or a related discipline from an accredited institution;
  • To be eligible for appointment as a tenured professor upon hire, the selected candidate must have a record of teaching, research/scholarly achievements, and service commensurate with a tenured faculty appointment at the rank of professor in the School of Communication Sciences and Disorders at UCF;
  • A record of administrative leadership and mentoring in a university setting.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Effective communication skills;
  • Experience overseeing complex budgets;
  • Experience with program accreditation;
  • Experience with student recruitment for undergraduate and graduate programs;
  • A record of federally funded research & mentoring faculty in securing external funding;
  • Experience with interprofessional education;
  • A record of facilitating successful collaborations within and outside the university setting;
  • Experience with alumni engagement; and
  • Experience with curriculum revisions and launching new educational programs.

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following:

  • A curriculum vitae.
  • A letter of interest describing qualifications for the position, such as research agenda and teaching experience/interest.

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.

About this job

Leads engineering and maintenance of broadcast and instructional media systems for the Nicholson School of Communication and Media. Manages IP-based transmission hardware, streaming devices, recording systems, and production equipment while serving as subject matter expert for all engineering operations.

Good fit if you have a bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in broadcast or studio engineering and 4+ years working with professional broadcast systems.

Full job description

The Opportunity:

The Broadcast Engineer I leads the engineering, maintenance, and development of all broadcast and instructional media systems within the Nicholson School of Communication and Media (NSCM). This position is responsible for broadcast information technology including IP digital transmission hardware, internet streaming devices, IP based hardware/software for audio/video recording and playout systems, non-linear editors, production switchers, encoders, decoders, power infrastructure, UPS systems, and automation systems. The Broadcast Engineer I independently manages the lifecycle of technical systems and infrastructure, ensuring optimal functionality, modernization, and compliance with industry standards. This position serves as the subject matter expert and primary point of contact for all engineering operations related to NSCM’s media production environments.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Maintain and repair all IP-based broadcast and AV systems, including IP based digital transmission/transmitter systems, internet streaming devices, digital IP audio/video record and playout systems, production switchers, routing switchers, encoders, decoders, automation and server/file storage systems, digital editing systems, field production gear, and broadcast related hardware.
  • Serve as the lead engineer for NSCM’s live and recorded productions, providing expert technical support and supervision during instructional and professional media projects. Take full ownership of system configuration, monitoring, and troubleshooting across camera, lighting, audio, transmission, and control room operations.
  • Develop, implement, and manage technical upgrade initiatives and infrastructure enhancements across all production and instructional spaces. Design detailed signal flow documentation and engineering schematics to guide installations, expansions, and workflow optimization. Provide specific IP signal flow diagrams for CAD/Visio documentation on all work performed on technical systems.
  • Independently schedule and execute preventive maintenance plans. Conduct detailed system diagnostics and repairs at the component level to ensure consistent system performance and reliability.
  • Lead technology forecasting and procurement strategies by researching emerging trends and evaluating new tools and platforms. Maintain comprehensive inventory and asset management systems to support operational continuity.
  • Administer and enhance equipment checkout systems and shared storage environments. Train, lead, and mentor student workers and technical support staff to uphold service excellence and technical reliability.
  • Partner with the NSCM Manager of Main Campus Operations to shape long-term capital and operational budgets. About this job

UCF College of Medicine seeks a psychiatrist to teach medical students and residents in psychiatry, psychopharmacology, and medical interviewing while providing outpatient psychiatric care at UCF Health Faculty Practice. This non-tenure track role emphasizes undergraduate and graduate medical education with significant clinical responsibilities.

Good fit if you have an M.D./D.O., are board certified or eligible in psychiatry and neurology, and have experience teaching medical students or residents.

Full job description

The Opportunity

The University of Central Florida College of Medicine (UCF COM) is seeking an experienced psychiatrist at the rank of assistant, associate, or professor of medicine to have a significant teaching role in undergraduate medical education (UME), graduate medical education (GME), and provide direct, outpatient psychiatric care at UCF Health Faculty Practice. This position is a non-tenure track appointment.


College of Medicine Educational Programs (60-70%)

The successful applicant will teach psychopathology, psychopharmacology, and fundamentals of medical interviewing in an integrated format to first- and second-year medical students and participate in case directed learning sessions. This position will serve as the discipline lead for the Integrated Sciences 4 module, which focuses on pre-clinical psychiatry and neurology. Additionally, teaching psychiatry didactics in the 3rd year clerkship, assisting with mid-clerkship evaluations, and teaching and mentorship in the psychiatry residency program will be required.  Collaborations with both basic science and clinical faculty to integrate and reinforce psychiatry concepts throughout the M.D. program curriculum is an essential element of this role.  All faculty are expected to pursue scholarly activities to fulfill the criteria for academic advancement. General and specialty-trained psychiatrists with an interest in medical education are encouraged to apply.

The College of Medicine aspires to become an extraordinary research-based institution training physicians of the future who will become exemplary clinicians, leaders in medicine, scholars in science, innovators in medical technology and compassionate providers of health care. 


Clinical Responsibilities (30-40%)

Psychiatric medical care will be provided at UCF Health Faculty Practice, an expanding adult outpatient multi-specialty clinic.  The successful candidate will provide care in a team that embraces other health care disciplines and involves collaborating with physicians and advanced practice practitioners from a variety of specialties including Primary Care, Rheumatology, Endocrinology, Dermatology, Cardiology, and Ophthalmology.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Candidates must hold an M.D./D.O. from an accredited institution. Candidates must be eligible for licensure or licensed to practice in the state of Florida. Must be board certified or board eligible by the American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology upon completion of training. Board certification would be expected within two (2) years of completion of training.
  • The candidate’s scholarly background and experience must be commensurate with the faculty rank for which the application is submitted.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience teaching medical students and/or residents in an LCME/ACGME accredited program.
  • Commitment to student-centered, active learning in a multidisciplinary environment that integrates basic sciences with clinical application.
  • Proficiency with instructional technology and digital platforms.
  • Track record of scholarly activity.

Additional Application Materials Required: 

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following: 

  • A curriculum vitae. 
  • A letter of interest describing qualifications for the position, such as research agenda and teaching experience/interest. 

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later. 

The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials. 


Questions regarding this search should be directed to: Brittany Hofmann at Brittany.hofmann@ucf.edu.

About this job

Postdoctoral position developing computational methods for analyzing laryngeal videoendoscopy recordings using computer vision and machine learning. Work on NIH-funded research at the intersection of engineering, clinical science, and AI, with opportunities to mentor students and publish in leading journals.

Good fit if you have a PhD in biomedical engineering, computer science, or related field, with experience in deep learning, computer vision, and Python or MATLAB.

Full job description

The Opportunity:

The Voice and Speech Informatics (VSI) Lab in The School of Communication Sciences and Disorders at the University of Central Florida is seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Research Associate with a strong engineering and computational background. This position is located at the UCF Main campus in Orlando, Florida, with an anticipated start date April 2027.


The postdoctoral scholar will work primarily on the development and application of computational methods for the analysis of high-speed laryngeal videoendoscopy recordings, with additional opportunities to contribute to projects involving acoustic, physiological, and wearable-sensor data. Research activities will involve computer vision, machine learning, deep learning, and multimodal data analysis. This is an exciting opportunity to work at the intersection of engineering, clinical science, and AI, contributing to NIH-funded research on vocal fold physiology and laryngeal imaging. The successful candidate will join a collaborative and interdisciplinary research environment with opportunities to develop novel computational methods, publish in leading journals, mentor student researchers, and contribute to ongoing NIH-funded projects.


The Voice and Speech Informatics (VSI) Lab develops computational methods that combine machine learning, computer vision, signal processing, and multimodal data analysis to study voice production, vocal physiology, and vocal health. We analyze laryngeal imaging, aerodynamic, electroglottographic, acoustic, physiological, and ambulatory monitoring data to address fundamental and translational questions related to voice function and disorders. The lab conducts NIH-funded research and collaborates closely with investigators across the Communication Technologies Research Collaborative (CTRC), providing access to diverse datasets, advanced instrumentation, and high-performance computing resources. The VSI lab and CTRC offer a highly interdisciplinary research environment at the intersection of engineering, artificial intelligence, and clinical science.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and evaluate computer vision, machine learning, and deep learning approaches for the analysis of laryngeal images and related biomedical data.
  • Analyze and integrate multimodal datasets, including laryngeal imaging, acoustic, aerodynamic, electroglottographic, physiological, and ambulatory monitoring data.
  • Prepare manuscripts for publication in peer-reviewed journals and present research findings at scientific conferences.
  • Mentor graduate and undergraduate researchers within the lab.
  • Contribute to collaborative research activities, including the development of grant proposals and new research initiatives.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • PhD in Biomedical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field
  • Proficiency in Python and/or MATLAB
  • Experience with deep learning, including PyTorch and/or TensorFlow
  • Experience developing, training, and evaluating computer vision and image segmentation models
  • Strong foundations in image processing and machine learning

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with video analysis, motion tracking, or object tracking.
  • Experience with medical image analysis
  • Experience with time‑series analysis
  • Experience with speech, voice, or acoustic signal processing
  • Experience with scientific software development, version control, and reproducible research practices.

Additional Application Materials Required:

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following:

  • Curriculum vitae.
  • Brief statement (approximately 2 pages) describing the applicant's research interests, relevant experience, career goals, and potential research directions related to machine learning, computer vision, and multimodal analysis of high-speed videoendoscopy (HSV) and other voice-related datasets.
  • Up to two representative publications or preprints that best demonstrate the applicant's expertise and potential to contribute to research in computer vision, machine learning, medical image analysis, and multimodal data analysis.

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.


The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.


 Questions regarding this search should be directed to: Dr. Hamzeh Ghasemzadeh, hamzeh.ghasemzadeh@ucf.edu

All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. H-1B visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H-1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.


Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled.

The Opportunity

The Department of Chemistry (science.ucf.edu/chemistry) and the National Center for Forensic Science (NCFS, www.ncfs.ucf.edu) at the University of Central Florida (UCF) invite applications for one full-time, 9-month, tenure-earning Assistant Professor in Forensic Toxicology. This is a joint position between the Chemistry Department and NCFS. This position is anticipated to begin in August 2027. Candidates hired at the assistant professor level are expected to develop externally funded, nationally competitive research programs. State-of-the art laboratory space and a competitive startup package can be expected. Successful candidates will contribute to teaching in both the undergraduate and graduate programs. The instructional duties and service assignments are in accordance with the department’s current equitable workload policy.

The Department of Chemistry at UCF is fueling the STEM workforce of the future, preparing students through five broad areas of study, including: materials, biochemistry, environmental chemistry, forensic chemistry, and chemistry education research. Our faculty are actively engaged in cutting-edge, interdisciplinary research in collaboration with the National Center of Forensic Science, the Nanoscience and Technology Center, the College of Optics and Photonics, the College of Engineering and Computer Science, and the College of Community Innovation and Education. The department offers a range of academic programs, which include both B.A. and B.S. degrees in Chemistry and a B.S. in Forensic Science, as well as M.S. programs in Chemistry and Forensic Science, and a Ph.D. in Chemistry. Our B.S. Forensic Science degree is accredited by the Forensic Science Education Programs Accreditation Commission (FEPAC) and UCF is a member of The Consortium for Nuclear Forensics, one of only 16 universities in the nation. The National Center for Forensic Science at UCF, a State of Florida Type II Research Center, leverages the expertise of Chemistry faculty to provide relevant and responsive forensic science research and training and operational support to communities that rely on science to achieve justice.

The UCF College of Sciences (COS) is the largest college at the university and a powerhouse for the regional and national STEM workforce, spanning the natural, computational, and social sciences with centers, institutes, and initiatives that serve as hubs for research and innovation. Through sharing and applying knowledge, COS is cultivating pathways for students to solve our world’s most pressing and complex problems. The mission of COS is to provide a world-class education in an environment where faculty, staff, and students thrive, research flourishes, and our community prospers. Several COS academic programs are nationally ranked by U.S. News and World Report, Princeton Review, and others.

Job.JobDescription:
The Opportunity

The School of Global Health Management and Informatics (SGHMI) in the College of Health Profession and Sciences (CHPS) at the Univiersity of Central Florida (UCF) invites applications for a 9-month, tenure-earning assistant professor or tenured associate professor for the Health Care Informatics programs. This positions is located at the UCF Downtown campus with an anticipated start date in August 2027. The successful candidate will perform research and teach face to face and full online undergraduate and graduate courses in the area of healthcare informatics, specifically related to artificial intelligence. UCF has world renowned infrastructure and support for online teaching.


The ideal candidate will have extensive experience in cutting edge AI technologies and their applications in healthcare. Candidates with a strong record of interdisciplinary scholarship and external grant funding for research are highly desirable.
 

They will join UCF’s School of Global Health Management and Informatics (SGHMI), home to some of the nation’s largest undergraduate and graduate programs in health services administration. The School offers a comprehensive portfolio of academic programs, including the Bachelor of Science in Health Services Administration (B.S. HSA), Master of Health Administration (MHA), Executive Master of Health Administration (eMHA), Master of Science in Healthcare Informatics (M.S. HCI), Bachelor of Science in Health Informatics and Information Management (B.S. HIIM), and the recently launched Bachelor of Science in Health Informatics (B.S. HI). Further expanding its academic offerings, SGHMI anticipates welcoming its first cohort of Master of Public Health (MPH) students in Fall 2027, creating additional opportunities for interdisciplinary education, research, and collaboration.

SGHMI is committed to academic excellence, with programs accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Healthcare Management Education (CAHME) and the Commission on Accreditation for Health Informatics and Information Management Education (CAHIIM). The undergraduate Health Services Administration program is also certified by the Association of University Programs in Health Administration (AUPHA).

For more information about the school, visit https://healthprofessions.ucf.edu/hmi/.


Minimum Qualifications for Assistant Professor:

  • Doctoral degree in a health discipline e.g., health care informatics, biostatistics, public health, or health services research) or an information technology discipline (e.g., management information systems, applied science, computer science, computer engineering, or biomedical engineering) from an accredited institution.
  • Industry or academic experience in research related to artificial intelligence applications in health care by the start of the appointment.
  • ABD's will be considered if the degree is conferred before the date of hire.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop a research agenda that supports tenure and promotion, along with the potential to secure external funding.

Minimum Qualifications for Associate Professor:

  • Doctoral degree in a health discipline e.g., health care informatics, biostatistics, public health, or health services research) or an information technology discipline (e.g., management information systems, applied science, computer science, computer engineering, or biomedical engineering) from an accredited institution at the time of application.
  • Industry or academic experience in research related to artificial intelligence applications in health care by the start of the appointment.
  • To be eligible for appointment as a tenured associate professor upon hire, the selected candidate must have a demonstrated record of teaching, externally funded projects/research, and service commensurate with a tenured faculty appointment rank of associate professor.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Early, mid-stage, or established investigators with expertise in artificial intelligence application in health care provision, including large language models, biomedical data processing, and data analysis.
  • Strong background in health informatics, digital health, and emerging healthcare technologies, including clinical decision support, health data interoperability, Internet of Things (IoT), wearable technologies, and other innovative technologies applicable to healthcare delivery and population health.
  • Expertise in responsible and trustworthy AI, including explainable AI, algorithmic fairness and bias, privacy, security, model validation, AI governance in healthcare, and AI interoperability, is desirable.
  • Demonstrated success in publishing high-quality research articles in top-tier international and national refereed journals or those who have completed a post-doc with an associated record of publication in the preferred research areas.
  • Actively engaged with various health informatics societies such as AMIA and HIMSS.
  • Demonstrated experience collaborating with healthcare providers, health systems, government agencies, industry partners, or other healthcare organizations on interdisciplinary research, implementary, or externally funded projects is preferred.

A Post Doctoral Scholar position available under the direction of Professor Saiful Khondaker at the University of Central Florida (UCF). In partnership with University of Washington, Khondaker leads PREM Center for quantum materials innovation and education excellence (CQMIEE) at UCF (https://prem2.cecs.ucf.edu/). Khondaker group’s current interest is in the discovery of exotic electronic and vibrational properties of 2D and quantum materials through Raman, TERS, electron transport, and SPM measurements.


The ideal candidate must have a Ph.D. in physics, electrical engineering or related field with demonstrated skills in one or more of the following areas:

(i) Fabrication of 2D materials based nanodevices using exfoliation, transfer, optical and electrical beam lithography (EBL) along with low noise electrical transport measurements (room temperature and low temperature). Strong command of EBL is required

(ii) Investigation of novel physics using Raman spectroscopy, tip-enhance Raman spectroscopy (TERS), Conducting AFM, and other related scanning probe microscopy (SPM) techniques.


In addition, candidates should have

• Strong publication record in high-quality journals with several first author papers, demonstrating an ability to effectively and efficiently report scientific results.

• Excellent written and oral communication skills.

• Creative, hardworking, and self-motivated with the ability and interest to pursue challenging problems independently as well as collaboratively with other groups.


Major Duties/Responsibilities:

• Lead and contribute to independent and collaborative research projects involving synthesis (exfoliation and transfer), device fabrication, and investigation of electronic, vibrational and other exotic properties of 2D/quantum materials.

• Lead the writing of research articles resulting from the work and publish those is scientific journals.

• Present research results at scientific conferences.

• Work with graduate and undergraduate students and provide peer mentoring. Co-lead project with students.

• Collaborate with researchers at UCF and CQMIEE

• Help maintain lab space and equipment’s

• Work safely and independently within a supportive group setting.

• Ensure compliance with environment, safety, health program requirements.


The position is for up to two (2) years with a salary of $57,000/yr along with other benefits.


To be considered for this position please send:

(a) curriculum vitae with publication list.

(b) summary of research accomplishments (2 page limit).

(c) a brief statement of research interests (2 page limit).


All application materials must be sent as one collated PDF document by email to Prof. Saiful Khondaker (saiful@ucf.edu).

The Opportunity

The Psychology Department at the University of Central Florida (UCF) invites applications for up to two (2) nine-month, non-tenure earning Lecturer positions. These annually renewable positions offer a clear career path with the possibility of promotion based on years of service and performance.

The first position will support our Psychology B.S. program. This position is located on the university’s main Orlando campus. Duties will include teaching a 4/4 load of large face-to-face, hybrid, and online courses (ranging between 75 and 400 students) and service in support of the program and department.

The second position will support both the Psychology B.S. program and Clinical Psychology M.A. program. The position is located on the university’s main Orlando campus. Duties will include teaching a 4/4 load of face-to-face, hybrid, and online courses at the undergraduate level. Face-to-face courses in support of the graduate program are taught at the Sanford/Lake Mary campus located approximately 30 minutes from the Orlando campus. Service is expected in support of both programs and the department. The instructional duties and service assignments are in accordance with the department’s current equitable workload policy.

The Psychology Department emphasizes breadth of psychology education while allowing students to pursue one of six specialized tracks: Clinical Psychology, Industrial Organizational Psychology, Human Factors, Experimental Psychology, Neuroscience, and General. Psychology is one of the most popular majors at UCF with over 4,000 undergraduate majors and 150+ graduate students. At the same time, we emphasize critical thinking, strong written and oral communication skills, and professional development. This is accomplished by offering career readiness, research opportunities, and high impact learning experiences such as honors theses, undergraduate teaching assistant internships, service learning, and study abroad. The Psychology B.S. degree is offered as a face-to-face, hybrid, and fully online program. The Online Bachelor’s Program was rated 3rd best in the country in the U.S. News and World Report’s 2026 rankings.

The Master of Arts Clinical Psychology Program, ranked the 2nd best in the country by Psychology.org in 2025, is a terminal master’s program offered at the UCF Sanford/Lake Mary campus. The program consists of two tracks:


Applied Pre-Licensure/Non-Thesis Track: The Applied Pre-Licensure/Non-Thesis Track is designed for students interested in delivering clinical services in a variety of settings including community agencies and private practice. After completing the program and after two years of postgraduate supervised clinical experience, graduates are eligible to become Licensed Mental Health Counselors (LMHCs) in the state of Florida. The Applied Pre-Licensure/Non-Thesis Track is accredited by the Masters in Psychology and Counseling Accreditation Council (MPCAC).

Research/Thesis Track: The Research/Thesis Track is designed for students who wish to focus on clinical research and/or are interested in pursuing entry into a doctoral program following the completion of their master’s degree. Students who complete this option are not eligible to become Licensed Mental Health Counselors upon graduation.

UCF is an economic engine, attracting and supporting industries vital to the region’s future while providing students with real-world experiences that help them succeed after graduation. For the first position, preference will be given to candidates who:

  • have demonstrated experience in successful undergraduate teaching of research and statistical methods, experimental psychology courses (e.g., social, development, cognition, physiological), and/or human-factors/engineering psychology,
  • have demonstrated experience in teaching online and face-to-face modalities,

Job.JobTitle: Assistant Scientist, Associate Scientist, Scientist in Large Nonlinear Computational Dynamical Systems, College of Optics and Photonics
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Orlando, FL
  • Benefits: Health insurance, paid time off, paid holidays

About this job

Conduct computational research on nonlinear dynamics and numerical modeling of semiconductor laser arrays at CREOL. Develop efficient numerical methods for large-scale simulations of coupled delay-differential equations and optimize computational approaches for complex laser networks.

Good fit if you have a Ph.D. in applied mathematics, computational science, physics, or related field, with experience in numerical methods, high-performance computing, or scientific programming.

Full job description

The Opportunity

The University of Central Florida (UCF) is looking for a 12-month, non-tenure earning assistant scientist, associate scientist, or scientist, to conduct research in the College of Optics and Photonics. This position is located at the UCF main campus with an anticipated start date in Spring 2027. UCF is undergoing rapid growth in the size of external research funding, academic stature, and student and faculty groups. UCF supports and benefits from economic growth in Central Florida, which is emerging as a major hub for technology development. The University is located in the metropolitan Orlando area, which offers a vibrant lifestyle and a variety of cultural and recreational activities.


CREOL (Center for Research and Education in Optics and Lasers) is one of the world’s foremost institutions for research and education in optical and photonic science and engineering. The College offers MS and PhD degrees in optics and photonics, and a BS degree in photonic science and engineering. The faculty engages in fundamental and applied research and education in lasers, optical fibers, semiconductor and integrated photonic devices, nonlinear and quantum optics, imaging, sensing, and displays. The college is home to the CREOL, Florida Photonics Center of Excellence (FPCE), and Townes Laser Institute (TLI), and the Institute for the Frontier of Attosecond Science and Technology (iFAST). In addition, the College of Medicine, which includes the Burnett School of Biomedical Sciences, provides rich opportunities for collaboration. For more information see www.creol.ucf.edu.

Applications are invited for a position in computational nonlinear dynamics and large-scale numerical modeling of semiconductor laser arrays at the College of Optics and Photonics (CREOL), University of Central Florida. Our research program investigates collective dynamics, synchronization, and self-organization in large arrays of coupled semiconductor diode lasers. The work combines experiments with computational and theoretical modeling of nonlinear dynamical systems with time-delayed interactions.


A major objective of this position is to develop and implement efficient numerical methods for increasingly large and complex systems of coupled nonlinear delay-differential equations (DDEs). Models range from arrays of single-mode semiconductor lasers described by Lang–Kobayashi-type equations to substantially larger multimode systems incorporating multiple optical modes, carrier dynamics, nonlinear interactions, heterogeneity, and delayed nonlocal coupling. As the number of lasers and optical modes increases, direct numerical simulation becomes computationally demanding. The successful candidate will therefore focus not only on physical modeling but also on developing, optimizing, and accelerating computational approaches capable of treating large laser networks efficiently.


The research scientist will contribute to several areas, including:

  • Numerical integration of large systems of nonlinear delay-differential equations
  • Modeling of single-mode and multimode semiconductor laser arrays
  • Optimization and acceleration of existing simulation codes
  • Parallel computing and high-performance computing (HPC)
  • GPU acceleration, where appropriate
  • Development of scalable numerical algorithms for systems containing large numbers of lasers and optical modes

An important component of the project will be determining how numerical algorithms and existing stimulation codes can be redesigned or optimized to achieve substantial improvements in computational speed while preserving numerical accuracy and stability. The position provides an opportunity to work at the intersection of computational mathematics, nonlinear dynamics, high-performance computing, and experimental photonics. The research is closely connected with ongoing experiments involving large semiconductor diode laser arrays. This interaction provides an unusual opportunity for computational researchers to test theoretical and numerical predictions against experimentally observed collective dynamics. This position allows for opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration involving researchers in optics, photonics, nonlinear dynamics, applied mathematics, and computational science.


Semiconductor-laser experience is not required. The successful candidate will work closely with experimental researchers, and the necessary background in semiconductor laser physics and external-cavity laser systems can be developed as part of the project.


Minimum Qualifications:
