Job.JobDescription:
The Opportunity

The University of Central Florida (UCF) is looking for a 12-month, non-tenure earning assistant scientist, associate scientist, or scientist, to conduct research in the College of Optics and Photonics. This position is located at the UCF main campus with an anticipated start date in Spring 2027. UCF is undergoing rapid growth in the size of external research funding, academic stature, and student and faculty groups. UCF supports and benefits from economic growth in Central Florida, which is emerging as a major hub for technology development. The University is located in the metropolitan Orlando area, which offers a vibrant lifestyle and a variety of cultural and recreational activities.

CREOL (Center for Research and Education in Optics and Lasers) is one of the world’s foremost institutions for research and education in optical and photonic science and engineering. The College offers MS and PhD degrees in optics and photonics, and a BS degree in photonic science and engineering. The faculty engages in fundamental and applied research and education in lasers, optical fibers, semiconductor and integrated photonic devices, nonlinear and quantum optics, imaging, sensing, and displays. The college is home to the CREOL, Florida Photonics Center of Excellence (FPCE), and Townes Laser Institute (TLI), and the Institute for the Frontier of Attosecond Science and Technology (iFAST). In addition, the College of Medicine, which includes the Burnett School of Biomedical Sciences, provides rich opportunities for collaboration. For more information see www.creol.ucf.edu.

The ideal candidate will work with the Semiconductor Diode Laser Group (https://www.creol.ucf.edu/sdl/) to participate in research in experimental optics. Our research focuses on large, high-power semiconductor diode laser arrays, with particular emphasis on external-cavity coupling, phase locking, coherent beam combining, and the collective dynamics of coupled laser systems. Current projects explore the emergence and control of synchronization, spatial and temporal coherence, and the other collective states in large arrays of coupled semiconductor lasers. The research combines advanced optical experiments with theoretical and computational modeling of nonlinear laser dynamics.

We are seeking a highly motivated researchers with strong experimental expertise in free-space optics, beam propagation, and semiconductor laser systems. The successful candidate will contribute to the development, alignment, characterization, and optimization of advanced optical and photonic experimental platforms involving semiconductor diode lasers and laser arrays.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Ph.D. from an accredited institution in Optics/Photonics, Electrical Engineering or a closely related field.
  • Strong hands-on experience with free-space optical systems, including optical alignment, optimization, and troubleshooting.
  • Solid understanding of Gaussian beam propagation, diffraction, focusing, imaging, and optical beam characterization.
  • Experience working with semiconductor lasers, laser sources, and associated optical components.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently align, characterize, and optimize complex free-space optical steps involving lenses, mirrors, beam splitters, spatial filters, detectors, and related instrumentation.
  • Experience with optical diagnostics, experimental data acquisition, and analysis is desirable.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Familiarity with the dynamics and modeling of semiconductor diode lasers and laser arrays.
  • Knowledge of nonlinear dynamics, synchronization, or nonlinear systems.

Job.JobTitle: Postdoctoral Research Associate in Large Nonlinear Computational Dynamical Systems
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Orlando, FL

About this job

Postdoctoral position at CREOL developing efficient numerical methods for large-scale simulations of coupled semiconductor laser arrays. Work combines computational modeling of nonlinear delay-differential equations with high-performance computing and experimental photonics research.

Good fit if you have a PhD in applied mathematics, computational science, physics, or related field, with strong programming skills and experience in numerical methods or high-performance computing.

Full job description

The Opportunity

CREOL (Center for Research and Education in Optics and Lasers) is one of the world’s foremost institutions for research and education in optical and photonic science and engineering. The College offers MS and PhD degrees in optics and photonics, and a BS degree in photonic science and engineering. The faculty engages in fundamental and applied research and education in lasers, optical fibers, semiconductor and integrated photonic devices, nonlinear and quantum optics, imaging, sensing, and displays. The college is home to the CREOL, Florida Photonics Center of Excellence (FPCE), and Townes Laser Institute (TLI), and the Institute for the Frontier of Attosecond Science and Technology (iFAST). In addition, the College of Medicine, which includes the Burnett School of Biomedical Sciences, provides rich opportunities for collaboration. For more information see www.creol.ucf.edu.

Applications are invited for a postdoctoral research position in computational nonlinear dynamics and large-scale numerical modeling of semiconductor laser arrays at the College of Optics and Photonics (CREOL), University of Central Florida. Our research program investigates collective dynamics, synchronization, and self-organization in large arrays of coupled semiconductor diode lasers. The work combines experiments with computational and theoretical modeling of nonlinear dynamical systems with time-delayed interactions.


A major objective of this position is to develop and implement efficient numerical methods for increasingly large and complex systems of coupled nonlinear delay-differential equations (DDEs). Models range from arrays of single-mode semiconductor lasers described by Lang–Kobayashi-type equations to substantially larger multimode systems incorporating multiple optical modes, carrier dynamics, nonlinear interactions, heterogeneity, and delayed nonlocal coupling. As the number of lasers and optical modes increases, direct numerical simulation becomes computationally demanding. The successful candidate will therefore focus not only on physical modeling but also on developing, optimizing, and accelerating computational approaches capable of treating large laser networks efficiently.


The postdoctoral associate researcher will contribute to several areas, including:

  • Numerical integration of large systems of nonlinear delay-differential equations
  • Modeling of single-mode and multimode semiconductor laser arrays
  • Optimization and acceleration of existing simulation codes
  • Parallel computing and high-performance computing (HPC)
  • GPU acceleration, where appropriate
  • Development of scalable numerical algorithms for systems containing large numbers of lasers and optical modes

An important component of the project will be determining how numerical algorithms and existing stimulation codes can be redesigned or optimized to achieve substantial improvements in computational speed while preserving numerical accuracy and stability. The position provides an opportunity to work at the intersection of computational mathematics, nonlinear dynamics, high-performance computing, and experimental photonics. The research is closely connected with ongoing experiments involving large semiconductor diode laser arrays. This interaction provides an unusual opportunity for computational researchers to test theoretical and numerical predictions against experimentally observed collective dynamics. This position allows for opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration involving researchers in optics, photonics, nonlinear dynamics, applied mathematics, and computational science.


Semiconductor-laser experience is not required. The successful candidate will work closely with experimental researchers, and the necessary background in semiconductor laser physics and external-cavity laser systems can be developed as part of the project.


Minimum Qualifications:

  • Ph.D. from an accredited institution in Applied Mathematics, Computational Mathematics, Computational Science, Physics, Optical Science, Electrical Engineering or a closely related discipline.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Strong experience in one or more of the following:
    • Numerical methods for ordinary and delay-differential equations.
    • Scientific computing and numerical analysis
    • Large-scale dynamical systems
    • High-performance computing
    • Parallel numerical algorithms
    • GPU computing
  • Strong programming skills are very important.
  • Experience with C/C++, Python, Julia, MATLAB, CUDA, or a comparable scientific-computing environment is desirable.

Additional Application Materials Required:

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following:

  • A curriculum vitae.
  • Brief statement of research interests and relevant experimental experience.
  • A list of publications
  • List of three professional references with contact information

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.

The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.

Questions regarding this search should be directed to: Dr. Yehuda Braiman at yehuda.braiman@ucf.edu.

All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. H-1B visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H-1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.

The position is anticipated for at least two years, with continued appointment and possible extension subject to satisfactory performance and availability of funding (up to a total of four years).

Tenure-earning assistant professor position in Art History at UCF starting August 2027. Teaches 3/3 load of undergraduate and graduate courses in 18th-19th century European, U.S., or Global art history, with online and in-person options, plus research and service expectations.

The Opportunity

The School of Visual Arts and Design (SVAD) in the College of Arts and Humanities (CAH) at the University of Central Florida (UCF) invites applications for a 9-month, tenure-earning, assistant professor in Art History. The position is located at the UCF main campus and is anticipated to start in August 2027.

The ideal candidate will have demonstrated teaching and research experience in 18th and 19th century European, United States, or Global Art History. They will carry a 3/3 teaching load that includes undergraduate and graduate courses in Art History that serves SVAD majors and the broader UCF student population.

Instructional modalities may include fully online and in-person formats as well as honors seminar sections. The successful candidate must be prepared to deliver high-quality instruction in these modalities as assigned. Additionally, they will guide students in developing undergraduate research projects, supervise internships, and teach lower and upper-division Art History electives aligned with program needs and the candidate’s expertise.

Faculty are also expected to produce research in the form of articles, books, and curation while actively pursuing external funding opportunities to support these endeavors. Primary responsibilities include research, teaching, maintaining regular office hours, assessing student performance in a timely manner, and service to the university.

In SVAD, we are dedicated to the exploration of creativity, where we engage the senses, ignite imagination, and nurture artistic talents. Our mission is to inspire and empower a diverse community of artists and designers. Our curriculum is thoughtfully designed to immerse students in the world of art and design. We offer a range of academic programs, including B.A., BFA, and MFA degrees, tailored to artists and designers of all backgrounds. With a team of over 50 dedicated faculty and staff advisors, SVAD is committed to guiding students toward the right educational path and helping them shape successful careers in the arts. Join our award-winning faculty, renowned for their expertise and passion for nurturing talent. Together, we spark the interests of our students and guide them on a journey of creative discovery. For more information about SVAD and our vibrant community, please visit our website at https://svad.cah.ucf.edu.

UCF is home to a growing and diverse student population of over 70,000 students, almost 2,000 faculty, and more than 4,700 staff. At UCF, we are committed to expanding access and seek candidates who will contribute to our mission through comprehensive, student-centered practices and effective teaching approaches that support the success of all students. For more information about UCF, please visit the website at https://www.ucf.edu.

  • Demonstrated college-level teaching experience (instructor of record, teaching assistantships with significant instructional responsibility, or comparable experience).
  • Demonstrated ability to teach a range of historical periods and/or global art histories.

Good fit if you have a Master's in Nursing, current RN license, recent inpatient clinical experience, and nursing teaching experience.

Job.JobTitle: Lecturer and Undergraduate Program Coordinator, Health Sciences
Job.JobDescription:
The Opportunity

The Department of Health Sciences in the College of Health Professions and Sciences (CHPS) at the University of Central Florida (UCF) invites applications for a 12-month, non-tenure earning, lecturer position. This is a face to face on campus position located at the UCF main campus with a start date in August 2027.

Candidates are required to be a Registered Dietitian Nutritionist (RDN) with substantial full-time teaching experience in an academic institution and a demonstrated commitment to high-quality instruction, student mentoring, curriculum development, and academic program administration.

The successful candidate will teach required undergraduate courses, including a General Education Program-approved nutrition course, an advanced, senior-level Health Sciences seminar or other courses consistent with departmental needs and the candidate’s expertise. They will also contribute to instruction in the department’s forthcoming graduate program in Nutrition Science and Dietetics.

In addition to teaching responsibilities, the selected candidate will serve as the Undergraduate Program Coordinator. This is a critical role that supports the quality, effectiveness, and continued development of the department’s undergraduate curriculum. The coordinator will work collaboratively with department and college leadership, faculty, staff, and university partners to advance curricular best practices, facilitate continuous program improvement, support student recruitment and success, and ensure fulfillment of institutional and General Education Program requirements.

The successful candidate will be expected to:

  • Teach required undergraduate courses, including a General Education Program-approved nutrition course, an advanced, senior-level Health Sciences Seminar or other courses consistent with departmental needs and the candidate’s expertise
  • Contribute to instructional and supervised practice aspects of our forthcoming Nutrition Science and Dietetics Coordinated Program.
  • Use evidence-based, inclusive, and student-centered teaching practices, including appropriate interprofessional education activities.
  • Mentor students in their academic, professional, and career development.
  • Coordinate undergraduate curriculum review and revision, prepare and manage curricular actions, including the development and submission of assessment plans, results, reports, and program improvement actions, and promote evidence-based curricular and pedagogical practices.
  • Coordinate the review and maintenance of General Education Program courses to ensure continued alignment with university standards, learning outcomes, assessment requirements, and reporting expectations.
  • Conduct transfer course evaluations and provide recommendations regarding course equivalencies, substitutions, and related curricular matters.
  • Conduct institutional effectiveness activities and contribute to academic program review, accreditation, and other institutional reporting activities, as applicable.
  • Collaborate with faculty, academic advisors, staff, and administrators to support the consistent implementation of undergraduate academic policies and procedures.
  • Coordinate and participate in undergraduate recruitment, outreach, orientation, and student engagement activities.
  • Participate in departmental, college, and university committees, governance activities, interprofessional education initiatives, and professional development.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Doctoral degree (i.e., PhD, DCN, DrPH, etc.) in Nutrition, Dietetics, Leadership, or a closely related field from an accredited institution at the time of application.
  • Credentialed as a Registered Dietitian Nutritionist (RDN) by the Commission on Dietetic Registration (CDR).
  • Minimum two academic years of college-level teaching experience as the instructor of record. Teaching experience gained as an instructor of record during doctoral study may be included.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Six or more years of full-time teaching experience as a faculty member and instructor of record at a baccalaureate-granting college or university.
  • Strong record of at least one of the following: teaching, mentorship, or program leadership.
  • Experience with curriculum development, curricular review, and academic program administration.
  • Excellent communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with diverse stakeholders.

Additional Application Materials Required:

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, candidates will be required to upload the following documents:

  • Cover letter addressing the applicant’s qualifications with specific examples of how their experience will support high-quality instruction, student mentoring and success, curriculum management and continuous improvement, and the overall effectiveness of the undergraduate program.
  • Curriculum vitae
  • Teaching philosophy

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.


The selected candidate will be required to submit a list of references and official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.


Questions regarding this search should be directed to: Dr. Martha Garcia-Stout, at martha.garcia-stout@ucf.edu.


Special Instructions to the Applicants:

All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. H-1B visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H-1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.

Job.JobTitle: Professor and Director, Dr. Yvette Kanouff School of Data, Mathematical and Statistical Sciences
Job.JobDescription:
The Opportunity

The College of Sciences at the University of Central Florida (UCF) invites applications for a full-time, 12-month, position of tenured professor and director of the newly formed School of Data, Mathematical, and Statistical Sciences with an anticipated start date on May 1, 2027. The successful candidate will serve as the inaugural Director of the School. The director is the unit head, provides leadership for the school, and is essential to the decision-making and administrative functions within the unit, including academic programs, budget, hiring, evaluations, and facilities. This appointment offers an opportunity to strengthen connections across the disciplines in the school and support their distinctive strengths. Nominations of ideal candidates can be communicated to the Committee Chair, Dr. Brett McCollum (brett.mccollum@ucf.edu).


The Dr. Yvette Kanouff School of Data, Mathematical, and Statistical Sciences (Kanouff School) is a new interdisciplinary unit within the College of Sciences formed from the merger of the Department of Mathematics and the Department of Statistics and Data Science. The new school has a growing, innovative population of faculty and students carrying out theoretical and applied research in Mathematics, Statistics, Data Science, Actuarial Science, and Artificial Intelligence / Machine Learning. The school’s undergraduate academic programs include degrees in Data Science, Actuarial Science, Mathematics, and Statistics. Graduate programming includes a M.S. degree in Statistics and Data Science with two tracks in Data Science and Statistical Computing and a SAS certificate program, a M.S. degree in Mathematical Science including tracks in Industrial Mathematics and Financial Mathematics, a Ph.D. in Mathematics including a track in Financial Mathematics, and a Ph.D. in Big Data Analytics including a track in Statistics. The Ph.D. in Big Data Analytics is the first Ph.D. program of its kind in the state of Florida and only one of a few across the globe and has been ranked #4 nationally by TechGuide’s Best Data Analytics Ph.D. programs in 2025.


With 70 full-time faculty, The Kanouff School serves over 120 graduate students and 800 program majors, provides prerequisite courses for colleges such as Engineering & Computer Science and Medicine, and offers General Education courses that support the broader undergraduate student community. As a significant service teaching unit, the school annually supports roughly 4,000 undergraduate FTE across more than 600 course sections of various class sizes. It is a collegial academic unit with broad representation that values collaborations and mentorship across subdisciplines. The school faculty collaborate with faculty from across the College of Sciences as well as the Institute of Artificial Intelligence, the National Center of Forensic Science, the Nanoscience and Technology Center, the College of Optics and Photonics, the College of Engineering and Computer Science, the College of Medicine, the College of Nursing, and the College of Community Innovation and Education, thus preparing our students for complex problem solving in an interdisciplinary world. For more information, visit https://sciences.ucf.edu/sdmss/.


The UCF College of Sciences (COS) is the largest college at the university and a powerhouse for the regional and national STEM workforce, spanning the natural, computational, physical, and social sciences and housing centers, institutes and initiatives that serve as hubs for research and innovation. Through sharing and applying knowledge, COS is cultivating pathways for students to solve our world’s most pressing and complex problems. With a mission to provide a world-class education in an environment where faculty, staff, and students thrive, research flourishes, and our community prospers; a number of COS academic programs are among those nationally ranked by U.S. News and World Report, Princeton Review, and others. For more information, please visit https://sciences.ucf.edu.

UCF, named one of the most innovative public universities in the nation by U.S. News & World Report, is located in Orlando, Florida and is classified as a Very High Research Activity university by the Carnegie Foundation. With more than 70,000 students, UCF is one of the largest universities in the country, offering more than 240 degree programs. UCF is an economic engine, attracting and supporting industries vital to the region's future while providing students with real-world experiences that help them succeed after graduation. For more information, visit http://www.ucf.edu.

Minimum Qualifications:

A Ph.D. in Data Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Actuarial Science, or a closely related field, from an accredited institution. In addition, to be eligible for appointment as a tenured professor upon hire, the successful applicant must have a distinguished record commensurate with a tenured faculty member at the rank of professor within the Kanouff School with respect to teaching, research, and service. Candidates will have a demonstrated record of administrative leadership in a university or similar setting for at least 2 years.


Preferred Qualifications:

Preference will be given to candidates who have demonstrated experience in:

  • handling faculty matters,
  • supervising staff,
  • managing budgets,
  • using strong communication skills,
  • having a distinguished record of teaching at the undergraduate and graduate levels, and
  • having a strong publication record reflecting experience conducting research within the disciplines of the school.

Additional Application Materials Required:

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/ . In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following materials: (1) a current CV, and (2) a 2-to-3-page letter of interest that addresses the qualifications, research and leadership experience, teaching philosophy, and vision for the school.


NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.


The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.


Review of applications will begin on November 16, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled.


Questions regarding the position should be directed to Dr. Brett McCollum, Search Committee Chair, at brett.mccollum@ucf.edu.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. H-1B visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H-1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.

Open until filled.

About this job

UCF Chemistry Department seeks a Postdoctoral Scholar to conduct computational chemistry research focused on nanophotonics, quantum mechanics, and machine learning-assisted modeling. The one-year position, renewable based on funding, includes working with Dr. Shengli Zou on research, manuscript preparation, and student mentoring.

Good fit if you have a PhD in computational chemistry or related field and experience with theoretical chemistry, relevant software, and programming languages.

Full job description

The Opportunity (Job description):


The University of Central Florida (UCF) chemistry department in the College of Sciences (COS) seeks to hire a Postdoctoral Scholar. The initial appointment will be for one year and may be renewed based on the availability of funding and satisfactory progress on the research project.


Responsibilities:

 The Postdoctoral Scholar will: 

  • Work collaboratively with the Principal Investigator (Dr. Shengli Zou).
  • Conduct advanced computational chemistry research with a focus on nanophotonics, quantum mechanics, and machine learning–assisted modeling and simulations.
  • Prepare manuscripts and conference presentations.
  • Assist the Principal Investigator with writing grant reports.
  • Assist the Principal Investigator with mentoring undergraduate and graduate students.

Minimum Qualifications:

A doctorate in computational chemistry or a closely related field from an accredited institution by time of hire is required. Strong background in theoretical and computational chemistry. Proficiency in relevant software, operational system, and programming languages.


Preferred Qualifications:


Preference will be given to candidates who have demonstrated significant contributions in computational chemistry, nanoscience, nanotechnology, catalysis, and/or sensing. Track record of high-quality publications in peer-reviewed journals. Experience in Machine learning.


Additional Application Materials Required:

 UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/.  In addition to the online application, candidates should upload:

  • CV/Resume
  • Cover letter with research interest
  • Names and contact information for three professional references, with at least two being academic references (including their positions/titles, affiliations, email addresses, and phone numbers).

The selected candidate will be required to submit documentation verifying the conferral of their qualifying PhD degree or equivalent academic credential.


NOTE: When applying, please have all your documents ready to upload at the same time. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.


Benefits of the position include:

Competitive salary and benefits package, with a starting salary of $60,000. The position offers opportunities for professional growth and career development. The appointment is renewable based on mutual agreement and the availability of funding. UCF provides a vibrant and inclusive research environment with state-of-the-art facilities.

Interested candidates may contact Dr. Shengli Zou at shengli.zou@ucf.edu for more information about the application process. Application review will begin on October 1st, and the position will remain open until filled. The expected start date is January 1st, 2027.

This annually renewable position offers a clear career path with the possibility of promotion based on years of service and performance. 

The selected candidates will take roles in developing curriculum and pedagogy with the intent of improving student learning in undergraduate courses in mathematics. Additionally, we are especially interested in individuals who can contribute through their teaching and service to the excellence of our academic community and foster an environment in which faculty, staff, and students of broad representation are welcomed and can thrive. The instructional duties and service assignments are in accordance with the school’s current equitable workload policy. 

The Kanouff School is a new interdisciplinary unit within the College of Sciences formed from the merger of the Department of Mathematics and the Department of Statistics and Data Science. The new school has a growing, innovative population of faculty and students carrying out theoretical and applied research in Mathematics, Statistics, Data Science, Actuarial Science, and Artificial Intelligence / Machine Learning. The Ph.D. in Big Data Analytics is the first Ph.D. program of its kind in the state of Florida and only one of a few across the globe and has been ranked #4 nationally by TechGuide’s Best Data Analytics Ph.D. programs in 2025. For more information about these programs at UCF visit https://sciences.ucf.edu/sdmss/.

Through sharing and applying knowledge, COS is cultivating pathways for students to solve our world’s most pressing and complex problems. The mission of COS is to provide a world-class education in an environment where faculty, staff, and students thrive, research flourishes, and our community prospers. Several COS academic programs are nationally ranked by U.S. News and World Report, Princeton Review, and others. For more information, please visit https://sciences.ucf.edu.

A doctorate in mathematics or a closely related field from an accredited institution at the time of hire. In addition, the successful applicant must have undergraduate teaching experience in mathematics at the lower division levels.

Preferred Qualifications:

Preference will be given to candidates with two or more of the following: 

  • Equivalent of three years of full-time college level teaching experience in mathematics. 
  • Experience in teaching mathematics at the upper division levels. 
  • Experience in implementation of student success initiatives. 
  • Experience using online technology in mathematics courses.

Job.JobDescription:
The Opportunity

The University of Central Florida (UCF) is looking for a 12-month, non-tenure earning assistant scientist, associate scientist, or scientist, to conduct research in the College of Optics and Photonics. This position is located at the UCF main campus with an anticipated start date in late Fall 2026 but no later than Spring 2027. UCF is undergoing rapid growth in the size of external research funding, academic stature, and student and faculty groups. UCF supports and benefits from economic growth in Central Florida, which is emerging as a major hub for technology development. The University is located in the metropolitan Orlando area, which offers a vibrant lifestyle and a variety of cultural and recreational activities.

CREOL (Center for Research and Education in Optics and Lasers) is one of the world’s foremost institutions for research and education in optical and photonic science and engineering. The College offers MS and PhD degrees in optics and photonics, and a BS degree in photonic science and engineering. The faculty engages in fundamental and applied research and education in lasers, optical fibers, semiconductor and integrated photonic devices, nonlinear and quantum optics, imaging, sensing, and displays. The college is home to CREOL, Florida Photonics Center of Excellence (FPCE), and Townes Laser Institute (TLI), and the Institute for the Frontier of Attosecond Science and Technology (iFAST). In addition, the College of Medicine, which includes the Burnett School of Biomedical Sciences, provides rich opportunities for collaboration. For more information see www.creol.ucf.edu.

The Optical Communication and Photonic Systems Group (https://www.creol.ucf.edu/ofc/) is seeking multiple Assistant Research Scientists to participate in research in integrated photonic systems for applications in free-space and optical fiber communication, datacenter interconnects, optical signal processing and computing.

Candidates with strong expertise as well as the ability to conduct independent research and supervise graduate students in one or more of the following areas are encouraged to apply:

  • Modelling, design and optimization of active and passive photonic devices using custom and commercial design and simulation packages
  • Multi-plane light conversion
  • Integrated device fabrication (in house and/or via foundry services) using various material platforms (SiN, Si, III-V)
  • Optical and electro-optical characterization of integrated devices and subsystems.
  • Digital signal processing, control/optimization, AI/ML
  • System applications and demonstrations

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Ph.D. from an accredited institution in Optics, Physics, Electrical Engineering or a closely related field.
  • 2 years of experience in the field.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in at least two or more areas of the following: active and passive photonic devices, multi-plane light conversion, integrated device fabrication, digital signal processing or system applications and demonstrations.

Additional Application Materials Required:

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following:

  • A curriculum vitae.
  • A letter of interest describing qualifications for the position, such as research agenda and teaching experience/interest.

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.

The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.

Questions regarding this search should be directed to: Dr. Guifang Li at li@ucf.edu.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. H-1B visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H-1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.

 

This is a Contract & Grants (C&G) funded position. Employment is subject to availability of funding and may cease at the time funding for this employment is depleted.

Job Close Date:

Open until filled.

Note to applicants: Please keep in mind that a job posted as ‘Open until filled’ may close at any time without notice. As such, we encourage you to submit your application and all required documentation as quickly as possible to ensure consideration for the posted position.

Department of Psychology:

The Department of Psychology at UCF has over 50 full-time faculty, approximately 4,500 undergraduate majors, and houses Ph.D. programs in Clinical Psychology, Human Factors and Cognitive Psychology, and I/O Psychology. For more information, visit https://sciences.ucf.edu/psychology/

The Opportunity:

The University of Central Florida’s (UCF) Department of Psychology, in the College of Sciences, seeks applicants to direct its in-house Psychology Clinic. The clinic provides assessment and psychotherapy to adults from the Central Florida community, using a low-cost sliding-scale fee system. Students currently enrolled in the UCF Clinical Psychology Ph.D. Program provide direct clinical services, under the close supervision of licensed Psychologists.

This is a full-time, 12-month staff position reporting to the Program Director, who is a faculty member within the Clinical Psychology Ph.D. Program, and who reports to the department chair. Compensation is competitive and commensurate with experience and qualifications.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Supervising graduate students in clinical practicum.
  • Supervising clinic staff and directing overall clinic operations.
  • Overseeing use of clinical records software and release of information requests.
  • Maintaining security of private health information.
  • Providing coverage for clinical emergencies during operating hours.
  • Developing and maintaining relationships with referring agencies.
  • Leading initiatives that support continuous improvement of the clinic.

Minimum Qualifications: 

  • A doctorate in clinical or counseling psychology from an APA (American Psychological Association) accredited program, completion of an APA-accredited internship or closely related field and have a minimum of 4 years of relevant experience.
  • Must possess a current clinical license in their current state jurisdiction of practice.
  • Must be license eligible in Florida at time of hire, licensed by the State of Florida within 6 months of hire date, and must maintain license.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Competence with and primary orientation in empirically supported assessment and psychotherapy approaches.
  • 4+ years of related experience acquired after receipt of doctoral degree.
  • Previous experience with clinical supervision of trainees using empirically supported assessment and psychotherapy approaches with adult patients.
  • Previous experience providing and/or supervising teletherapy.
  • Licensed as a Psychologist in the United States.

 

Additional Application Materials Required:

  • Resume/Curriculum Vitae (CV).
  • A cover letter outlining your background and motivation for pursuing this opportunity, including your interest in leading and supporting the Psychology Clinic at UCF.

 

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

  • This is a full-time role (40 hours per week), generally scheduled Monday through Friday, with flexibility to adjust specific days and times based on clinic needs.
  • All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.

Job.JobTitle: Professor and Miller Technology Endowed Chair in Intelligent Work Systems, The Barry S. Miller College of Business
Job.JobDescription:
The Opportunity

The Barry S. Miller College of Business at the University of Central Florida invites applications for the Miller Technology Endowed Chair in Intelligent Work Systems, a 9-month tenured position at the rank of professor. This position is located on the UCF Main Campus with an anticipated start date in Fall 2027.

The central question addressed by this chair is: How should organizations design work and allocate responsibilities between humans and intelligent technologies to maximize organizational performance? Advances in artificial intelligence, robotics, automation, and digital platforms are fundamentally reshaping the nature of work. We seek a scholar whose work advances understanding of organizational design, the future of work, human-AI collaboration, leadership, workforce systems, organizational behavior, decision-making, or related areas.

This endowed chair is part of a broader investment, five endowed chairs in all, each committed to advancing scholarship and education at the intersection of technology and business transformation. The Miller Chairs are not organized around traditional academic disciplines, but around consequential problems emerging from the intersection of technology, organizations, and markets.

Miller Chairs are intended for scholars whose work has shaped—or has the clear potential to shape—how organizations function in a technology-driven economy. The successful candidate will play a central role in shaping the intellectual direction of the College’s technology-focused initiatives and will contribute to the School of Technology Leadership and Innovation (STLI), a university-wide initiative focused on translating advances in technology into organizational capability, market innovation, and executive practice.

The UCF College of Business is one of the largest business schools in the United States and is located in Orlando, one of the nation’s fastest growing and most dynamic economic regions. UCF is a Carnegie R1 institution and is recognized for its leadership in innovation, partnerships, and its identity as Florida’s Technology University.

The college is actively investing in initiatives that position it at the forefront of technology-enabled business education, including interdisciplinary programs, applied research collaborations, and new models of engagement with industry.

Responsibilities include:

  • Serve as an intellectual architect for the college’s Intelligent Work Systems initiative by building collaborations among faculty, industry, and government that establish UCF as a national leader in the field.
  • Demonstrate ability to translate scholarly expertise into organizational practice through industry partnerships, executive education, public engagement, policy influence, or other mechanisms that create measurable impact.
  • Conduct high-impact research on how organizations design and manage the interaction between people, technology, and decision systems.
  • Contribute to the development of new academic programs and executive offerings aligned with the College’s technology focus.

  

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Ph.D. in business, economics, information systems, engineering, computer science, psychology, or a closely related field from an AACSB-accredited (or equivalent) institution at time of application.
  • A record of scholarly achievement sufficient to qualify for appointment with tenure at the rank of Full Professor in the College of Business.
  • Demonstrated impact in research related to organizational design, leadership, decision-making, or technology-enabled work systems.
  • Evidence of an active and sustained research agenda with publications in leading peer-reviewed journals.
  • Experience teaching at the undergraduate and/or graduate level.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Candidates should demonstrate a history of engaging with organizations in ways that shape practice, including through applied research, advisory roles, or collaborative initiatives.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead interdisciplinary collaborations that produce new research, educational programs or industry partnerships.
  • Commitment to translating scholarship into executive education and organizational capability.
  • A record of leadership in shaping academic programs, research centers, or major initiatives.

 

Additional Application Materials Required:

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following:

  • Cover letter
  • Curriculum vitae
  • Research statement
  • Teaching statement
  • Contact information for three professional references will be required prior to extending an offer

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.

The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.

Questions regarding this search should be directed to: Dr. Pradeep Bhardwaj at Pradeep.bhardwaj@ucf.edu.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. H-1B visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H-1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.

Open until filled

This position is located on the UCF Main Campus with an anticipated start date in Fall 2027.

The central question addressed by this chair is: How should financial systems evolve to create, allocate, govern, and exchange capital in an increasingly intelligent, digital, and interconnected economy? Technologies such as artificial intelligence, digital platforms, blockchain, embedded finance, and advanced analytics are transforming financial institutions, markets, and organizational decision-making.  We seek a scholar whose work advances understanding of financial systems, financial markets, financial institutions, accounting information systems, financial technology, corporate finance, banking, digital assets, financial regulation, or related areas.

The Opportunity


The Singla Lab at the University of Central Florida College of Medicine in Orlando seeks a highly motivated, creative, and ambitious postdoctoral fellow to study treatment resistance and tumor-microenvironment interactions in various cancer models and associated toxicological studies.


This part of the project focuses on developing cancer models; therefore, we are looking for a postdoctoral fellow who will conduct innovative cancer research using functional studies with 3D culture models and organoids. Identify the underlying mechanisms using cell biology and molecular biology techniques. They will also be expected to perform research, write manuscripts, assist in grant proposals, and present their findings at local and national meetings. The fellow should work independently, lead project(s), troubleshoot issues, present their work, and train other lab members as part of their postdoctoral training. 


Prof. Singla’s lab is a friendly and welcoming place with great excitement for cancer and cardiovascular research.


Minimum Qualifications


The ideal candidate should have a Ph.D. in cancer biology/immunology/molecular biology with a strong background in cancer cell culture models (2D, 3D, and organoids), cancer mouse models such as xenotransplantation models, and basic and advanced molecular biology techniques. Candidates should possess a track record of scientific productivity, as well as excellent oral, written, and interpersonal communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications


Experience in testing preclinical animal models, including PDX using humanized mice, syngeneic mouse models, and xenografts, is highly desired.


Additional Application Materials Required


A cover letter, CV, names and contact information of three professional references, and date of availability will be required to be considered.

Job Posting Title: 

Post Doctoral Scholar

 

The Opportunity:

The Department of Civil, Environmental and Construction Engineering at the University of Central Florida is inviting a motivated Postdoctoral Associate to join the DISCOVER (Digital-Twin Infrastructure Science for Operations and Visualization in Engineering Resilience) Laboratory and become part of an interdisciplinary research team conducting research at the convergence of multiscale computational mechanics, civil infrastructure resilience and digital twin modeling. The position will require extensive collaboration across disciplines to tackle research that incorporates Engineering Mechanics, Structural Engineering, AI and Data Science. The candidate will assist the DISCOVER lab with managing existing research projects and preparing research proposals and publications in the research areas listed above.

The Postdoctoral Associate will lead the development of research proposals and reports, collaborate in sponsored research projects, supervise graduate research assistants, represent the DISCOVER Lab at national and international conferences, symposia, and professional meetings through published research works and presentations. The selected candidate will have an opportunity to work in a research-oriented laboratory equipped with state-of-the-art hardware and software tools, performing cutting-edge research related to digital twin modeling of large-scale infrastructure systems. The position is perfect for recently graduated post-doctorate professionals looking to grow their research records (with additional, optional opportunities to grow their teaching portfolio, according to the candidate’s preference and career goals). However, other more-experienced candidates will also be given consideration.

 

Minimum Qualifications: 

  •  PhD from an accredited university in Civil Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, or related field.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills.
  • Demonstrated potential to lead the development of research proposals and advise graduate students.
  • Demonstrated leadership/managerial and organizational skills.
  • Full professional proficiency in one of the following languages: Python (including PyTorch and TensorFlow), Julia (including Flux.jl and CUDA.jl), C++.

Preferred Qualifications:

Job.JobTitle: Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor, Transportation Engineering Systems
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Orlando, FL
  • Benefits: Health insurance, paid time off, paid holidays

About this job

Full-time, tenure-earning or tenured faculty position in Transportation Engineering Systems within Civil Engineering. UCF's Transportation Science program ranks first in the U.S. and will house the newly established Florida Transportation Research Institute.

Good fit if you have a doctorate in Engineering or related field, expertise in transportation (vehicles, logistics, data analytics, traffic operations, or related areas), and research experience.

Full job description

The Opportunity   

 The University of Central Florida (UCF) is dedicated to increasing the prominence of its Civil, Environmental, and Construction Engineering (CECE) Department. UCF offers B.S., M.S., and Ph.D. degrees in Civil Engineering and the undergraduate degree is ABET-accredited.  

The CECE department houses several high-impact labs. Transportation Science and Technology at UCF is ranked the top program in the U.S. and 19th globally in the 2025 Shanghai Ranking. Learn more about the Transportation Science program at UCF here: https://www.ucf.edu/transportation-science/. The CECE department faculty maintain diverse, active, and successful research programs. Learn more about the CECE department at https://www.cece.ucf.edu/. UCF is a leader in Transportation in Florida and will house the newly established multimillion-dollar Florida Transportation Research Institute (FTRI) mandated by the Florida legislature and Florida Secretary of Transportation in 2024. 

To strengthen these efforts, we invite applications for a full-time, 9-month, tenure-earning assistant professor or tenured associate professor, or professor position in Transportation Engineering Systems within the Civil Engineering program, with an anticipated start date of August 8, 2027.  

The selected candidate hired for this position is expected to have either demonstrated (tenured) or shown a clear potential (tenure-earning) for creative and independent research that has led (tenured) or would potentially lead (tenure-earning) to strong extramurally funded research and national/international recognition. The selected candidate is also expected to train postdoctoral scholars, serve as the primary advisor for graduate students, and teach graduate and undergraduate courses in Civil Engineering.  

Minimum Qualifications:  

  • A doctorate from an accredited institution in Engineering, Computer Science, or a closely related field at the time of the appointment.  

  • To be eligible for appointment as a tenured associate professor or professor upon hire, the selected candidate must have a demonstrated record of teaching, research, and service commensurate with a tenured faculty appointment at the rank of associate professor or professor in the applicable tenure home.  

  • Candidates must have expertise in one or more aspects of transportation, including but not limited to the following: connected vehicles/automated vehicles’ applications; transportation technologies; traveler behavior and demand modeling; freight and transportation logistics; applications of econometrics and data analytics to transportation planning; traffic signals’ control and technologies; traffic operations; smart mobility; big data and internet of things; air mobility; transportation economics and policies; etc.  

  • Successful applicants will have either demonstrated or shown a clear potential for creative and independent research that has led or would lead to strong extramurally funded research. 

  

Preferred Qualifications:  

  • Preference will be given to those with a few years of experience in academia or industry with a proven ability to publish in top transportation and transportation technology journals. 

Additional Application Materials Required:  

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following:  

  • A curriculum vitae, 

  • A signed cover letter, 

  • A two-page maximum statement outlining research vision and teaching interests,

  • A list of at least three professional references complete with address, phone number, and email address. 

   

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.  

  

The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Orlando, FL
  • Benefits: Health insurance, paid time off, paid holidays

About this job

Full-time, 9-month lecturer position teaching nursing leadership and management courses primarily in online MSN and DNP-Executive programs at UCF's College of Nursing. Rank (lecturer, associate lecturer, or senior lecturer) determined by credentials and experience; start date Fall 2027.

Good fit if you have a doctorate in nursing or health-related field, current RN license, and documented teaching experience in academic settings.

Full job description

The Opportunity

The College of Nursing at the University of Central Florida (UCF) invites applications for multiple full-time, 9-month, non-tenure earning faculty positions as Lecturer in the Department of Nursing Systems. The selected candidates will teach nursing leadership and management courses, primarily in the online MSN-Leadership and Management program, the DNP-Executive programs, and other programs as assigned. The positions will be located on the UCF Academic Health Sciences Campus at Lake Nona and are expected to start Fall 2027. The appropriate rank (lecturer, associate lecturer, or senior lecturer) will be determined based upon the selected candidates’ credentials and prior experience.

The selected candidates will work collaboratively with colleagues, remain actively involved in professional organizations, and actively participate in College of Nursing faculty governance.

Responsibilities include:

  • Teach online courses in the MSN -Leadership and Management Program, DNP -Executive Program, and other graduate or undergraduate courses as assigned and qualified.

  • Plan, organize, and deliver instruction that supports student learning and success.

  • Support the College of Nursing mission and departmental efforts to advance excellence in teaching and learning.

  • Collaborate with the department chair and faculty colleagues to plan, develop, and improve courses and curricula.

  • Advise and mentor students and, as appropriate to rank, support adjunct faculty and early-career faculty.

  • Participate in department, college, and university service, including committee leadership as appropriate to rank.

Minimum Qualifications for a Lecturer:

  • Earned doctorate in nursing or a health-related field from an accredited institution at he time of application.

  • Graduate degree in nursing (master’s degree in nursing if doctoral degree is not in nursing).

  • Unencumbered RN license. Florida licensure expected by date of hire; with multi-state endorsement expected by date of hire.

  • Documented teaching experience (online, hybrid, and/or classroom) in an academic setting.

Minimum Qualifications for an Associate Lecturer:

  • Earned doctorate in nursing or a health-related field from an accredited institution at the time of application.

  • Graduate degree in nursing (master’s degree in nursing if doctoral degree is not in nursing).

  • Unencumbered RN license. Florida licensure expected by date of hire; with multi-state endorsement expected by date of hire.

  • Five or more years of full-time academic teaching experience (online, hybrid, and/or classroom) at the baccalaureate level or above as demonstrated on CV.

  • A consistent record of excellence in teaching and service to colleges and universities as demonstrated by teaching/course evaluations and CV.

Minimum Qualifications for a Senior Lecturer:

  • Earned doctorate in nursing or a health-related field from an accredited institution at the time of application.

  • Graduate degree in nursing (master’s degree in nursing if doctoral degree is not in nursing).

  • Unencumbered RN license. Florida licensure expected by date of hire; with multi-state endorsement expected by date of hire.

  • Five or more years of full-time academic teaching experience (online, hybrid, and/or classroom) at the baccalaureate level or above.

  • A consistent record of excellence in teaching and service to colleges and universities as demonstrated by teaching/course evaluations, and CV.

  • Demonstrated leadership in student advising, professional development, and/or mentoring.

  • Demonstrated leadership in peer mentoring including orientation of new or adjunct faculty.

  • Demonstrated leadership in curriculum or course development, enhancement, and/or revision.

  • Demonstrated leadership in departmental, college, university, and professional service, through leadership roles or contributing leadership to specific work of the committees.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Expertise in nursing leadership, including healthcare finance, quality improvement, patient safety, and systems leadership.

  • Demonstrated experience designing courses and curricula.

  • Certification or formal preparation in online education quality standards, such as Quality Matters or the Online Learning Consortium.

  • Experience using virtual simulation applications in teaching or learning.

  • Experience teaching online courses in leadership, informatics or AI, population health management, financial management, ethics and professional behavior, or organizational dynamics.

  • Certification in nursing leadership, such as NE-BC, NEA-BC, CNML, or CENP.

  • Demonstrated scholarship, such as publications or national presentations.

  • Active participation in professional organizations related to nursing leadership, nursing management, or executive health leadership.

  • Formal training or experience in leadership coaching, executive coaching, or mentorship programs that support leadership development in healthcare settings.

Additional Application Materials Required:

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following:

  • A curriculum vitae.

  • A letter of interest describing qualifications for the position, such as teaching experience/interest.

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.

The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Orlando, FL
  • Benefits: Health insurance, paid time off, paid holidays

About this job

UCF College of Medicine seeks three full-time primary care physicians (Internal Medicine or Family Medicine) for outpatient practice in Orlando. Faculty positions include patient care, teaching medical learners, and potential clinical research involvement.

Good fit if you have an M.D. or D.O., Florida licensure or eligibility, board certification or eligibility, and prefer outpatient settings.

Full job description

The Opportunity

The University of Central Florida (UCF), College of Medicine Faculty Practice at UCF Health in Orlando, FL is seeking three (3) full-time primary care physicians in Internal Medicine or Family Medicine to join an expanding multi-specialty academic practice. Applicants should be exceptional clinicians who have demonstrated a value-based philosophy of patient care and are seeking an exclusively outpatient care environment. The majority of the assignments for the selected candidates will be to provide direct patient care while building their outpatient practice in collaboration with multiple specialties. Being faculty in the College of Medicine, they may have small roles for teaching or precepting medical learners and other health-related trainees (e.g., for medical students and interprofessional education), as well as participating in clinical research (e.g., sponsored pharmaceutical trials). In that the UCF Health practice is growing in size and scope, the faculty assignment is likely to include a role in Federally Qualified Health Clinics (FQHCs) which would involve providing care in a team that embraces other health care disciplines and involves advanced practice practitioners. The positions are non-tenure track clinical appointments at the rank of assistant, associate or professor of medicine. These are full-time positions at five days a week, with protected non-face-to-face patient care and administrative time.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Candidates must have an M.D. or D.O. degree from an accredited medical or osteopathic school.

  • Candidates must be eligible for licensure or actively licensed to practice in the state of Florida.

  • Must be boarded or board eligible in their specialty upon completion of training. Board certification would be expected within two (2) years of completion of training.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • It is preferred that the candidate have at least three years of experience in a busy high-volume outpatient clinic practice as well as prior experience in rendering care that involves physician extenders.

  • Previous experience working with medical as well as interprofessional health care learners in a clinical outpatient setting is desired.

  • Candidates with publications or other scholarly output are encouraged to apply.

Additional Application Materials Required:

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload a curriculum vitae and cover letter.

Job.JobTitle: Associate Dean for Students and Associate Professor or Professor of Medicine
Job.JobDescription:
The Opportunity

The College of Medicine (COM) invites applications for the position of associate professor or professor of medicine and Associate Dean for Students. This senior educational leadership role reports to the senior associate dean for undergraduate medical education (SADME) and is responsible for promoting a supportive, student‑centered learning environment that strengthens engagement, professional development, well‑being, and academic success for students in the M.D. program.  

The Associate Dean provides strategic leadership for programs and services supporting medical students across both the pre‑clinical and clinical phases of the curriculum. This includes initiatives focused on academic success, career development and advising, student activities and organizations, student well-being, and student financial services. 

The Associate Dean for Students serves as a key architect of the medical student experience within the College of Medicine, shaping a culture that supports learners academically, professionally, and personally. This leader plays a central role in cultivating an environment where medical students feel valued, empowered, and equipped to thrive throughout their medical education journey. The ideal candidate will bring at least five years of progressively responsible experience in student affairs, academic support, student success, medical education, or related higher education roles, along with an understanding of the unique challenges facing medical students, outstanding communication and organizational skills, and strong management skills.

UCF COM has 120 medical students per class, serves more than 3000 undergraduate and graduate students, and partners with HCA Healthcare to sponsor residency and fellowship programs. As a key member of the college’s educational leadership team, the Associate Dean will contribute to advancing the educational mission of the college with excellence, collaboration, and integrity. The position collaborates extensively with college leadership, including the Associate Dean for Medical Education and Department Chairs, to advance the college’s missions in an integrated manner.

This is a non-tenure earning or tenure-earning position and is expected to be a partial FTE administrative appointment (0.80 FTE), with the remaining effort allocated to teaching, clinical practice, scholarship, or other academic responsibilities consistent with the selected candidate’s background and departmental needs. Tenure track candidates are welcome to apply but must be eligible for tenure upon hire.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Overseeing student affairs functions to include the Offices of Admissions, Career Services, Counseling and Wellness, Student Academic Support Services, Student Financial Services, Student Services, and Registrar.

  • Supervising, mentoring, and supporting the Assistant Deans for Students and professional staff engaged in student support and advising.

  • Leading the four-year comprehensive advising program for medical students, including providing faculty development for advisors, leading the Careers Curriculum for medical students, and supporting students in the residency application and match.

  • Leading the Medical Student Performance Evaluation process for fourth-year medical students to ensure production of reliable, accurate, and consistent MSPEs across the Associate and Assistant Deans for Students in alignment with AAMC guidelines.

  • Planning and overseeing major student events, such as orientation, the White Coat Ceremony, Match Day, Class Day, and Commencement.

  • Managing the development, revision, and implementation of policies related to medical students and student affairs in accordance with institutional standards and applicable regulatory and accreditation requirements.

  • Meeting with students facing academic, professional, and conduct related concerns, and advising students with respect to their rights and responsibilities in the promotions and conduct processes.

  • Ensuring compliance with LCME accreditation standards related to student affairs and the learning environment and contributing to continuous quality improvement efforts to enhance the student experience.

  • Advancing initiatives that support medical student success, wellness, and readiness for residency.

  • Collaborating with faculty, staff, and institutional partners to ensure an integrated and holistic approach to medical student support.

Minimum Qualifications :

  • M.D., D.O., or Ph.D. from an accredited institution.

  • M.D. candidates must have completed ACGME-accredited residency.

  • ABMS board certification.

  • Tenure track candidates must be eligible for appointment as a tenured associate professor or professor of medicine upon hire. The selected candidate must have a demonstrated record of teaching, research, and service commensurate with a tenured faculty appointment at the rank of associate professor or professor of medicine in the College of Medicine.

Preferred Qualifications

  • M.D. or D.O. degree from an accredited university with completed ACGME-accredited residency.

  • Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to work with medical trainees.

  • Experience developing and evaluating academic support or career advising programs for medical students.

  • Knowledge of residency advising, match processes, and medical student success frameworks (AAMC Careers in Medicine, NRMP, AAMC resources).

  • Working knowledge of LCME accreditation standards related to student affairs.

  • Experience leading or supporting trainee conduct, professionalism, or promotion processes.

  • Active membership and engagement in national medical education organizations (e.g., AAMC and/or AAMC affinity groups related to medical trainees).

Additional Application Materials Required:

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following:

Job Posting Title: 

Post Doctoral Scholar

The Opportunity:

University of Central Florida (UCF) invites applications for one two-year Postdoctoral Research Scholar position at the HARP Lab (Human Factors, AI, Risk, and Privacy Lab). The candidate will work with Dr. Grace Fox and members of her interdisciplinary team at UCF and collaborate with academic partners within UCF and internationally. The candidate will work on several collaborative projects and funding proposals related to the research areas of focus at the HARP lab including cybersecurity, privacy, artificial intelligence, risk, trust, and human behavior. The successful candidate will collaborate with faculty, graduate students, and external partners.

Responsibilities:

Responsibilities include designing and conducting empirical behavioral research using mixed methods, qualitative and quantitative research designs including interviews, focus groups, surveys, and experiments, analyzing quantitative and qualitative data, publishing in leading conferences and journals across various disciplines, contributing to grant proposal development; mentoring graduate and undergraduate researchers.

The candidate will work with Dr. Fox and her team to manage project milestones, participate in team meetings, lead and contribute to the dissemination of findings across several projects in collaboration with graduate students, and faculty collaborators in UCF and internationally. The candidate must have excellent interpersonal, writing, and research skills, initiative, strong time management and organizational skills, and the ability to prioritize and meet deadlines and work independently and as a research team member. 

Minimum Qualifications: 

  •  A Ph.D. degree from an accredited educational institution in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Management Information Systems, Psychology, Human Factors, Human-Computer Interaction, Statistics Data Science, or a related discipline is required.
  • The candidate must have experience conducting and publishing research in one or more areas related to privacy and cybersecurity from a behavioral perspective.
  • Experience designing and leading quantitative human factors studies.
  • Record of publishing in well regarded journals/conferences within their field of study.
  • Strong experience in various advanced statistical methods (e.g., HLM, SEM, non-linear dynamical systems).
  • Experience working in multidisciplinary teams.

Preferred Qualifications: 

  • The candidates should have future research publication goals and plans.
  • Prior experience in designing and conducting research experiments is highly desired.
  • Experience working on funded projects and proposals.
  • Strong Programming skills (e.g., R, Python, MATLAB) are a plus.
